included.head: 000a480f917b32c09a8e80a31bd223e254841592
included.title: fix(io): read a placed layer's custom warp over its source rect (#8227)
included.body:
## Fixes

Fixes #8227

## Problem

A PSD smart object with a `warpCustom` warp whose `warp.bounds` sit off the contents' own `0..Sz` rect (the reporter's file: bounds -425, -675 to 2425, 2175 over a 2850 × 2850 source) re-rendered shifted. Edit Contents or Replace Contents moved the contents 15 % / 24 % into the frame and cut off their right and bottom edges. `Warp::map` evaluates the mesh at `(x - bounds.left) / w`, and the import took `bounds` from the file as is. Photoshop draws the mesh over the source rect; `bounds` only frames the control points.

## Solution

- **Import** (`blocks::parse_placed_warp`): a `SoLd` / `SoLE` custom warp spans the source rect `0..Sz` (`over_source`). This runs after the existing "moves nothing" check, so identity meshes over offset bounds still read as no warp, as before. Preset styles keep their box, since they are built from it.
- **Export** (`smart_map::sold_bytes`): a custom warp made in PhotoCraft can still be stored over another box (the warp box's image in source space, or the hull frame from #4113). It is re-expressed over the source rect with the new `Warp::over_box`, so it reopens drawing the same. `over_box` is exact: each new patch is a piece of one old patch, or of its clamped edge where the box runs past the old one. `Trnf` is computed from the stored warp as before, so the placement round-trips.
- **Export keeps the file's warp:** an imported `warp` / `quiltWarp` block that still reads as the layer's warp is written back verbatim, with its own `bounds`.

`PlLd` records (CS2 and older) store no source size and are left as they were. In-app editing and `.pcraft` keep the warp's own box; only the PSD mapping changes.

## Tests

- `blocks::tests::offset_custom_warp_bounds_still_span_the_source`: the reporter's numbers (Sz 2850 × 2850, bounds -425, -675 to 2425, 2175, a bent mesh). The source corners land on the mesh's corner points.
- `smart_map::tests::custom_warp_bounds_off_the_source_round_trip`: a warp made here over a box past the source is written over the source rect, reads back drawing the same, and keeps its placement. An imported block with offset `bounds` reads the same and is written back unchanged.
- `geom::warp::tests::over_box_keeps_the_surface`: a box inside the old one, a box past it, a box across a patch boundary, and the same box. Also checks that presets and empty or non-finite boxes are unchanged.

All three fail without the fix.

Also run:
- `cargo test -p photocraft-io --lib` (237 passed)
- `--test smart_contents_identity`
- `cargo test -p photocraft-geom --lib`
- the engine's smart and warp lib tests
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-geom -p photocraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --check`


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Custom mesh warps can now be fitted to different source rectangles while preserving interior boundaries and placement.
  * Placed layers correctly account for their source dimensions when applying custom warps.
  * Template updates preserve equivalent warp representations and geometry when source bounds differ.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of empty, invalid, missing, or non-finite source dimensions without altering existing warp behavior.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

included.head: ee19856487ba51effc9396354964184d67dd7354
included.title: Layers panel: a click on the empty space below the layers deselects them (#8100)
included.body:
Fixes #8100

### Problem
In Photoshop, a click on the empty part of the Layers panel, below the last layer, deselects every layer (Select › Deselect Layers). In PhotoCraft that click did nothing, so the only way to have no layer selected was the menu item.

The canvas-side behaviour (a Move/Auto-Select click on the pasteboard or an empty spot) is in the open PRs #5912 and #5009. This PR is the Layers panel part.

### Solution
`crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs`, Layers panel list:
- **The click:** the empty space below the bottom-most row, already a drop zone for layer drags (#1721), now takes a plain click. When layers are selected, the click runs `select.deselectLayers`: one history step, recorded like the menu item.
- **Drags:** a drag dropped there still moves the layers below the last row, as before. Only a click deselects.

### Tests
`layer_shortcut_tests::a_click_below_the_layers_deselects_them`, in the running app:
- with "Top" selected, a click 40 points below the last row leaves no layer selected and no active layer;
- a click on the row selects it again.

It fails without the change: the layer stays selected.

```
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- layer_shortcut_tests panels::
cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                         # clean
```

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Clicking empty space below the last row in the Layers panel now deselects all layers and clears the active layer.
  - Clicking an existing layer row continues to select that layer.

included.head: 3d7d62e349447a2078df23fdc7e5d42f1960e4ea
included.title: PSD layer comps: an entry without enab inherits the previous visibility, as in Photoshop (#8093)
included.body:
Fixes #8093

### Problem
Photoshop stores a layer's state per layer comp in `cmls.layerSettings`, and writes `enab` (visibility) only where it **changes** from one comp to the next. An entry without `enab` has the last `enab` before it, or is visible when none came before.

PhotoCraft read a missing `enab` as "this comp leaves the layer as it is". So on a fresh open, Layer Comps › Apply could show layers Photoshop hides, or hide layers it shows. The reporter's two files:

| File | Comp | Photoshop | PhotoCraft before |
|---|---|---|---|
| repro_comp_new_layer.psd (C: `[c1 {}], [0 {enab false}]`) | c1 | C visible | C hidden |
| repro_comp_inherit.psd (A: `[c1 {}], [c2 {enab false}], [c3 {}], [0 {}]`) | c3 | A hidden | A visible |

In real character PSDs with ~10 comps, the result was whole groups on or off, and composites up to 211 levels off.

### Solution
`crates/io/src/comps_map.rs`, `decode_comps`, for each layer's `layerSettings`:
- **Order:** the entries are walked in order, keeping the last `enab` seen.
- **Real comps:** an entry for a real comp gets its own `enab` or the inherited one, starting from visible. So every comp the layer has an entry for now records a visibility, and `layerComp.apply` (which honours each comp's Visibility option) shows what Photoshop shows.
- **Last Document State:** the entry for comp 0 keeps exactly what it records, as before. Our own writer emits that entry without `enab` when a document has no Last Document State, and inheriting there would invent one on the next open.

Positions are read as before. A comp whose Visibility option is off still doesn't apply visibility.

`crates/io/tests/comps_artboards.rs`: the synthetic round trip has a comp that records nothing for one layer. A PSD can't say "leaves it alone": that entry has no `enab`, which Photoshop reads as the previous comp's visibility, and so does the import now. The test's expectation says so.

### Tests
`comps_map::tests::a_comp_entry_without_enab_inherits_the_previous_visibility` builds both of the reporter's layers' `cmls` with the same entries:
- A is visible in c1, hidden in c2, and hidden in c3 (inherited);
- C is visible in c1 (no `enab` before it);
- the Last Document State keeps C hidden and records nothing for A.

It fails without the change: those comps had no visibility, so applying them left the layers as they were.

```
cargo test -p photocraft-io --lib                         # 225 passed
cargo test -p photocraft-io --test comps_artboards
cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test duplicate_layer_comps
cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib -- comp
cargo clippy -p photocraft-io --lib --tests -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                    # clean
```


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Corrected layer visibility handling when composition entries omit visibility information.
  - Preserved explicit visibility settings for the Last Document State and compositions that do not capture visibility.
  - Improved PSD round-trip behavior so inherited visibility matches Photoshop’s handling.
  - Kept position-only composition behavior and out-of-range warnings unchanged.

- **Tests**
  - Added coverage for visibility inheritance across compositions, newly added layers, position-only entries, and Last Document State entries.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

included.title: i18n(pt-br): translate 131 runtime labels that still showed in English
included.body:
Adds 131 Brazilian Portuguese strings (I'm a native speaker). They are labels the UI translates at runtime through `tl!(…)` or `fmt(tl!(template), …)`, which `i18n-coverage` can't list, so in pt-BR they still showed in English. Other catalogs already had them.

| Area | Examples |
|---|---|
| Channels panel menu | Novo canal…, Mesclar canal de cor especial, Converter em canal alfa, Sair da máscara rápida, A cor indica áreas mascaradas |
| Layer Style › Blending Options | Mesclagem geral, Raso / Profundo, A máscara de camada oculta os efeitos, Esta camada:, Camada subjacente: |
| Canvas right-click menus | Cinza-escuro, Criar demarcador de trabalho…, Transformação livre do demarcador, Copiar traçado completo |
| Color Picker titles | Seletor de cores (Cor de primeiro plano) |
| Rasterize prompts | Esta camada de texto precisa ser rasterizada antes de continuar. … |
| GPU and monitor status | Adaptador gráfico: {adapter}, Perfil do monitor em uso: {profile} |
| Status messages | Preferências salvas, Falha ao reproduzir a ação: {error}, {shortcut} atribuído. |
| Liquify tool tooltips | Deformação para frente, Torcer no sentido horário, Franzir, Inflar |

Terms follow the catalog's own wording: demarcador for path, canal de cor especial for spot channel, Mesclar for Merge, Traçado for stroke, Seletor de cores, Configurações de cores.

Each source string was checked in the code: it is passed through `tl!` (directly, through a template, or by the helper that draws it, such as `item()` in the Channels panel or `tl!(tool.label())` in Liquify). I left out strings that are only used as untranslated accessibility labels (Commit transform, Cancel transform) and Liquify labels that aren't drawn from `label()` (Freeze Lasso, Reconstruct All, Mask None).

Only `pt-br.tsv` changes (131 rows in labelled sections at the end). Every row has three columns, `{placeholders}` match the source, there are no duplicate keys, and `cargo xtask i18n-coverage` still reports pt-br at 1909/1909. No proprietary resources were used.

included.head: 168701779cdd471b655a0b4376ce2c52ca2f6999
included.title: CodeRabbit follow-ups for the #8095 batch
included.body:
TL;DR: three small fixes CodeRabbit found in PRs from the #8095 batch. A typo in `baseline` no longer clears superscript, an Indexed/Bitmap save warns whenever flattening loses a layer, and ABR import no longer keeps a second copy of a file of up to 1 GiB.

#8095 merged the batch at `bc5e4d4c8`. This fix-up was pushed to #8084 after that, so it is not on main yet. This PR is only that commit, on top of main at `b097800e7`.

## Changes

- **#5807, `type_cmds.rs`:** an unknown `baseline` value (e.g. `"superscipt"`) reset superscript or subscript to Normal. It is now a BadParams error in `type.setStyle`, `type.edit` and `type.create`, and `apply_char_props` leaves the style unchanged for it. `null` is still ignored.
- **#4816, `palette_map.rs`:** Indexed and Bitmap have no layers in Photoshop, so the save stays a flat file, as Multichannel already does. Until now the save only warned for two or more layers. It now warns whenever flattening loses something: more than one layer, or a single layer that is hidden, masked, clipped, below full opacity, not Normal, has effects, or is not a pixel layer.
- **#7180, `preset_import_cmds.rs`:** the apply closure cloned all params, including a base64 `data` string of up to ~1.3 GiB. It now gets only `replace` and `select`.

## Testing

- New tests: `unknown_baseline_is_rejected_and_keeps_the_style` and `indexed_save_warns_whenever_flattening_loses_a_layer`. Both fail without the fix. The existing `select: true` ABR test covers the apply params.
- Locally (Windows): fmt, clippy `-D warnings` on engine and io, `photocraft-io` and `photocraft-engine` lib and integration tests, `panic_hunt --ignored`, and a wasm check of both crates all pass.

  * Improved text styling validation for baseline settings. Invalid values are rejected, while existing styles remain unchanged.

  * Lossless export is correctly recognized for documents with no layers or a single compatible visible raster layer.

included.head: a0e538ccdd225cd264efe1a87e3cb22e571f5275
included.title: Transform: remember selected interpolation (#8067)
included.body:
Fixes #8067

## Problem
Transform sessions used hard-coded interpolation defaults, so choosing Nearest Neighbor only affected the current transform. The next transform opened with Bicubic (or Bilinear for selection transforms).

## Change
All transform entry points now read the existing General › Image Interpolation preference. Changing the options-bar interpolation updates that preference, so later transforms reuse the selected mode. The shared preference also supplies Image Size's default. A UI regression test selects Nearest Neighbor, commits a transform, opens another, and checks that the selection remains.

## Validation
- The regression test failed before the fix (`bicubic` instead of `nearest`) and passes with the fix.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -j 12 -p photocraft-ui-egui -- --test-threads=8` — 3,147 unit tests passed, 13 ignored; all integration tests passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 12 -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo check -j 12 -p photocraft-ui-egui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` — passed with three existing engine dead-code warnings.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Transform tools now use the configured image-interpolation preference when starting a session.
  - Selected interpolation settings are preserved for subsequent transform sessions.
  - Changing interpolation options updates the General image-interpolation preference.
  - Nearest, Bilinear, and Bicubic interpolation choices continue to be supported consistently across transform workflows.

included.head: 480c12304d5cacdfd8f7af210afad5d5905e7619
included.title: Pencil: align 1 px click snapping with the line walker (#4895)
included.body:
Fixes #4895

`grid_center` used `floor` for odd-sized tips while the line walker treats values within `1e-7` of a pixel boundary as exactly on it. A 1 px Pencil Shift-click just below a grid corner could therefore snap to one cell on pointer-down and rasterize into its neighbor on release.

Reuse the line walker's grid-cell rule for odd-sized tip snapping. This keeps the click endpoint, cursor, and rasterized line on the same pixel. Add unit and UI regression coverage, including the TL/TR/BL/BR/center subpixel matrix.

Related report: #8040.

CMYK JPEG exports included a JFIF APP0 marker alongside a four-component frame and Adobe APP14. Windows Photos rejected the resulting file, matching the CMYK/JFIF issue confirmed in VectorCraft #3084.

included.head: 5579cf5439856fed93f41a669a3fc9b56d5813cf
included.title: Compose: Extend Softer outer glows past Size (#7899)
included.body:
## Problem

#7899 reports that a Softer Outer Glow falls to zero at `Size`, while Photoshop keeps a short fading tail. The current two-box tent has finite support, which causes the hard cutoff.

## Change

- Preserve the existing tent profile and add a short, range-scaled tail only to Softer outer glows.
- Derive the tail from the shape's Euclidean outside-distance field, max-combine it with the existing blur, and include its support in CPU effect margins.
- Use the same tail stage in the GPU compositor. Inner glows and Precise glows are unchanged.

Reference comparison from the issue: [Photoshop vs PhotoCraft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96cdaebe-4752-47af-b51e-de41d8adea8f).

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — passed.
- `cargo test -j12 -p photocraft-compose --lib softer_outer_glow` — 2 passed.
- `cargo test -j12 -p photocraft-gpu --lib softer_outer_glow` — 1 passed.

- `cargo clippy -j12 -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed.

- `cargo test --release -j12 -p photocraft-io --features corpus,heif --test corpus psd_tools_import_flatten_oracle -- --nocapture` — passed; `layer_effects.psd` matched with no bad pixels.

included.head: ec9b6b7ee55927f7180a2dac37227f40449f22e0
included.title: CLI: reject ignored or conflicting mcp/serve launch options
included.body:
Closes #8037.

`photocraft-cli mcp` and `serve` silently accepted launch options they then ignored. `mcp stray.psd` went straight into MCP initialization. A repeated option quietly kept its last value. `--control-token-file` without `--bridge`/`--port` did nothing. In bridge mode, `--automation-read-root`/`--automation-write-root` were dropped even though the desktop process holds the roots, so the flags suggested file access that was never granted.

## Change (`apps/photocraft-cli/src/lib.rs`)

- New `validate_server_args`, run after parsing and before any server starts. For `mcp` and `serve` it refuses:
  - positional arguments;
  - an option given twice (`--flag v` or `--flag=v`);
  - empty values;
  - `--control-token` together with `--control-token-file`;
  - explicit token flags without `--bridge` (mcp) or `--port` (serve);
  - root flags on `mcp --bridge`, with an error saying to set them on the desktop app.
- Every subcommand: a flag where a value should be (`--format --quality 80`) is now "needs a value" instead of becoming the value. `--help`/`-h` in that position still prints usage. `--flag=--value` still passes a value that starts with `--`.
- These are usage errors: exit 2, message on stderr, stdout left empty for the protocol.
- Token environment variables (`PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN`, `PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN_FILE`) are still ignored in headless/stdio mode on purpose, so one left in a shell profile doesn't break headless use.

No documented launch line changes meaning. I checked every `mcp`/`serve` example in `docs/`, `book/` and the README.

## Docs

- `photocraft-cli --help`, `docs/mcp.md`, `book/src/automation/cli.md` and `book/src/automation/mcp.md` describe the rules and recommend absolute root paths in MCP client configs.

## Tests (`apps/photocraft-cli/tests/cli.rs`)

- `server_modes_reject_ignored_or_conflicting_options`: each refusal above for both `mcp` and `serve`, checking exit 2, the message and an empty stdout.
- `server_validation_does_not_consume_stdio_or_create_files`: four launch lines (stray positional, repeated root, repeated `--port`, repeated `--control-token-file`). Before this change each would have started a TCP server and written the token file. With stdin held open, each now exits 2 and creates no token file.
- `every_subcommand_answers_help` and `unknown_flags_are_usage_errors`: help in a value position, a missing value in `batch`, and the `--flag=--value` form.

- [x] `cargo test -p photocraft-cli`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p photocraft-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`

No engine commands, protocol tools, document fields or L0–L6 code changed.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

included.head: b85b638e773b28feb9d0e06072575236e2b81afc
included.title: Keep '#' inside quoted .cube TITLE when parsing
included.body:
Found while testing `crates/cms/src/lutfile.rs:111 (parse_cube) and :227 (write_cube)` (no existing issue): .cube LUT title containing '#' is truncated when the file is read back.

## Cause
`parse_cube` strips comments with `line.split('#').next()` on every line, including the `TITLE "..."` line. A title such as `Look #3` is therefore cut at the `#`, and the closing quote is lost.

## Fix
On a `TITLE` line with a quoted string, comment stripping now starts after the closing quote, so a `#` inside the quotes is kept as part of the title. A trailing `# note` after the closing quote is still treated as a comment.

## Verified
- Regression test `lutfile::tests::cube_title_with_hash_round_trips`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p photocraft-cms --lib cube_title_with_hash_round_trips`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`write_cube` is unchanged because it already writes the title in double quotes. Comment handling on other lines, and on `TITLE` lines without a closing quote, is unchanged.

included.head: acc3420c6d5e88255790778f6e744c6cb9455fca
included.title: Keep previous crop length when normalizing rounds to zero
included.body:
Found while testing `crates/ui-egui/src/crop_size.rs:86-107 (format_length / normalize_length)` (no existing issue): Crop size length field normalizes a tiny positive value to the invalid "0 px".

## Cause
`normalize_length` accepts any positive finite number, but `format_length` rounds to a limited number of decimals. A tiny value such as `0.001` therefore becomes `0 px`, which `parse_length` rejects.

## Fix
`normalize_length` now parses the formatted string again. If `parse_length` rejects it, the function returns the previous value.

included.head: 24970b162288e10dd0fd66ad210f53c664d1b5a4
included.title: Open: a file without type never waits for the font scan (#7332)
included.body:
Part of #7332.

## What the logs show

The reporter attached two debug logs (0.10.0, MSI build, Windows 11, RTX 4060 laptop). Both have a single silent gap of about 8 to 9 minutes on the main thread, starting right after launch. The first line after each gap is wgpu/naga building the canvas shaders for the newly opened document, and the whole naga burst takes well under a second. So naga is not what stalls. It is just the first thing that logs once the stall is over.

In both logs the stall ends about 7.5 to 9 minutes after launch, however long the user waited before opening. That matches the installed-font scan that `type_tool::warm_fonts` starts on a background thread at launch:

- The background open's worker decodes the file and finishes in a few milliseconds.
- `jobs_ui::after_open` then calls `file_open::with_missing_fonts` on the UI thread, which calls `type_extra_cmds::missing_fonts`.
- `missing_fonts` locked `photocraft_text::shared()` before it looked at the layers. The first `shared()` call blocks until the font scan finishes. That happened even for a JPG with no type layers.
- The open card had last painted 2% (or 95%), so the window sat there "Not responding" until the scan finished. Later opens are fast because the scan is done by then, and it starts over on the next launch. That is exactly what was reported.

PSDs with type also stall at 95% but stay responsive, because `io::text_import` waits on `shared()` on the worker.

## Change

- `type_extra_cmds::missing_fonts` returns at once for a document without type layers and never touches the shared text engine. This fixes the reported case: any JPG/PNG/etc. on the first open after launch.
- New `type_extra_cmds::has_type_layers`. When the opened document has type layers, `Session::start_open`'s worker waits for the shared engine itself (progress reads "Loading fonts"). The UI-thread missing-font check that follows then finds the engine ready and no longer freezes the window.
- Regression test `a_document_without_type_never_waits_for_the_text_engine`: it holds the shared engine locked and checks that `missing_font_warnings` still answers for a document without type. Before this change it blocked on the lock.

## Not addressed here

Why the font scan takes about 8 minutes on this machine is still unknown. The logs don't cover it: `FontDb::load_system_fonts` logs nothing, and it may come down to a very large font folder or slow per-file mapping on Windows. Until that is found, Type tool font menus show "Loading fonts…" for that long, and a document with type waits on its worker. The window stays responsive in both cases. A follow-up should time the scan and log the file count.

Tests were not run locally; CI will verify.

included.head: 960d927a37e3db23615830537e67fe732df0c5d1
included.title: Windows on ARM: auto picks DirectX 12 for Qualcomm graphics (#7537)
included.body:
Part of #7537.

**What the issue showed.** On Windows 11 ARM64 with 0.10.0, editing Layer Style › Inner Shadow and then drawing made PhotoCraft exit with no error window. The log shows the Vulkan driver losing the device ("driver implementation is at fault"), egui-wgpu panicking while it drew the window on the lost device, and then a second panic in wgpu-hal's Vulkan swapchain. The reporter then set Preferences › Performance › GPU Backend to **DirectX 12** and [could not reproduce it any more](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/7537#issuecomment-6263392879).

**Change.** On Windows, `auto` already ranks a DX12 adapter before Vulkan for Intel, whose Vulkan driver is known to crash. This PR applies the same rule to Qualcomm, the GPU in Windows on ARM PCs, so these machines start on DX12 without anyone changing a setting:

- `dx12_first_on_windows(vendor)` lists the makers that get DX12 first: Intel (`0x8086`) and Qualcomm. Qualcomm has two ids: `0x5143` from its Vulkan driver and `0x4D4F4351` ("QCOM") from DXGI. Both are matched, so the DX12 adapter wins.
- `intel_dx12_applied` becomes `dx12_default_applied`. It returns the maker's name, so the System Info note says "Qualcomm graphics on Windows: using DirectX 12 …" or "Intel graphics …".
- An explicit backend preference, `WGPU_BACKEND` and `--safe-gpu` are unchanged. Nothing changes off Windows.
- `docs/development.md` now mentions Qualcomm next to the Intel default.

**Not in this PR.** The window still can't survive a lost device on any backend. Open PR #6464 handles that by saving documents for recovery and closing cleanly. Issue #7537 stays open for it.

**Caveat.** The log doesn't name the adapter. The Qualcomm part comes from the platform: Windows on ARM devices ship Adreno GPUs. I have no ARM64 device, so this hasn't been run on one.

**Tests.** New unit test `qualcomm_on_windows_defaults_to_dx12` in `apps/photocraft/src/gpu_startup.rs`, and the Intel test now uses the renamed helper. Tests were **not run locally** and nothing was built; CI will verify.

included.head: 67a9c53f26d4365620a600180cabd7b6e229b859
included.title: perf(raster): tile content bounds compare rows in blocks (P32, #211)
included.body:
Part of #211 (P32, brush release on a long stroke).

P32 ("brush release: 600-point stroke, 200 px soft, 24 MP") went from 0.31–0.36 ms to 7.5–8.1 ms p50 (p95 up to 22 ms, over its 16 ms budget) between 2d2e4993 (10-14) and main 46e538b3, reproduced on Linux (fork A/B, ubuntu-latest, 3 interleaved rounds). The canvas refresh in that row is of an empty rect, so the time is in the engine: an engine-only copy of the row puts it in the `paint.stroke` commit (0.17 → 3.93 ms min), not in offering the live stroke.

Bisecting that bench on the fork (first-parent, 2d2e4993..46e538b3) lands on 286ff735 (#3847): the commit takes 0.13 ms min at its parent 3e428e73 and 2.97 ms at 286ff735. Since then, `Session::edit` reports `step_damage(before, after)` for every edit. For the released stroke that asks for the painted layer's content bounds, which scans every tile the stroke touched (each is new, so the per-tile cache in `compose::bounds` misses). `Tile::content_bounds` compared each row pixel by pixel against the default pixel, so the mostly untouched rows of a soft stroke's tiles cost a slice compare per pixel.

## What

`Tile::content_bounds` compares each row against one row of the default pixel in 64-byte blocks: an untouched row is a few block compares, and a row with content is narrowed to the first and last differing byte inside the first and last differing block. A pixel differs exactly when one of its bytes does, so those bytes' pixels are the first and last differing pixels and the bounds are the same. Every caller (`Surface::content_bounds`, the cached `compose::bounds::content_bounds` the GPU planner and the CPU compositor use, `step_damage`) gets the same result, faster.

## Measured

A/B on the fork (ubuntu-latest, 4 cores): main 46e538b3 vs this branch, the same engine-only copy of P32's row built at each commit (one target dir each, binaries checked to differ), interleaved, 5 rounds × 7 releases on the 6000×4000 document.

| | main | this branch | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `paint.stroke` commit, p50 | 4.43–5.20 ms | 1.31–1.62 ms | −70 % |
| `paint.stroke` commit, min | 2.66–3.14 ms | 1.02–1.28 ms | −61 % |
| Offering the live stroke, p50 | 0.15–0.16 ms | 0.14–0.17 ms | unchanged |

Same result: an FNV fingerprint over every commit's JSON reply (its damage rect included) is identical on both sides in every round. `cargo test -p photocraft-raster --lib`: 30 passed.

This does not bring the commit back to the 0.17 ms it took at 2d2e4993; I haven't broken down the remaining 1 ms, and this PR leaves `step_damage` itself as it is.

## Tests

`tile_content_bounds_match_a_per_pixel_scan`: one differing byte at every byte position of a pixel, at and around the 64-byte block boundaries and the row ends, in pixel sizes 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 16 bytes, checked against a per-pixel scan; plus a pixel differing in every byte. The existing `tile_content_bounds_scans_against_the_given_pixel` and `content_bounds_and_prune` still apply.

  * Boundary calculations now remain consistent across different pixel sizes, byte positions, block boundaries, and fully differing pixels.
* **Reliability**
  * Added comprehensive coverage for varied raster comparison scenarios, helping ensure accurate content bounds.

included.head: afeea2f643f015d8010b5b67b06ccb46cd5f55c1
included.title: Decode numeric character references in File Info XMP text
included.body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs:690 (xml_unescape), used by li_values, find_attr and read_file_info` (no existing issue): File Info does not decode numeric character references in XMP text, so it shows `
` and `©` literally.

## Cause
File Info did not decode numeric character references in XMP text, so it showed `
` and `©` literally. `xml_unescape` only handled the five named XML entities, so the raw references stayed in Description, Title and the other fields. Saving an edited field then ran `xml_escape` over them, which turned `
` into `&#xA;` and corrupted the stored text.

## Fix
`xml_unescape` now makes a single pass and decodes decimal and hex numeric character references along with the five named entities. A single pass means `&#38;` decodes to `&` and not `&`. Malformed or unknown references are left as they are.

## Verified
- Regression test `numeric_character_references_are_decoded`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test xmp_charref`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`xml_escape` and the write path are unchanged. The decoding fix is enough because the read side no longer returns raw references to be re-escaped.

included.head: 6d2c6cc0174c05ee19d00f28f645f81814f62a2c
included.title: fix(atn): a Group Layers step keeps its explicit layer through .atn (#7236)
included.body:
## Summary

Fixes #7236. A recorded `layer.groupLayers` step with an explicit layer now exports its target the way every other layer reference in this file does, and the import restores it; the implicit form (group the current selection) survives unchanged.

The issue's reproduction: a recorded step `["layer.groupLayers", {"layer": "A", "name": "Group"}]` groups A when replayed directly, but after a strict `.atn` round trip the exported descriptor had `From: target_ref("Lyr ")` — the target layer, not A — and the re-imported step was `{"name": "Group"}`, so playback grouped the selection (B and C) instead.

## The change

- `make_to`: `layer.groupLayers` exports `From` through the existing `layer_ref` helper — a `layer` param becomes a named `Lyr ` reference, its absence keeps the previous `target_ref("Lyr ")` form byte for byte (crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs:1153).
- `make_from`: the `layerSection` branch reads the `From` reference it already checked for and restores `{"layer": name}` through the existing `layer_target` helper; no `From` still imports as `layer.new.group` (crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs:1124).

Both helpers are the same ones the rest of the file uses, so the descriptor holds the standard named-reference form our `.atn` bytes already carry for other layer commands; import needed no new code paths.

## Boundary

Photoshop-authored `From` references we cannot restore (a zero-based index) keep the old implicit import — the group lands on the current selection at playback, exactly as before this change; the exporter never writes those forms. The target-reference form (`Trgt`) also stays implicit, which is what the issue's passing control needs.

## Tests

`cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib atn_cmds` — 25 passed, 0 failed (`crates/engine/src/atn_cmds/tests.rs`):

- `group_layers_keeps_its_explicit_target_through_atn`: the explicit form round trips as `{"layer": "A", "name": "Group"}`; the implicit `{"name": "Group"}` and `{}` forms round trip unchanged; `layer.new.group` stays a plain new group.
- `group_layers_from_index_reference_stays_implicit`: an index `From` imports as the implicit group once more, not an invented target.

Also ran: `cargo fmt --check -p photocraft-engine`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask wasm` (all crates pass) on head 6d2c6cc0. My sandbox's Windows print-spooler tests make the full local lib suite crawl, so its breadth rests on the hosted checks for this head.

## Not verified

- No Photoshop-authored `.atn` fixture with a `make`/`layerSection` step and a named `From` was examined; the named-reference export form is the same one this file already emits for other layer commands, but a Photoshop-made action file could differ in details (e.g. an extra/absent field) that our import has not seen before.
- Playback semantics beyond the round-tripped params (that replay groups exactly A in a real session through the Actions panel) are not covered by a UI-driven test here.

included.title: Actions: Emboss saves to and loads from .atn as Photoshop's Embs step (#7946)
included.body:
Fixes #7946

### Problem
Filter › Stylize › Emboss (`filter.stylize.emboss`) records and plays in PhotoCraft's own Actions, but the `.atn` writer had no Photoshop event for it:
- `actions.save` refused the action ("has no Photoshop equivalent");
- with `skipUnsupported` it left the step out, so the saved action silently lost the relief.

Photoshop has the filter, so the step has a Photoshop form.

### Solution
`crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs`: Emboss joins the mapped events as Photoshop records it:
- the event is `Embs`;
- `Angl` ↔ `angle`, `Hght` ↔ `height` and `Amnt` ↔ `amount`, all plain integers (Photoshop's Emboss dialog takes whole degrees, pixels and percent).

The same table entry works both ways: saving writes `Embs`, and loading a Photoshop action with an Emboss step gives `filter.stylize.emboss` back. Like the other pixel filters, a step recorded against a layer mask is still not exported as a pixel filter.

### Tests
`atn_cmds::tests::emboss_saves_as_photoshops_event_and_loads_back`:
- an action with `filter.stylize.emboss {angle: 130, height: 1, amount: 70}` (the reporter's step) saves with nothing skipped;
- the file holds an `Embs` event with `Angl` 130, `Hght` 1 and `Amnt` 70 as integers;
- loading it gives the same step and params.

It fails without the change: the save errors with "no Photoshop equivalent".

```
cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib -- atn_cmds
cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                        # clean
```

- **New notes:** a click off the notes adds one with what the bar shows, so it follows the last note picked, as in Photoshop. Typing another author or picking another colour still changes it.

- with two notes ("Ann" pink and "Bob" blue) and the bar set to "Me" yellow, clicking each note shows its own author and colour;

included.head: 3af447a315e2ddc6363ebfeb62252748903f5b39
included.title: Type: hovering a served font fetches it after a short rest, not as the pointer passes
included.body:
## Problem

With served fonts (`fonts/manifest.txt`, #1875), hovering a row in the font menu previews that family on the canvas, and for a family that isn't fetched yet the preview asks the host for the whole family (`type_font_preview::set` → `served::request`). Since #5222 that preview reaches the canvas from the options bar too, so moving the pointer down the menu downloads every family it passes over.

Measured in Chrome on a web build of main `03d0c7e3` serving 1,700 Google Fonts families: moving the pointer over 10 rows, 60 ms on each, fetched 15 font files from 10 families, 3.5 MB, in under a second. We embed the web build in a sandboxed iframe (opaque origin), so nothing is cached between sessions and this repeats every time.

## Change

- A family that isn't installed previews (and so is fetched) once the pointer has rested on its row for 0.25 s (`HOVER_FETCH_DELAY`). Moving to another row starts the wait again; while waiting, `request_repaint_after` brings the frame that previews it.
- Installed fonts (bundled, system, or served and already fetched) preview at once, as before. Picking a font (a click, or the arrow keys) still fetches it at once.
- Tests in `type_font_preview.rs`: passing over rows asks for nothing and a rest previews the family (`a_served_family_is_asked_for_only_once_the_pointer_rests_on_its_row`); an installed family previews on the first frame.

A note on large catalogs: at ~1,700 families, laying out every row each frame the menu is open is noticeable too. #884 lays the rows out with `ScrollArea::show_rows`, and #7821 wraps them in a `ScrollArea`, where `show_rows` would cover it. This PR leaves the rows alone, so it doesn't conflict with either.

## Measurements and screenshot

Web builds of main `03d0c7e3` without and with this change, Chrome (WebGPU, macOS), page served with CSP `sandbox allow-scripts allow-downloads` and the same 1,700-family `fonts/manifest.txt`. Pointer over the first 10 rows (ABeeZee … Adamina), 60 ms each, then 1.2 s on Abril Fatface:

| | main | + this change |
|---|---|---|
| Moving over 10 rows | 15 font files from 10 families, 3.5 MB | nothing |
| Resting on Abril Fatface | nothing new (fetched while moving) | 1 file, previewed on the canvas |

With this change, after the rest:

![Abril Fatface previewed after a rest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kuvshin888/photocraft/pr-screenshots/font-hover-after.png)

## Checks

- Linux, Rust 1.99.0, main `03d0c7e3` + this commit: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --locked --lib -- type_font_preview font_picker_tests` (24 passed), `cargo xtask wasm`.
- The measurements above, in Chrome.

  * Installed fonts continue to preview immediately.

included.title: Layers: the pointer over a thumbnail shows what ⌘-click loads, with the +/−/× badge (#7824)
included.body:
Fixes #7824

### Problem
⌘/Ctrl-click on a layer, mask or vector-mask thumbnail in the Layers panel loads it as a selection, and ⇧, ⌥ and ⇧⌥ make that add, subtract or intersect. Hovering the thumbnail with those keys held left the plain arrow, so nothing said what the click would do. Photoshop changes the pointer over the thumbnail and adds the selection mode's +, − or × badge.

### Solution
`crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs`, Layers panel row:
- **One test for "would load":** the ⌘-click check (which thumbnail, and not the Background, which has no transparency) is now one closure, `load_at`. Both the click and the hover use it, so the cursor shows exactly where a click loads.
- **Cursor:** over such a thumbnail with ⌘ held, the pointer is a pointing hand.
- **Badge:** with ⇧, ⌥ or ⇧⌥ also held, the hand gets the badge the selection tools already draw for add, subtract and intersect (`tool_feedback::draw_badge`). ⌘ alone (a new selection) has no badge, as for the selection tools. The mode comes from `channels_panel::load_operation`, the same as the click.

The click itself is unchanged.

### Tests
`layer_shortcut_tests::command_over_a_thumbnail_shows_the_load_cursor`:
- the badge for ⌘, ⌘⇧, ⌘⌥ and ⌘⇧⌥ is none, add, subtract and intersect;
- in the running app (kittest), hovering a layer's thumbnail with ⌘, ⌘⇧ or ⌘⌥ shows the pointing hand;
- without ⌘, or over the Background's thumbnail, it doesn't.

It fails without the change: the pointer over the thumbnail stays the arrow.

```
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- thumbnail load_cursor
cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -- -D warnings   # clean
```

included.title: Fixed Size marquee: Width and Height in any length unit (#7910)
included.body:
Fixes #7910

### Problem
With the Rectangular or Elliptical Marquee set to Style › Fixed Size, Width and Height were pixel fields only. To select, say, 50 × 30 mm, you had to work out the pixels at the document's resolution yourself. In Photoshop, a right-click on these fields picks their unit (px, in, cm, mm, pt, pica, %).

### Solution
`crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs` (marquee options bar):
- **Unit menu:** with Fixed Size, a right-click on Width or Height opens the length-units menu that the rulers and Free Transform's W and H already use (`rulers::unit_menu`), with the current unit checked.
- **Display:** both fields show the size in the picked unit, converted at the active document's resolution (72 ppi without a document). Percent is of the document's width or height.
- **Typing:** a number typed is in that unit; a typed unit ("2 in") converts as before.
- **Exact pixels:** leaving a field re-reads the rounded text it showed; when that is all that happened, the pixels are kept, so a unit that rounds doesn't nudge the size.
- **Storage:** the size is still kept in pixels (`marquee_width`/`marquee_height`), so the marquee drag and saved tool options are unchanged.

`crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs`: the picked unit is a new tool option, `marquee_unit` (default `pixels`, `serde(default)` so older settings load), and Reset Tool resets it (`tool_reset.rs`).

Fixed Ratio's fields stay plain numbers.

### Tests
`fixed_size_shows_and_takes_the_unit_picked_on_its_fields`, driving the options bar in a kittest harness (a 254 ppi document, so 10 px = 1 mm):
- Fixed Size 100 × 50 px shows 100 and 50;
- right-click on Width › Millimeters shows 10 and 5, and the stored size is still 100 × 50 px;
- typing 20 into Width then gives 200 px;
- in Inches, entering and leaving Height (50 px, shown as 0.197 in) without an edit keeps 50 px, not the 50.038 px the rounded text reads back as.

It fails without the change: the right-click opens no unit menu.

included.head: d51202c5a459565afe4e3b7d563c09241c5cd19a
included.title: Smart Blur: 3.5× faster at radius 12 with identical output (#7921)
included.body:
Closes #7921.

Smart Blur read each neighbour one channel at a time through bounds-checked `Image::get`. On High quality that is 441 neighbours per pixel at radius 12, which took 6.25 s on 24 MP.

## Change (`crates/algo/src/blur2.rs`)

- Neighbour offsets are precomputed as sample offsets into the source window.
- Normal mode with 1–5 channels sends interior pixels (those whose whole kernel lies inside the window, which with the usual halo is every pixel) through `smart_rows::<N, A>`. Each offset sweeps a whole row, so loads are contiguous. A rejected neighbour adds `-0.0`, an exact identity, instead of branching.
- Every pixel still sums its neighbours in the same order as before, so **the output is bit-identical**.
- Border pixels, Edge Only / Overlay Edge, and layers with 6+ channels keep the per-pixel path, now with precomputed offsets.
- If the row pass ever stops early it returns only the rows it finished, so the per-pixel fallback never reads an already-blurred centre.

## Timings

`cargo run --release -p photocraft-algo --example bench_filters2 smart`, 6000×4000 RGBA8, High quality, 20 threads:

| radius | before | after | speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | 0.55 s | 0.23 s | 2.4× |
| 12 | 6.25 s | 1.78 s | 3.5× |
| 100 | 3.64 s | 0.95 s | 3.8× |

`bench_filters2` gains the r12 and r100 rows (it only measured r3, which hid the slowdown). I also tried a planar (one array per channel) layout with per-channel passes. It was slower (r12 2.85 s), so it isn't included.

## Tests

`crates/algo/src/smart_blur_tests.rs` keeps the previous kernel as an oracle and compares bits across:

- Rgb, Gray, Cmyk and Lab layouts, plus Multichannel with 1–8 channels, each with and without alpha;
- radii 0.1–17.5, all three qualities, all three modes, two thresholds;
- output rects that are the usual tile, the whole window, overhanging the window, and empty;
- NaN, ±inf and -0 samples, and a 1 px window where every neighbour is outside.

Both fast paths were mutation-checked: breaking either one fails the oracle test.

- [x] `cargo test -p photocraft-algo --lib --tests`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p photocraft-algo --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`
- [x] `cargo xtask wasm`

No command, document field or format changes. No `xtask perf` scenario covers Smart Blur yet, so this PR doesn't move the scorecard.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

- **Bug Fixes**

  - Preserved expected behavior across blur modes, quality settings, thresholds, and channel configurations.

Create Rectangle / Ellipse / Triangle / Polygon (a single click with a Shape tool) showed Width and Height only in the ruler unit (Preferences › Units & Rulers), which is pixels by default. included.head: 4a3f3ba665a91b2934e9dd907655cdbd31cf1279
included.title: Liquify: Alt-drag brush resize keeps the brush in place and no longer paints a dab (#7884)
included.body:
Fixes #7884

### Problem
In Filter › Liquify, Alt+right-drag (or Ctrl+Alt-drag) changes the brush size and density (#4702), but two things were off:
- **The brush moved with the pointer.** The outline was drawn under the pointer, so it slid sideways as you dragged to resize, and so did the point the next stroke would start from. Outside Liquify, the brush tools' Alt-drag keeps the brush where it is and only changes its size, as Photoshop does in both places.
- **The press painted.** The resize started only once egui recognised the drag, a few points after the press. On that first frame the press was taken as a stroke, so every Alt+right-drag left a small dab, and a step to undo.

### Solution
`crates/ui-egui/src/liquify_ui.rs`:
- **Outline:** while the brush is being resized, it stays at the gesture's anchor (`brush_circle_at`), and so does the hover point the dialog keeps. Only its size changes.
- **Anchor:** the anchor is where the button went down (`press_origin`), so the outline doesn't jump when the gesture starts.
- **Start:** the gesture starts on the press (`is_pointer_button_down_on`), not on `drag_started`, so its first frame isn't a stroke.

The size and density mapping (`resized_brush`) is unchanged.

#7905 reports the moving outline too (its second point); it also says the gesture doesn't respond at all on Windows, which this doesn't address.

### Tests
- `alt_drag_resize_keeps_the_brush_where_it_started`, driving the real dialog (`show`) with pointer events:
  - an Alt+right press over the canvas, then a 60-point drag to the right;
  - afterwards the brush is larger, the brush point is still where the press was, and no stroke was recorded.

  Without the change it fails on both counts: the point follows the pointer, and the press leaves a stroke.
- `the_brush_outline_follows_the_pointer_except_while_resizing`: the outline position with and without a resize in progress.

```
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib liquify    # 16 passed
cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt --all -- --check                         # clean
```


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Brush outlines now remain anchored at the initial press position while resizing with Alt-drag.
  - Brush resizing begins promptly when the pointer is pressed, providing more responsive feedback.
  - Resizing no longer records unintended paint strokes.

included.head: aede66995d91ace98dfba8f159c841f0ef13fe84
included.title: Slice Select: Delete deletes the selected slice, not the layer (#7862)
included.body:
Fixes #7862

### Problem
With the Slice Select tool and a slice selected, pressing Delete didn't delete the slice. The key went on to Layer › Delete, so in a one-layer document the status bar said "a document must keep at least one layer", and in any other document it deleted the active layer. Photoshop deletes the selected slice. The Delete button in the Slice Select options bar already did, but not the key.

### Solution
- **`crates/ui-egui/src/slice_ui.rs`, new `keys`:** Delete or Backspace with no modifiers deletes the selected slice through `slice.delete`, as the options-bar button does, and clears the selection. It acts only with the Slice Select tool and a selected slice, and not while a text field or a widget that deletes with these keys has focus.
  - **Locked slices** (View › Lock Slices) are refused with the message the options bar shows, and stay.
  - **An auto slice** has nothing to delete: it is made from the user slices around it. The key does nothing there, and still doesn't reach the layer.
- **`crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs`:** it runs next to the selected-guide handler (`guide_select::keys`), before the shortcuts that delete layers or clear pixels.

### Tests
`slice_ui::tests::delete_deletes_the_selected_slice_not_the_layer`, through the app's shortcut handling, for both Delete and Backspace:
- a slice drawn with the Slice tool and selected with Slice Select is deleted, the document keeps its layer, and no error is shown;
- with View › Lock Slices on, the slice stays and the status says the slices are locked;
- with an auto slice selected, nothing is deleted and the layer stays.

It fails without the change: the key never reaches the slice handling.

```
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- slice_ui guide_select layer_shortcut   # 22 passed
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- shortcut delete                        # 143 passed
cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -- -D warnings                  # clean
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                       # clean
```


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Delete and Backspace now correctly remove a selected user slice in Slice Select mode.
  * Locked slices display an error instead of being deleted.
  * Auto slices remain protected from deletion.
  * Successful deletion clears the slice selection while preserving the document layer.

included.head: 194dcf3631ec81e481995b79060143931ae8ab27
included.title: Replace Contents: contents of another size keep the placement's centre, as in Photoshop (#7844)
included.body:
Fixes #7844

### Problem
Layer › Smart Objects › Replace Contents with contents of another pixel size kept the placement's scale but pinned the new contents to the old placement's top-left corner. Photoshop keeps the placement's centre (the transform's reference point), so new contents grow or shrink around the middle. Mockup templates rely on that: a print area whose artwork changes size stays where the designer centred it.

In the issue's case, a 200 × 200 placement centred at (500, 500) and replaced by 400 × 200 contents ended up centred at (600, 500), not (500, 500). At 150 % it ended up at (650, 500).

### Solution
`crates/engine/src/smart_cmds.rs`:
- **`replace_contents_bytes`** compares the old and new contents' bounds before the swap. It uses `source_image`, the cached decode the re-render uses anyway, so nothing is decoded twice. Each instance's placement is then moved by the difference of their centres, in source pixels. The new contents' centre lands where the old one did, and the placement's scale, rotation and skew are kept.
- **`move_in_source`** composes that move under the placement: `transform · translate(dx, dy)`. For a perspective placement it adds the move to the homography's third column (`H · T`).
- **What doesn't move:**
  - A warped or stacked instance is left as it was. Its mesh or stack is laid out over the old contents' box, so moving the placement wouldn't move the warp with it.
  - When the old contents can't be decoded (an unavailable linked file), the placement is kept as before.
  - Contents of the same size don't move.
- **Undo:** still one step for all instances.

Relink and Update Modified Content are unchanged.

**#6914** (Replace Contents `fit`: stretch / contain) touches the same command. Its default `keep` is this behaviour, so the two fit together: with this change, `keep` keeps the centre as Photoshop does.

### Tests
- **New `smart_cmds::tests::replaced_contents_of_another_size_keep_the_placement_centre`**, the issue's case scaled down: a 20 × 20 placement centred at (50, 50) replaced by 40 × 20 contents.
  - At 100 % the bounds go from (40, 40, 60, 60) to (30, 40, 70, 60).
  - At 150 % they go from (35, 35, 65, 65) to (19, 34, 81, 66): still centred on (50, 50). Resampling softens one edge pixel on each side, as the issue's expected width of 601 for 600 also shows.
  - Replacing with the same contents again doesn't move them.

  It fails without the fix: the bounds stay pinned to the top-left.
- **Updated `export_replace_and_linked_contents`:** it asserted the old top-left anchoring. It now checks that the replaced contents keep the old centre (within a pixel) and their scale, and it samples the linked update inside the new placement.

```
cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib smart_cmds             # 45 passed
cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test explicit_layer_target # 2 passed
cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test smart_duplicates      # 6 passed
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib replace               # 29 passed
cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                   # clean
```


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Replacing image contents with differently sized imagery now preserves the placed object’s scale and center, preventing unexpected shifts.
  * Linked instances remain aligned when their shared source is updated.
  * Repeated replacements with same-sized imagery preserve existing bounds.
  * Replacements continue when the previous linked source cannot be accessed, without changing placement.
  * Warped and stacked smart objects retain their existing source-space placement during replacement.

included.title: Brush: with airbrush build-up on, number keys set Flow and Shift+number sets Opacity (#7785)
included.body:
Fixes #7785.

In Photoshop, when airbrush-style build-up is on, the number keys set the brush's Flow and Shift+number sets its Opacity. PhotoCraft always set Opacity.

`opacity_keys::apply` now swaps the two roles for the Brush and the Eraser while the brush's `build_up` is on. Nothing changes for:
- the Pencil, which has no Flow;
- the Eraser in Pencil or Block mode, which has no build-up (its options bar already disables Flow and the airbrush button for those modes), so digits still set Opacity there;
- every other tool (layer opacity/fill, Gradient/Paint Bucket opacity).

Two-digit entry (4 then 5 = 45%) and the 1% Flow floor work as before. The module doc and the shortcut row in `docs/brush-parity.md` mention the swap.

Test: `with_build_up_digits_set_flow_and_shift_digits_set_opacity` covers the Brush with build-up (digit sets Flow, Shift+digit sets Opacity), the Pencil (unchanged), the Eraser in Brush mode (swapped) and in Pencil mode (not swapped). It fails on main, where the plain digit sets Opacity.

* **Documentation**

included.head: 8591ca19046071c27b56561c997935dc6dc98611
included.title: Scale layer-effect noise by coverage so it follows the glow
included.body:
Fixes #7833

## Cause
The effect `noise()` step skipped only pixels with coverage of exactly 0. It added a fixed-size offset `(n - 0.5) * 2 * amount` to every other pixel. The Softer glow and shadow blur leave tiny non-zero values across their whole rectangular reach, so pixels the glow barely touches (around 1e-18) got up to about 0.5 coverage from noise. That made a speckled rectangle that the map bounds cut off.

## Fix
Noise now scales the coverage, `v * (1 + (n - 0.5) * 2 * amount)`, instead of adding a fixed offset. The speckle fades out with the glow or shadow and can no longer show up where the effect itself is invisible. Full noise can still punch holes in the solid part.

## Verified
- Regression test `effects::tests::effect_noise_stays_inside_the_visible_falloff`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p photocraft-compose --lib effects::tests::effect_noise_stays_inside_the_visible_falloff`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Effect bounds (`margin()`), the blur and the GPU path are unchanged. The GPU already sends effects with noise to the CPU path, so the same fix covers Drop and Inner Shadow and Inner Glow there too.

included.title: Free Transform: a result may take what Memory Usage allows, not 2^30 px (#7807)
included.body:
Part of #7807 (the 2³⁰ px cap). Builds on #7837 (its first two commits); the last three commits are this PR. #7839 makes the error text copyable.

A transform's result was capped at 2³⁰ px, so a stitched layer past about 1 GP couldn't be transformed on any machine. Three changes:

- The warp writes each tile into the result as soon as it is warped. Before, every finished tile kept its `f32` pixels until the last one was done: 16 bytes a pixel of an RGBA result on top of the result itself.
- The result is priced in bytes at its pixel format (with the alpha the warp adds) against Preferences › Performance › Memory Usage (default 8192 MB), which `Session::apply_prefs` now passes to the engine, as it does the effect-cache budget. Past it, the message names the setting: "… would be 37708 x 35259 px (10144 MB), more than the 8192 MB Memory Usage allows (Preferences › Performance) …".
- A result the warp would clip is refused. The warp places pixels within ±2²⁰ px and clamps the rest away, so a wide strip could fit the budget and lose its end; a plain move past ±2²⁰ px already emptied the layer silently on main. It now says "… would reach past ±1048576 px, the farthest a transform places pixels".

Extra memory per result pixel and time, 100 MP 8-bit layer, release build, M4 Max:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| scale 110 % | 16.4 B, 0.8 s | 4.8 B, 0.6 s |
| rotate 15° | 12.5 B, 0.8 s | 3.4 B, 0.5 s |
| 90 % + 15°, Bilinear | 12.7 B, 0.5 s | 3.4 B, 0.3 s |
| 90 % + 15°, Bicubic | 19.9 B, 1.0 s | 12.4 B, 0.8 s |

The report's case (90 % and 15°, a 37708 x 35259 px 8-bit result) is refused on main; with this it takes 10.7 s and 6.1 GB on top of the 4.3 GB layer.

## Testing

- `a_gigapixel_layer_transforms_within_memory_usage`: the report's result fits the default at 8 bits, is refused at 16 bits with the message above, and fits with Memory Usage doubled.
- `memory_usage_is_what_a_transform_may_take` (integration test, real budget): refused at 1 MB, applied at 2 MB; fails on main.
- `a_result_past_the_warps_reach_is_refused_not_clipped`: a 2,000,016 px strip from x = 0 and a small layer moved 1.1M px are refused, the document untouched; the strip centred fits. Fails with the check off (the move then succeeds and leaves the layer empty). `output_clipped_matches_the_clamped_bounds` ties the check to the clamp.
- The #3773 and #6430 budget tests now use the byte budget; huge scales are still refused before anything is built.
- Engine unit tests run against 2²⁰ px of the widest format (32-bit CMYK with alpha, 20 MB), so every result the old 2²⁰ px test limit allowed still fits at any depth.
- algo, engine and ui-egui, merged into current main: 5881 tests pass; clippy `-D warnings`, wasm check, rustfmt, `xtask layers`, `scorecard --check` and `panic_hunt` clean.

## Not covered

- At 32 bits a pixel takes 16 bytes, so the default allows a smaller result than the old cap (537 MP rather than 1074 MP); the old cap let a 32-bit result alone take 16 GiB.
- A Bicubic downscale still makes a reduced copy of the source first (Photoshop's widened Bicubic); that copy isn't priced, and it is allocated infallibly, as on main. Everything the result itself needs is allocated fallibly.
- Puppet Warp keeps its own 2³⁰ px bound.
- No perf scenario covers Free Transform (P23 is not measurable), so `cargo xtask perf --quick` doesn't exercise this; the numbers above come from a throwaway harness.

included.head: 4d6d735ff9ea834dd373acb4edb874bd2db7ebaf
included.title: Camera raw: a developed raw keeps its EXIF (RW2 included), so File Info shows its Camera Data (#6957)
included.body:
Fixes #6957

### Problem
A camera raw that PhotoCraft develops opened without its EXIF, so File › File Info › Camera Data was empty: no make, model, date taken, exposure, f-stop, ISO or lens. The raw file carries all of them in its standard TIFF/EXIF directories. `raw.rs` noted that developed raws "carry no EXIF", and File Info reads Camera Data from the document's EXIF block.

### Solution
- **`crates/codecs/src/lib.rs`, new `raw_exif(bytes)`:** the EXIF block of a camera raw built on TIFF: IFD0's descriptive tags (make, model, date, software, artist, copyright) and the Exif and GPS directories. It is the block a TIFF opens with (`tiff_exif`), values copied as bytes and bounded as for TIFF, with two differences for a raw:
  - **Panasonic RW2** is read too. Its classic TIFF header has 0x55 (`IIU\0`) in place of 42 (`File::parse_raw`, used only here).
  - **PixelXDimension and PixelYDimension are left out.** In a raw they give the sensor's or the preview's size, not the developed image's.

  `None` when the file isn't built on a classic TIFF stream or has neither directory.
- **`crates/io/src/raw.rs`, `developed_document`:** the developed image's EXIF is the raw's. This covers the default open and a Camera Raw re-develop.
  - Covered: NEF, ARW, CR2, DNG and RW2, the formats the issue found with empty Camera Data.
  - Not covered: CR3 and RAF aren't TIFF streams. CR3 previews are #5922.
- **Orientation:** none to undo. The block never carries Orientation (IFD0's structure, resolution and orientation tags aren't copied), and the developed image is already upright. The upright-preview note was updated to say so.

Saving keeps the EXIF as for any other document, with the image's own resolution and orientation.

### Tests
`crates/io/tests/raw.rs`:
- **`a_developed_raw_keeps_its_exif`** (synthetic CR2 with Orientation 6): the developed document's EXIF reads back as Canon / Canon EOS Synthetic, exposure 1/100 s. It carries no orientation, and the document is still the upright 16 × 48.
- **`a_developed_rw2_keeps_its_exif`** (synthetic RW2 with an Exif directory holding exposure and pixel dimensions): the EXIF reads back as Panasonic / DC-Synthetic, 1/60 s. Its Exif directory has ExposureTime but no PixelXDimension or PixelYDimension.

Both fail without the fix: the developed document has no EXIF.

```
cargo test -p photocraft-io --test raw                                      # 14 passed
cargo test -p photocraft-codecs --lib tiff                                  # passed
cargo test -p photocraft-codecs --test tiff_exif                            # 7 passed
cargo clippy -p photocraft-codecs -p photocraft-io --lib --tests -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                  # clean
```

included.head: b287a884f4edc8d65d449f70b25716e995c21114
included.title: Actions: a background filter's step is recorded only by the recording it started in (#7289)
included.body:
Fixes #7289

### Problem
A background job (a filter started with `Session::start`, as the app runs Gaussian Blur and other slow filters) journals its step when its result is applied, not when it starts. An action that started recording in between got that step. For example:
- the job starts while recording A;
- A stops and B starts;
- the result lands, and B records a Gaussian Blur that was never run during it.

Replaying B then blurs. The same happened for a job started before any recording.

### Solution
A job remembers which recording it was started in, and only that recording gets its step.
- `ActionState::take` (`crates/engine/src/actions_cmds.rs`) counts recordings: each `actions.record` bumps it.
- `dispatch` (`crates/engine/src/jobs.rs`) stores the take that is recording when a job starts in `Running::recorded_by`. It does this once recording resumes after the command, so a job started while recording A is A's.
- `apply_job`: when another recording is running, its steps so far are committed first (`flush_recording`), and its start is moved past the job's journal entry. That recording keeps its steps before and after the result and leaves the job's out. A job started and applied in the same recording records as before.

As the issue leaves open, a job whose recording stopped before the result landed doesn't add a step to it afterwards.

### Tests
`jobs::tests::a_job_lands_in_the_recording_it_was_started_in_only`. Without the fix, the first case fails:
- **Started in A, applied after A stopped and B started:** A is empty. B holds only its own steps (`file.new` before the result, `desaturate` after it), not the blur.
- **Started before any recording, applied while B records:** B is empty.
- **Control, started and applied while A records:** A holds the blur.

```
cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib a_job_lands_in_the_recording   # passes; fails without the fix
cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib -- jobs:: actions                # 59 passed
cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests -- -D warnings          # clean
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                             # clean
```


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Background job results are now recorded in the action recording that was active when the job started, rather than being attributed to a later recording.
  * When the original recording remains active, it continues to capture the job result when the job is applied.
  * Journal entries from before a later recording began are no longer included in that recording because of a background job.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

included.head: 566bccf6bbea0cc150ed0f8f0954cab112fab428
included.title: Vanishing Point: perspective clone samples without allocating per pixel (#7491)
included.body:
Fixes #7491.

**What users saw:** a Vanishing Point perspective clone stroke made about three heap allocations per sampled pixel (4.6 million for one 40-dab stroke on a 24 MP image).

**Cause:** `sample` in `crates/algo/src/vanishing.rs` read its 2×2 bilinear footprint with `read_region` (output `Vec` plus a decoded default-pixel `Vec`) and `collect`ed the result into a new `Vec`, once per covered pixel of every dab.

**Change:** `sample` writes into caller-owned scratch. `clone_stroke` reads each dab's source footprint once into a reused buffer (`read_region_into`); a footprint outside it is read with one `read_region_into` into the same reused corner buffer (one tile lookup instead of four `read_pixel` calls). The window is skipped when it is more than 4× the dab's destination area (cloning from near to far in strong perspective), where decoding it would cost more than it saves. Output is byte-identical to `main`.

Why not just `read_pixel` for the four corners, as the issue suggests: I measured it, and it removed the allocations but was ~15% *slower* than `main`, because each corner is a separate `BTreeMap` tile lookup.

While rewriting the corner reads, `x0 + 2` became `saturating_add(1)` for the far corners: a source near `i32::MAX` panicked with "attempt to add with overflow" in debug builds. This is the same class as #918 (fixed for the destination footprint); I found no open issue for this line.

**Benchmark** (release, Apple Silicon, RGBA8 6000×4000, one 40-dab stroke of 300 px; harness kept out of the repo because the counting allocator needs `unsafe`):

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| heap allocations | 4,621,154 | 404 |
| time | 100–125 ms | 46–53 ms |
| whole-image checksum | identical | identical |

Near-to-far cloning toward the horizon, where the window is skipped (8000×6000, 200 dabs at v = 0.03 cloned from v = 0.97, 41 runs, median):

| dab size | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 30 px | 0.32 ms | 0.29 ms |
| 60 px | 0.98 ms | 0.81 ms |
| 120 px | 4.30 ms | 3.43 ms |

In that regime each sample still makes one allocation (`read_region_into` decodes the default pixel), against three on `main`.

**Tests:**
- `sample_at_the_edge_of_i32_does_not_overflow`: fails on `main` ("attempt to add with overflow").
- `sample_interpolates_across_tile_edges`: a footprint straddling a tile edge, read from the surface, from a window holding it, and from a window holding half of it; four different corners in four tiles (both axes of the corner order); plus the default pixel outside every tile.
- Byte-for-byte comparison against the old `clone_stroke` (not committed) on RGBA8/16/32F, Gray8/GrayA8/Gray32F, CMYKA8, CMYK32F and Lab16A, on a torn-off plane, near the horizon and with NaN/inf/out-of-plane points: identical.
- `cargo nextest run -p photocraft-algo`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-algo --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`.

**Not covered:** #7492 (`Surface::tile_mut` cloning the default pixel), handled in #7556.

**Overlap:** #3281 (Vanishing Point tear-off and Stamp tool) restructures `clone_stroke` and touches the same `sample` line, so these two conflict. If #3281 lands first, I'll merge `main` and redo this on top of it.

_Investigated and written with Claude Code; I reviewed and ran it locally._

included.head: 1f6dbf8415b33cb15e8ce4cc30b5acf5e6a449f4
included.title: Lasso: a short straight segment places a vertex instead of closing the outline
included.body:
Addresses #7629 for the Lasso's ⌥ mode. Measured; the reasoning for the dedicated Polygonal Lasso is at the end, and if the report is about that one instead, say so and I'll keep looking.

### What I measured

With the **Lasso** tool and ⌥ held (Photoshop's straight-segment mode), a click closer to the last vertex than the radius for grabbing the first one ended the selection instead of placing the vertex:

```
three ⌥ clicks at (50,50) (90,50) (90,90)   →  drag points = 3
a fourth ⌥ click at (85,91), 5 points away  →  before: drag = None, selection committed (50,50)-(90,90)
                                               after:  drag points = 4, nothing committed
```

That radius is `8.0 / point_zoom`, so every segment shorter than 8 points on screen was impossible to draw: the click meant to continue the outline finished it instead, and tracing anything small meant the selection kept ending after three vertices.

### What changed

Both closing gestures stay; they just stop sharing one radius:

- **clicking the first vertex** is aiming at a target, and keeps the 8-point grab radius;
- **clicking the last vertex again** is the same click repeated, so it only has to allow for a hand's jitter — 3 points (`SAME_POINT`).

Everything else is untouched: Enter closes, Escape cancels, Backspace and right-click retract, releasing ⌥ with the button up closes, and the Freeform Pen still ends an open path by clicking its last point.

### Tests

`a_short_alt_lasso_segment_places_a_vertex_instead_of_closing` pins all three cases: the 5-point click places a fourth vertex with nothing committed; a click 1–2 points from the last vertex still closes the outline; and a click 4–5 points from the *first* vertex still closes it. On `main` the first case leaves `drag = None` with the triangle already committed.

The existing `clicking_the_last_point_again_closes_the_outline` passes unchanged — it clicks 1.4 points from the last vertex, inside the jitter allowance. My first attempt dropped that gesture for the Lasso altogether and the gate caught it, which is what sent me to the two-radius version.

### The dedicated Polygonal Lasso, for the record

I could not reproduce it there, and I checked the two mechanisms that looked likely:

- `polygon_click` closes only near the **first** vertex, so nothing stops a short segment;
- egui reports a double click from the time between clicks **and** their distance (`max_click_dist`, 6 points), so two quick clicks further apart than that are not a double click. A probe placing a fourth vertex 4 units from the third, clicked in the next frame, keeps the vertex and commits nothing.

So if the reporter was on the Polygonal Lasso proper, this is not their bug, and their zoom level and roughly how short the segments were would tell us where to look.

`cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, layers, wasm all pass.

included.head: e71fa3ab161b4a6485004f906a86eb32dca2f565
included.title: Actions: a setting Photoshop's event cannot hold refuses the step
included.body:
Closes #7668, and fixes two more of the same kind that it turned up.

Crystallize is mapped with one field:

```rust
ev!("Crst", "crystallize", "Crystallize", "filter.pixelate.crystallize", &[F("ClSz", "cellSize", Kind::Long)]),
```

while the command takes `{"cellSize":3..300=10,"seed":u32=0}`. Photoshop's `Crst` descriptor has nowhere to put a seed, so `seed: 37` was dropped on export and replay seeded from 0 — a different pattern, with `skipped` empty and nothing in the file to say so. The report measures 583 differing colour components at every bit depth.

Auditing every mapped event against the params its command accepts turned up two more:

| step | silently dropped | what replay does instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `filter.pixelate.crystallize` | `seed` | seeds from 0 (#7668) |
| `filter.blur.radialBlur` | `centerX`, `centerY` | spins or zooms about the middle |
| `filter.other.minimum` / `.maximum` | `preserve` | keeps squareness |

(`layer.flattenImage`, `tools.swapColors` and `filter.blur.blur` also take params the event has no field for, but those are targets and selectors rather than settings that change the pixels, so they are left alone.)

### What changed

A table of the settings a mapped event cannot hold, with the value the event plays as:

```rust
const UNHOLDABLE: &[(&str, &[(&str, &str)])] = &[
    ("filter.pixelate.crystallize", &[("seed", "0")]),
    ("filter.blur.radialBlur", &[("centerX", "0.5"), ("centerY", "0.5")]),
    ("filter.other.minimum", &[("preserve", "squareness")]),
    ("filter.other.maximum", &[("preserve", "squareness")]),
];
```

A step that leaves such a setting at the value the event plays as exports exactly as before. A step that sets something else is refused: strict export names it, `skipUnsupported: true` leaves it out and reports it. That is the path `pixel_target` already takes for a filter aimed at a mask, "no field for a mask … so such a step can't be exported faithfully".

What this deliberately does **not** do is invent descriptor keys. I have no Photoshop to read a real `.atn` with, so writing a guessed `FlRs` into `Crst` or a `Cntr` into `RdlB` would be a clean-room violation and could make the file wrong in Photoshop as well as here. If you can confirm those keys from a Photoshop-written file, preserving the settings is strictly better than refusing them and I will follow up.

### Tests

`a_setting_the_event_cannot_hold_is_refused` — each of the four steps with a non-default value: strict export fails naming the step, `skipUnsupported` reports it in `skipped`. `settings_at_the_value_the_event_plays_still_export` — the same steps at the default (and with the setting absent): written, `skipped` empty.

  * Crystallize exports support a seed of `0` or no seed; Radial Blur supports a center of `(0.5, 0.5)` or no center settings; Minimum and Maximum support `preserve: "roundness"` or no preserve setting.

included.head: f30966569467231f34765998d136eb36ed6140f2
included.title: Actions: a Selective Color step keeps the values of its scalar form
included.body:
Closes #7672.

`image.adjustments.selectiveColor` takes a range two ways, and `adjust_cmds::selective_from_params` reads both:

```jsonc
{"reds": [35, 0, 0, 0]}                  // the array form: c, m, y, k
{"colors": "reds", "cyan": 35}           // the scalar form: one range, the channels it changes
```

`selective_to` only looked for the arrays. A step recorded in the scalar form exported with an empty `ClrC` list — a Selective Color adjustment that changes nothing — and `skipped` was empty, so nothing said the values had gone. The report measures it on one red pixel: `[0.6509804, 0, 0, 1]` run directly, `[1, 0, 0, 1]` after export and replay.

### What changed

`selective_to` now builds the rows the way the command does: the arrays first, then the scalar form over the range it names, so a step that gives both (`"reds": [...]` plus `"colors": "reds", "cyan": 35`) exports what playing it would produce. An unknown range in `"colors"` cannot be written and refuses the step, as before.

### Tests

`a_selective_color_step_in_the_scalar_form_keeps_its_values` — the reported step round-trips to `reds: [35, 0, 0, 0]` with `method: "absolute"`; the scalar form over an array keeps both; and the array-only form is unchanged. On `main` the first assertion reads an empty adjustment.

`cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, layers, wasm all pass.
