included.head: fd6fc92015fd08560362b4b32844edf97722f292
included.title: packaging: the portable zip holds the files, not a folder with the files in it
included.body:
Fixes #7699.

`Compress-Archive -Path <folder>` archives the folder itself, so the portable zip contained

```
photocraft-<version>-windows-<arch>-portable\photocraft.exe
photocraft-<version>-windows-<arch>-portable\photocraft-cli.exe
photocraft-<version>-windows-<arch>-portable\portable.txt
...
```

rather than those files at its root. `<folder>\*` archives the contents.

Four things say the root is what was meant:

- this script's own synopsis — `photocraft-<version>-windows-<arch>-portable.zip   photocraft.exe + photocraft-cli.exe + portable.txt`;
- `portable.txt` ("While this file sits next to photocraft.exe…") and the advice to "copy the whole folder", which with a wrapper means the user's folder contains one more folder before the exe;
- VectorCraft's `packaging/windows/windows7.ps1`, which writes its portable zip with `Compress-Archive -Path (Join-Path $Stage '*')`;
- storytold/craft-launcher#627 — the launcher's portable install looked for the program at the archive root and found a wrapper folder instead. (That side now unwraps a single wrapper folder, so this is belt and braces; if you would rather keep the wrapper here, the launcher copes either way and the synopsis is what should change.)

Nothing read the layout back after writing it, which is how it drifted, so the three files are now checked inside the archive and the build fails loudly if they are not at its root.

### How this was checked

I have no Windows or PowerShell here, so I have not run `package.ps1`: the change copies the line that already works in `windows7.ps1`, and the check uses `Expand-Archive` + `Test-Path` + `throw` exactly as `sign.ps1` and this script use them. `packaging-lint` runs on this PR and is the static check; a maintainer running the packager on a Windows runner is the real one. No Rust is touched, so `cargo xtask ci` has nothing to say about it.

included.head: ab844f9cbcd1f1839ed7f286776331cb72e399aa
included.title: Actions: a fractional setting an integer field cannot hold is refused, not rounded
included.body:
Closes #7669 and #7670. **#7671 (Stroke) is not in this change** — see below.

`Kind::Long` wrote its param through `long()`, which rounds:

```rust
fn long(v: f64) -> D {
    D::Integer(v.round().clamp(f64::from(i32::MIN), f64::from(i32::MAX)) as i32)
}
```

Photoshop's field really is an integer, so a fractional setting cannot be written — but rounding it put a different edit in the file than the one recorded, with `skipped` empty and nothing to say so. Measured through `actions.save` and back:

| step | recorded | in the file | read back |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filter.pixelate.crystallize` | `cellSize: 5.4` | `ClSz 5` | `cellSize: 5` |
| `filter.distort.ripple` | `amount: 81.4` | `Amnt 81` | `amount: 81` |

(The first row is the new round-trip test run against `main`: `left: Some(5.0), right: Some(5.4)`.) The reports measure what that does to the pixels — 385 to 583 differing colour components at every bit depth.

### Why Stroke is out

`edit.stroke` normalises the width itself:

```rust
// crates/engine/src/extra_cmds.rs:137
let width = p.get("width").and_then(Value::as_f64).filter(|w| w.is_finite()).unwrap_or(1.0).clamp(1.0, 250.0).ceil() as usize;
```

`.ceil()`, so `width: 2.4` renders at **3** — an integer field can hold that exactly, and refusing the step would throw away something expressible. On `main` it renders at 3 and exports `Wdth 2` with `skipped` empty, which is wrong in both directions this PR could have gone. @PerchAnton's #7696 normalises it instead, which is the only approach that reproduces what the user saw. My first version refused it; that was my mistake.

### What changed

The refusal is a field's own kind, `Kind::LongExact`, carried by the two fields whose command uses the setting as written:

- Crystallize's `ClSz` — `cell_size: f(p, "cellSize", 10.0).clamp(3.0, 300.0)`, no rounding
- Ripple's `Amnt` — `amount: f(p, "amount", 100.0).clamp(-999.0, 999.0)`, no rounding

`long_exact` returns `None` for a value such a field cannot hold — a fraction, or a magnitude past `i32` — and `fields_to` passes that up. The step then takes the path a step with no Photoshop equivalent already takes: strict export names it and fails, `skipUnsupported: true` leaves it out and lists it in `skipped`.

The first version sent **all 26** `Kind::Long` fields through `long_exact` on the strength of three reports, one of which turned out to need the opposite. The other 24 keep `long()` until someone has read each against its command.

Refusing, rather than exporting a near miss, is what the rest of this file does: `pixel_target` already refuses a filter step aimed at a mask because "Photoshop's descriptor for a plain event has no field for a mask … so such a step can't be exported faithfully".

The strict error now reads "can't be written as a Photoshop step: it has no equivalent event, or a setting its event can't hold", since both cases arrive there.

### Tests

- `a_fractional_setting_an_integer_field_cannot_hold_is_refused_not_rounded` — both reported steps: strict export fails naming the step, `skipUnsupported` reports it in `skipped`. On `main` the first `unwrap_err` panics with `Ok(…)`.
- `whole_number_settings_for_integer_fields_still_round_trip` — the same with whole numbers, plus `edit.stroke`, which still exports: written, `skipped` empty, and every param read back as itself. Numbers compare by value and anything else as it is, so string settings (`size`, `color`, `location`) are checked rather than passing vacuously through `as_f64` on both sides.

`cargo xtask ci`: all 5 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, layers, wasm).

### Still to do here

@PerchAnton has offered their `atn_crystallize_cell_size.rs` and `atn_ripple_amount.rs` suites (four tests each) for this PR, with their authorship kept. Waiting on @echelon to confirm the order before moving them, per the discussion below.

### Not in this change

`long()` stays for the hand-written mappings that use it (`Lvls` input/output levels, `Thsh`, `Tlrn`, `Qlty`, `NCol`, `Dpth`, the Color Balance triples). Most take whole numbers from a range the command already clamps, and each is its own command scope; if you'd like them refused on the same footing, I'm happy to follow up.

included.head: 8f0a4842982c209a5e8735e197a26f078ebfe682
included.title: Move tool: a selection lifts up to a pixel's own coverage (#7655)
included.body:
Closes #7655.

⌘-clicking a layer thumbnail loads the layer's transparency as a partial selection, correctly. But dragging that selection with the Move tool left a faint ghost of the soft pixels behind, as in the issue's second screenshot.

The Move tool floats the selected pixels (`select.float` → `Floating::new`). For each pixel it lifted `a·k` and left `a·(1 − k)`, where `a` is the pixel's alpha and `k` the selection. With the selection made from the layer's own transparency, `k = a`, so every half-transparent pixel left `a·(1 − a)` behind (64 where `a` was 128). The lifted copy also came out fainter than the original.

### Photoshop, measured

All on macOS 27 with Photoshop 2025, exported with Quick Export as PNG and read pixel by pixel.

**The issue's case.** I used a layer with a red block whose alpha ramps from 0 to 255, ⌘-clicked its thumbnail, and dragged with the Move tool.
- Nothing is left where it was.
- The moved pixels keep their alpha: 2, 9, 64, 128, 192, 252, the same as the original.

**A case that separates the rules.** Layer B is a uniform 50 % red fill (alpha 128). The selection is another layer's ramp transparency (`k`). I moved B and read the residue left behind:

| `k` | 0.035 | 0.13 | 0.25 | 0.38 | **0.50** | 0.63 | 0.75 | 0.88 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Photoshop leaves | 121 | 100 | 72 | 38 | **0** | 6 | 8 | 6 |
| `a·(1 − k)`, before | 123 | 111 | 96 | 80 | 64 | 48 | 32 | 16 |
| `max(a − k, 0)`, this PR | 119 | 94 | 64 | 32 | **0** | 0 | 0 | 0 |

In every column, what Photoshop lifts plus what it leaves equals the pixel's alpha. It leaves nothing once the selection covers the pixel's own coverage. So Photoshop lifts about `min(a, k)`, not `a·k`.

The coverage rule is exact when `k = a` (this issue) and for opaque pixels. Elsewhere it is within 8 levels of Photoshop; the product was up to 64 levels off.

### Change

- **`float_cmds::Floating::new`:** the piece takes `min(a, k)` of a pixel's alpha, and the layer keeps `max(a − k, 0)`.
- **Opaque pixels split as before.** For `a = 1`, `min(1, k) = k` and `1 − k`, so a feathered move of an opaque layer is unchanged.
- **Also unchanged:** a copy (⌥) still leaves the original, and the Background's hole still takes the background colour.

Not changed: Free Transform with a selection (`transform_cmds::split_selected`) still uses the product. I haven't measured Photoshop there.

### Tests

- New: `a_layers_own_transparency_floats_its_soft_pixels_whole` (float_cmds/tests). It checks that:
  - a half-transparent area floated by its own transparency leaves alpha 0 behind and arrives at 0.5;
  - an opaque area moves whole;
  - a half selection of an opaque pixel still splits it 0.5 / 0.5.

  It fails without the fix, because 0.25 is left behind.
- `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, the engine suite (2,015 tests), `panic_hunt -- --ignored`, the release build, `cargo xtask wasm` and `cargo xtask layers` pass. I ran these in this branch's own target directory.

### Verified in the app

On macOS 27 with a release build, using the same files as in Photoshop. In each case I loaded the selection, dragged with the Move tool, deselected and exported.

- **Ramp, before the fix:** a pink ghost, alpha up to 64.
- **Ramp, with the fix:** no residue, and the moved alpha is 2, 9, 34, 64, 128, 192, 252, as in Photoshop.
- **Two-layer case, with the fix:** the residue is the bottom row of the table, within 8 levels of Photoshop and exact at `k = a`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

  * Copying partially transparent pixels preserves their opacity in both the original and copied locations.

included.head: 3a0596e775fc4c69b8206b4bfb964cfbcd46b17b
included.title: Transform a type layer with a missing font as its pixels (#7278)
included.body:
Closes #7278.

Rotating or scaling a type layer whose font is missing set the text again in a substitute font. Free Transform updates the layer's transform, then `refresh_text` re-renders the text with whatever face the font database supplies. With the font missing, that is the fallback, so the glyphs change on commit even though the preview showed the original pixels turning.

### Photoshop, checked

I used a PSD with "Missing" set in Chalkduster, with the font name in the file changed to `Chalkdustqz` so neither app can find it.

- **⌘T:** Photoshop 2025 says the fonts are missing and the layer "may look fuzzy or pixelated if you transform it". It offers Transform or Cancel.
- **On Transform:** a 15° rotate turns the existing Chalkduster pixels. The layer stays a type layer, and its font still reads `[Chalkdustqz]`.

### Change

- **`transform_cmds::apply_transform`:** for a type layer with missing fonts and a rendered cache (`keeps_pixels`), the cache is warped with the transform, the way a smart object's fallback cache is. The layer's `transform` still updates as before.
- **`refresh_text`:** for such a layer, it only rebuilds the TySh record through the new `type_cmds::refresh_record`, so a PSD save carries the new transform. It doesn't re-render the text.
- **`check_layer_budget`:** now prices that warp too, so an oversized one is refused before anything changes.
- **Unchanged:** a type layer whose fonts are all present still re-renders from its transform, so it stays sharp. Distort and Perspective on type are still refused.

Not in this PR: Photoshop's confirmation dialog before the transform. This PR keeps PhotoCraft's existing missing-font warnings and just transforms.

### Tests

- New: `a_type_layer_with_a_missing_font_transforms_its_pixels` (transform_cmds). It creates a type layer in a missing font and gives it pixels the fallback face would never draw, as a PSD would. After a translate, it checks that:
  - the layer is still a type layer with the new transform;
  - the same pixels moved by the translation;
  - the TySh record is rebuilt.

  It fails without the fix, because the cache is re-rendered with the fallback face.
- `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, the engine suite (2,015 tests), `panic_hunt -- --ignored`, the release build, `cargo xtask wasm` and `cargo xtask layers` pass. I ran these in this branch's own target directory.

### Verified in the app

On macOS 27 with a release build, side by side with Photoshop 2025, using the same PSD:

- **Before the fix:** a 15° Free Transform re-set "Missing" in the fallback sans.
- **With the fix:** the rotated Chalkduster pixels stay, the same as in Photoshop. Type › Resolve Missing Fonts still lists `Chalkdustqz`.
- **Round trip:** saved to PSD from PhotoCraft and opened in Photoshop. The layer shows the rotated Chalkduster pixels and is still a type layer naming `[Chalkdustqz]`.

included.head: 35c7065692e4d6e2bcab8dd3f321a3ab5ed77bd8
included.title: Refuse .atn export of resolution-only Image Size without keepPrintSize
included.body:
Fixes #7245

## Cause
An .atn Image Size descriptor with only a resolution and a resample mode imports as keepPrintSize:true. Strict export wrote that descriptor for a resolution-only command that never had keepPrintSize. After the round trip the command scaled pixels: an 8×8 document recorded as a resolution change to 144 ppi (no pixel scaling) came back as 16×16 at 144 ppi instead of 8×8.

## Fix
`image_size_to` now refuses to export a resolution-only Image Size with a resample mode unless `keepPrintSize` is true. The step is reported as skipped instead of silently changing meaning. A regression test checks that the refusal happens.

## Verified
- Regression tests `atn_cmds::tests::image_size_resolution_only_does_not_gain_keep_print_size`, `atn_cmds::tests::image_size_intentional_controls_still_round_trip`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib atn_cmds::tests::image_size_`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The import mapping in `image_size_from` is unchanged, so descriptors from Photoshop still import as keep-print-size. Explicit keepPrintSize:true and explicit width/height commands still round-trip as before. The separate resample:"none" case from #7189 is also untouched and still exports.

included.head: 9f1083d31ed7cac99d48ebf94621ca67b78c81c4
included.title: Move typed text with a drag from just outside it (#5956)
included.body:
Closes #5956.

While typing, any press outside the text committed it (`type_tool::pointer_down`: "a click outside commits"). Photoshop 2025 moves the text when the press is just outside it, shows the Move cursor there, and keeps typing. Only a press further out commits.

### Photoshop, measured

On macOS at 100 %, while typing point text:

| Where the drag starts | Photoshop |
|---|---|
| about 20 pt below and left of the glyphs | moves the text, still typing |
| 35 pt to the right of the glyphs | moves the text, still typing |
| 48 pt from the glyphs | commits the text, which doesn't move |
| about 60 pt or 100 pt away | commits the text, which doesn't move |

### Change

- **`type_transform`:** `pointer` gets a plain-press branch. When the press is outside the text frame but within `MOVE_REACH_PT` (40 screen points) of it, it starts the existing temporary type transform with `Hit::Inside`, which is a move.
  - That's the same gesture the ⌘/Ctrl drag inside the frame already uses. Typing carries on, and the release applies one `type.edit` transform in the session.
  - The start code that the ⌘ branch and the new branch share moved into `start`.
- **Unchanged:** a paragraph box's handles still resize the box. Further out, a press commits as before.
- **`cursor`:** shows Move in that zone (`move_zone`), so the pointer tells you a drag will move the text.

### Tests

- New: `a_drag_just_outside_the_typed_text_moves_it` (type_tool_tests). It checks:
  - 20 pt right of the frame the cursor is Move, and a drag moves the text by the drag, keeps typing, and adds one History step;
  - 100 pt away there is no Move cursor, and a click commits.

  It fails without the fix: no Move cursor, and the press commits.
- `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, the ui-egui suite (3,193 tests), `cargo xtask wasm` and `cargo xtask layers` pass. I ran these in this branch's own target directory.

### Verified in the app

On macOS 27 with a release build, side by side with Photoshop 2025:

- **Near the text:** I typed "Hello" with the Type tool and dragged from about 25 pt to the right of it. The text moved with the drag and the caret stayed, so typing carries on.
- **Far from it:** a click about 90 pt away committed the text where it had been moved.

Both match Photoshop.

included.head: b3224447a9d721c2210d8cea364266522b32f35b
included.title: Carry on an open path from its end with the Pen (#6593)
included.body:
Closes #6593.

After a Pen path was finished, with Escape or ↩, a Pen click on one of its endpoints started a new subpath at that spot. Photoshop 2025 carries on drawing the same path from there. To check, I drew two anchors, pressed Escape, then clicked the last anchor and placed another point: Photoshop extended the path to three anchors.

`vector_ui::pen_down` only looked at the path being drawn. With no path in progress, every press started a new one, and `commit_path` added it to the selected path as another subpath.

### Change

- **Resuming:** with no Pen path in progress, a press on the first or last anchor of an open subpath of the path a new one would join loads that subpath into the Pen (`resume_at`). That path is the one selected in the Paths panel, else the work path.
  - From the last anchor it continues as it was.
  - From the first anchor it is reversed, with in and out handles swapped, so drawing carries on past that end.
  - The press then acts on the Pen's last anchor as before, so a drag from it pulls out the next segment's handle.
- **Committing:** `PenPath::resumes` records which subpath was picked up. `commit_path` writes it back in place with `path.set` (`with_resumed_subpath`) as one History step, instead of adding a second subpath. Only that subpath's anchors and closing change, so its path operation is kept. The draft remembers its document and the subpath as it was. If either changed before the commit (another document, or the path edited meanwhile), the drawing is added as a new subpath instead, so nothing is overwritten. Closing on the far anchor closes that subpath.
- **Unchanged:** Shape mode and a targeted vector mask, which take new paths, never resume. A press anywhere else starts a new subpath as before.

### Tests

- New: `the_pen_carries_on_an_open_path_from_either_end` (pen_variants_tests) checks:
  - Extending from the last anchor gives one subpath of 3 anchors, in one History step.
  - From the first anchor, the subpath is reversed and continues past it.
  - A press elsewhere still adds a second subpath.
  - Closing on the far end of a resumed subpath closes it.

  It fails without the fix: the old code made a second subpath.
- New: `a_resumed_subpath_keeps_its_operation_and_a_stale_draft_adds_a_new_one`. A Subtract subpath stays Subtract when carried on; a draft whose path was replaced meanwhile lands as a second subpath.
- `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, the ui-egui suite (3,194 tests), `cargo xtask wasm` and `cargo xtask layers` pass.

### Verified in the app

On macOS 27 with a release build, side by side with Photoshop 2025:

- **Before the click:** two Pen anchors, then Escape. The path stays (History: Work Path), as in Photoshop.
- **The resume:** a click on its last anchor, then a new point. The line carries on from that anchor, with one more History step.
- **The result:** `path.info` over the control channel shows a work path of one subpath with three anchors, as in Photoshop.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

  * Click elsewhere to start a separate subpath, or click the opposite endpoint to close and commit the resumed path.

included.title: Open the selection menu on a Quick Selection right-click (#7268)
included.body:
Closes #7268.

A right-click on the canvas with the Quick Selection tool opened the Brush Preset picker (size and hardness). `paint_mouse::has_brush_picker` includes Quick Selection, because it has the options-bar brush chip, and that same check decided what the canvas right-click opened. `canvas_tool_menu::applies`, which lists the tools whose right-click opens the selection menu, didn't include it.

In Photoshop 2025, a right-click with Quick Selection opens the same menus as the other selection tools:

- **With a selection:** Deselect, Select Inverse, Feather…, Select and Mask…, Save Selection…, Make Work Path…, Layer Via Copy, Layer Via Cut, Free Transform, Transform Selection, Fill…, Stroke… and so on.
- **Without one:** a context menu.

Its brush is set from the options bar.

### Change

- `canvas_tool_menu::applies` now includes `Tool::QuickSelection`.
- A new `paint_mouse::right_click_picker`: the tools with a picker and no canvas menu. The canvas right-click (`canvas_buttons`) and the control channel's secondary pointer (`pointer_secondary`) use it. `has_brush_picker` still decides who has the chip, so the Quick Selection tool's chip opens and closes the picker as before.

### Tests

- New: `quick_selection_chip_toggles_the_picker_and_right_click_opens_the_selection_menu`. The chip opens and closes the picker; a right-click opens the selection menu and no picker. It fails without the fix.
- The canvas-menu tests that listed Quick Selection with the brush tools (`brush_picker_taps_…`, `brush_chip_toggles_…`, `control_channel_opening_uses_the_same_dismissal_guard`) now expect the selection menu for it. `secondary_taps_keep_selection_menus_open` covers it with and without a selection.
- `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, the ui-egui suite (3,193 tests), `cargo xtask wasm` and `cargo xtask layers` pass.

### Verified in the app

On macOS 27 with a release build, side by side with Photoshop 2025:

- **With a selection:** a Quick Selection right-click opens the selection menu with the same rows as Photoshop's (Deselect … Content-Aware Fill…).
- **The chip:** still opens the Brush Preset picker.
- **Without a selection:** a right-click opens PhotoCraft's existing no-selection menu, the one the other selection tools use (Select All, Reselect, Color Range…, Load Selection…). Photoshop's no-selection menu also lists layer commands for every selection tool. That's outside this change.

included.title: Show Technique and Range in the glow Layer Style pages (#6698)
included.body:
Closes #6698.

The Layer Style dialog left out glow settings that the engine already supports (`layer.layerStyle.innerGlow` / `outerGlow` take `technique` and `range`):

- **Inner Glow** had no Technique and no Range.
- **Outer Glow** had no Technique, and showed Range before Contour, where Photoshop shows it after.

Since the issue was filed, Source and Choke were added. Anti-aliased is the checkbox beside Contour.

- **Inner Glow fields**, in Photoshop 2025's order: Blend Mode, Opacity, Color, **Technique** (Softer / Precise), Source, Choke, Size, Contour (+ Anti-aliased), **Range**, Noise.

- **Engine defaults:** both glows' defaults gain `technique: "softer"`, Inner Glow's gains `range: 50`, and the `innerGlow` command docs now list `range`. These are Photoshop's factory values.

Not in this PR: **Jitter**. It only acts on gradient glows, which the dialog doesn't offer yet (its Color field is a single swatch), so I left it for a follow-up with the gradient fill.

- New: `glows_show_and_keep_technique_and_range`. It checks both glows' field order, that a Precise Inner Glow at 30 % Range and a Precise Outer Glow show those values in the dialog, and that OK keeps them. It fails without the fix: the Inner Glow fields lack Technique and Range.

included.head: ec0fc7cb0e1aae518e1ea572494e6b626852856d
included.title: Actions: Minimum / Maximum with Preserve: Roundness is no longer exported as Squareness (#7233)
included.body:
Fixes #7233

### Problem
`filter.other.minimum` and `filter.other.maximum` take `preserve: "squareness" | "roundness"`, but their `.atn` event (`Mnm ` / `Mxm `) maps the radius only. A step with `preserve: "roundness"` was exported without the option, even by strict export. On import it replayed as the default Squareness, which changes the shape at the corners and therefore the pixels and any mask made from them, and nothing was reported.

### Solution
`crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs`:
- `ev!` gains an optional `unless` guard: params the descriptor can't carry, so the step isn't exported. That is the same treatment `pixel_target` already gives a step aimed at a mask or channel.
- Minimum and Maximum use it with `preserves_roundness`.

As a result, strict export refuses an action holding such a step and names it. Export with `skipUnsupported` leaves the step out and lists it as skipped. Squareness, explicit or by default, exports as before.

As the issue suggests, this refuses the case rather than guessing Photoshop's descriptor for the shape option. Without a Photoshop-recorded action using Roundness, the encoding can't be verified; once one is available, the shape can be mapped and this guard dropped.

### Tests
`atn_cmds::tests::minimum_and_maximum_with_roundness_are_not_exported_as_squareness`, for both filters (fails before this change):
- with `preserve: "roundness"`, strict export is an error, and lenient export reports the step as skipped;
- with no `preserve` or `"squareness"`, the step exports and imports back with radius 2 and no other shape.

```
cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib atn   # 16 passed
cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt --all -- --check                  # clean
```


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Minimum and Maximum filter steps configured with `preserve: "roundness"` are now reported as unsupported during export: strict exports fail, while skip-unsupported exports mark the steps as skipped.
  * Steps with no preserve setting or with `preserve: "squareness"` continue to export and import with their radius intact.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

included.head: f2a487b08845e907d78368767f236fc478fb8ae4
included.title: Flatpak: a second launch hands its files to the running PhotoCraft over a Unix socket (#1540)
included.body:
Part of #1540 (the Flatpak side of #3708 / #3755).

## What changed

Inside a Flatpak, a second launch now hands its files to the running PhotoCraft over a Unix socket instead of a loopback port. #3755's hand-off binds `127.0.0.1` and records the port in `instance.json`; every `flatpak run` gets its own network namespace, so the second sandbox's loopback never reaches the first and the launch fell back to a separate window, as the PR noted. `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/app/<app id>/` is the same directory in every sandbox of the app and the user's alone (0700), so the primary listens on `instance.sock` there (0600) when `FLATPAK_ID` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` are set, and writes `"socket"` instead of `"port"` to `instance.json`. Everything else is unchanged: the `instance.lock` election, the 256-bit token checked first and in constant time, the client cap, the request deadline, the `ok`-only-once-taken reply and the retry loop. A socket file left by a crashed primary is unlinked under the lock before binding; the primary removes its socket on shutdown. Outside Flatpak, and on Windows, nothing changes.

- `apps/photocraft/src/single_instance.rs`: `Transport` (`Loopback` | `Socket(path)`), chosen by `transport()`; `Endpoint` in `instance.json`; `Listener` and `Stream` over the two socket kinds; `claim_in` takes the transport so tests can pick it.
- `docs/development.md`: the "One instance per user" paragraph describes the sandbox case and drops the "needs its own follow-up" note.

## Evidence

The built binary run twice with the sandbox's environment (`FLATPAK_ID=ai.storyteller.photocraft XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000`), the second with another file while the first is open:

```
$ cat ~/.config/photocraft/instance.json
{"pid":175734,"socket":"/run/user/1000/app/ai.storyteller.photocraft/instance.sock","token":"…"}
$ ls -l /run/user/1000/app/ai.storyteller.photocraft/instance.sock
srw------- 1 diego diego 0 Oct 18 23:48 /run/user/1000/app/ai.storyteller.photocraft/instance.sock
$ photocraft ~/Pictures/photocraft-test/blue.png
INFO  [main] photocraft: handed 1 file(s) to the running PhotoCraft
exit=0 after 0.85 s
```

The file opened as a tab in the first window. On the real Flatpak (0.10.0, `--share=network` not granted) the same second launch opens a separate window, which is the report in #1540; with `flatpak override --user --share=network` it hands over through loopback, which confirms the namespace as the cause. That `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/app/ai.storyteller.photocraft` exists inside the sandbox was checked with `flatpak run --command=sh`.

In two real sandboxes (this head built in release, packaged with `package.sh --formats tar` and the bundle manifest, installed as branch `test`, network not shared: `flatpak override --show` read `shared=!network`):

```
$ flatpak run ai.storyteller.photocraft//test            # first terminal: one window
$ ls -l /run/user/1000/app/ai.storyteller.photocraft/instance.sock
srw------- 1 diego diego 0 Oct 19 17:58 /run/user/1000/app/ai.storyteller.photocraft/instance.sock
$ flatpak run ai.storyteller.photocraft//test ~/Pictures/photocraft-test/blue.png   # second terminal
INFO  [main] photocraft: handed 1 file(s) to the running PhotoCraft
exit=0 after 0.19 s
$ wmctrl -l | grep PhotoCraft
0x09e00004  0 diego-Nitro-ANV15-51 blue.png — PhotoCraft      # still one window, the file is a tab
```

Closing the window removes `instance.sock` within a second and leaves no `photocraft` process; a third `flatpak run` becomes a new primary with a fresh socket, and closing it removes that one too.

## How it was tested

- New tests in `single_instance.rs`: `a_sandboxed_second_launch_hands_its_paths_over_a_unix_socket` (socket mode 0600, `instance.json` carries `socket` and no `port`, the second launch is forwarded, a wrong token is refused, shutdown removes the socket), `a_crashed_primary_s_socket_file_does_not_block_the_next_one`, and `the_socket_transport_needs_a_flatpak_id_and_a_runtime_directory`. The existing loopback tests are unchanged apart from reading the endpoint type.
- `cargo test -p photocraft --bin photocraft single_instance --locked` (14 tests), `cargo clippy -p photocraft --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.
- End to end with the built binary and `FLATPAK_ID`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` set as the sandbox sets them: see Evidence.

## Risk and rollback

Low: the socket transport is taken only when `FLATPAK_ID` is set, and a bind failure there falls through to the standalone launch exactly as before. Revert the single commit to roll back.

* **New Features**
  * Flatpak launches now use a local Unix socket for single-instance handoff. Windows and non-Flatpak Linux continue to use loopback TCP.
  * Socket access is restricted to the owning user. Stale socket files are replaced, and the active socket is removed when the primary app instance shuts down. Existing handoff validation and request limits remain in place.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated the development guide to explain Flatpak’s single-instance communication and socket location.

included.head: a35e60f33591c8431d4f3e2b5a892d777d85de2d
included.title: Show every blend mode in the open dropdown list (#7261)
included.body:
Closes #7261.

The blend modes weren't missing. Every dropdown list (`widgets::dropdown_with` and `dropdown_with_tooltips`) was capped at 420 pt, which is 14 rows. In the Layers panel the list stopped at Overlay. Soft Light through Luminosity sat behind a thin scroll bar that's easy to miss.

### Change

- **List height:** the list grows to the visible window like a context menu, reusing `menu_scroll` (`min_scrolled_height`, which works around egui sizing a just-opened popup at 400 pt). It scrolls only when the window is too short.
- **List position:** the list opens under its box, or above it if only that fits. Otherwise it opens under the box and egui moves it up to fit the window.
- **Why not ComboBox:** `egui::ComboBox` has no setting for where the list opens. With the height lifted, egui put the list beside the box, the only place it fit, and moved it to the other side when a longer mode (Linear Dodge (Add)) widened the box, away from the pointer.
- **New `combo` helper:** it draws ComboBox's box itself (same look, same ids, same `ComboBox` accessibility info) and opens the list with `egui::Popup`. Because the ids match, `ComboBox::is_open`, `PressCombo` (press-drag-release) and the arrow keys keep working.

### Tests

- New: `the_open_blend_list_shows_every_mode`. With the list open, Normal through Luminosity are all painted and unclipped. The list stays in the box's column, and doesn't move as the box widens to Linear Dodge (Add). It fails without the fix: Soft Light is never painted.

included.title: Studio: the floating Properties card has the Adjustments tab (#7265)
included.body:
Fixes #7265.

## What and why

Under the Studio-layout themes, Window › Adjustments (and the rail's Properties button) showed the floating **Properties** card with the document's properties. The Adjustments grid could not be reached.

The menu side already works: `view_cmds::invoke` runs before the `panel_alias` fallback, and `panel_tab` maps `window.panel.adjustments` to `("properties", 1)`, so the command shows Properties and selects tab 1 (`window_panels_select_dock_tabs` covers this). The Pro dock draws tab 1 as `adjustments_grid` (`dock_body`). Studio doesn't dock Properties, though. `properties_window` floats it as a card that only ever called `properties_body` and ignored `dock_tabs.properties`.

- The card's title becomes the group's pill tab strip (`tab_strip::pill_tabs`, as Studio's docked cards use), **Properties | Adjustments**. Tab 1 draws `adjustments_grid`. The strip follows and sets `dock_tabs.properties`, so the menu, its checkmark and the Pro dock agree with the card. Picking an adjustment switches back to Properties, as in the dock.
- It uses `dock.visible_tabs`, so a tab closed in the dock stays closed on the card. Its context menu works too: Close hides one tab (and the card with the last), and Close Tab Group hides the card. That close logic moved from the dock's `Action::CloseTab` into `dock::close_tab`, so both use the same code.
- The title bar still drags the card. It is registered before the tabs (as in `widgets::card_ex`), so the tabs keep their clicks.

included.title: Refuse strict ATN export of Select and Mask with brush strokes
included.body:
Fixes #7539

## Cause
The `select.refineEdge` ATN mapping (`REFINE_EDGE`) has no field for `refineStrokes`, and `fields_to` only walks the fields it declares and silently ignores any others. So a step with Refine Edge Brush strokes was exported as a plain Select and Mask. Strict export reported no error and no skipped step, and playback after reimport gave a different selection.

## Fix
Select and Mask now exports through a dedicated `refine_edge_to` that returns no Photoshop equivalent when `refineStrokes` is non-empty. Strict export now returns an error for such a step, and `skipUnsupported` export lists it in `Skipped`. Steps with no strokes, an empty array or null still round-trip as before, and the existing pixel-target check is kept.

## Verified
- Regression test `atn_cmds::tests::refine_edge_with_brush_strokes_is_not_exported_without_them`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib refine_edge_with_brush_strokes_is_not_exported_without_them`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
No Photoshop descriptor encoding for Refine Edge Brush strokes is added, because no verified encoding exists. The import mapping and the other Select and Mask fields are unchanged.

included.head: 1c29f87ed9eebf6993821bdba7ec15e0beb926da
included.title: feat(engine): parameter schema types and display-string renderer
included.body:
## What

Adds `crates/engine/src/param_schema.rs`: a typed description of a Command's input parameters.

- `Param { key, kind, optional, unit, default }` with a `Kind` enum covering the shapes the registry's `params` strings express today — bounded ranges (int/float), bool, text, choice lists, color, JSON, nested objects/arrays to the depth a doc describes, `Alt` unions, and a verbatim `Free` word for unbounded type words (`id`, `index`).
- `Unit` as a field (only the four that occur as value types: `px`, `pt`, `%`, `deg`) and `Default` incl. `Symbol` for UI-resolved defaults (`=foreground`, `=bottom selected`) the engine must not interpret.
- `UNIVERSAL` — one canonical list of keys every command accepts (`coalesce`, `target`, `layer`, `channel`), instead of today's three disagreeing hand-maintained versions of it.
- A renderer producing the agent/human Display string in the documented `{"radius":0.1..1000=1}` format (`docs/control-protocol.md`) **from** the schema, so the published string can be derived from one description instead of maintained beside it.

Pure addition: nothing reads the module yet, no dispatch/UI/file behavior changes, `std`-only, engine-side (L5), wasm-clean.

## Why

Motivated by #7596 (unknown parameter keys silently succeed), #7597 (parameter ranges kept in three hand-synced copies that demonstrably drift) and #7598 (the two hand-written parsers of the params string silently corrupt valid grammar — e.g. `0.5..5000 px?` loses its maximum). All three reduce to the same root: a command's parameter description is prose, re-parsed differently by each reader. This PR makes that description data, with the rendering contract pinned by tests; nothing else changes.

## Tests

8 golden tests over the documented grammar: ranges with defaults (int/float, negative bounds), choice lists with/without defaults, bool defaults, units and optional markers (`"size":0.5..5000 px?`), nested objects (`{"in":0..255,…}`), arrays, `Alt` unions (`"pixels"|"mask"|{"channel":i}`), symbolic defaults, the open-ended marker, prose-notes pass-through, and universal-key merge/dedup.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib` — 1775 passed (incl. the 8 new)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm` — green

No commands, shortcuts, menus or file handling touched; parity and scorecard unaffected.

* **New Features**
  * Added a typed way to describe command parameters, including supported values, ranges, defaults, units, and optional fields.
  * Parameter schemas can describe nested objects and arrays, include notes, and render in a documented format.

included.head: dbdd8ff66e6cb5bf8d97e7f1a8d7fbc03418c204
included.title: Toolbar: colour chips stay centred when the tools scroll (#7316)
included.body:
Closes #7316.

In a window too short for the tools, the toolbar's tool column scrolls. egui then widens the UI by the scroll bar's width, and the colour chips, which were centred in `ui.available_width()`, moved right with it. Default Colors and Switch Colors moved with them. The shift is about 3 px in the Studio and Pro themes, and more with Classic's wider solid bar. That matches the screenshots in the issue: the lighter strip at the right of the tool column is the scroll bar.

### Fix

`color_chips` is now centred in the tool column's width as it was before the tools' `ScrollArea` (`full.width()`, captured above it). The chips therefore sit under the tools whether or not the column scrolls. The Pro themes had the same shift in a short enough window; the reporter's window was just tall enough to hide it.

### Tests

- `color_chips_stay_centred_when_the_tools_scroll`: for every theme, with one and two columns, at 1x and 2x, the chips paint at the same x in a 420 pt window (the tools scroll) as in a 1400 pt one. It runs a few frames, since the scroll bar only appears once the overflow has been measured. It fails without the fix (`[18.0, 28.0]` vs `[15.0, 25.0]`).
- `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, the ui-egui suite, `cargo xtask wasm` and `cargo xtask layers` pass.

### Verified in the app

On macOS 27, Studio theme, in a 552 pt tall window where the tools scroll, measured against the tool buttons' centre of 25.0 pt:

- **Before:** white chip and swap arrows centred at 27.75 pt.
- **After:** 24.5 pt and 24.75 pt.

Classic looks right too. For reference, Photoshop 2025 centres its swatches under the tool icons in the same way.

included.title: Refuse .atn export of crops with output size or resolution
included.body:
Fixes #7191

## Cause
`crop_to` in the `.atn` mapper wrote only the crop rectangle, angle and Delete Cropped Pixels. It ignored `targetWidth`, `targetHeight`, `resolution` and `resample` and still reported success. Strict export accepted the step, and the reloaded action cropped only to the rectangle, keeping the document's old size and resolution.

## Fix
`crop_to` now returns no descriptor when a non-null `targetWidth`, `targetHeight` or `resolution` is present. Strict export now rejects such a step, and opt-in skipping lists it in `skipped`. Plain rectangle crops export unchanged.

## Verified

## Not changed
Crops are still exported without Photoshop descriptor fields for output size and resolution, because the correct field names are not confirmed. `crop_from` (import) is unchanged. A crop with only `resample` still exports, because without a target size `resample` does not affect the result.

included.head: cf8fccf2f395bdae0761e636da676b25dbf3710d
included.title: fix(atn): refuse strict export of canvas-bound selection modifies and placed pattern buckets
included.body:
Fixes #7540, fixes #7541, fixes #7542, fixes #7543, fixes #7544, fixes #7545, fixes #7546.

Strict `.atn` export wrote these steps without an option their descriptors have no field for, so they replayed differently. As the tickets allow, they're now refused rather than changed: strict export fails with the step named, and an export with `skipUnsupported` lists it as skipped. Nothing about Photoshop's descriptor keys is assumed.

- **Feather, Contract, Smooth, and Expand (which has the same flag):** `applyAtCanvasBounds: true` changes how the selection is padded at the canvas edge, but the events carry only the radius (#7540, #7541, #7542). The event table gains an `uncarried:` list of such flags per event, which keeps it general for the next one.
- **Paint Bucket with `contents: "pattern"`:** Fill's `Pttn` names no pattern and has no placement, so the following replayed with the current pattern at its defaults (#7543, #7544, #7545, #7546). They're now refused:
  - an explicit `pattern`;
  - a `scale` other than 100;
  - an `angle` other than 0;
  - a `phase` other than `[0, 0]`.

Defaults still export (`applyAtCanvasBounds: false`, a pattern bucket with no pattern, scale 100, angle 0 and phase `[0, 0]`), and the modify steps round-trip as `{"radius"}`.

## Test

`canvas_bound_modify_and_placed_pattern_bucket_refuse_strict_export`:
- each of the four modify events with `applyAtCanvasBounds: true` fails strict export; with `false` it exports and imports as `{"radius": 2}`.
- a pattern bucket with a pattern, scale, angle or phase fails strict export; with none of them, or all at their defaults, it exports.

included.head: 6a24011ab80164f3b531c40baf6a7c998f72376b
included.title: fix(atn): keep a Transform Selection's interpolation; refuse what the transform descriptor can't carry
included.body:
Fixes #7515, fixes #7516, fixes #7517, fixes #7518, fixes #7519.

Two problems in the Free Transform / Transform Selection `.atn` mapping.

- **#7515, import:** the export writes a Transform Selection's interpolation (`Intr`), but the importer read it only for a layer transform, so a selection replayed with the default resampler. It's now read for both targets.
- **#7516–#7519, export:** the descriptor scales and rotates about the centre (`FTcs` average), with no skew and no warp. The importer already refuses `Skew` and `Usng`. A step with another reference point, a skew or a warp exported as a plain scale and replayed differently. Such steps are now refused, as other transforms the descriptor can't hold already are: strict export fails and a partial export skips the step. This applies to Transform Selection and Free Transform, which share the descriptor.
  - Refused: a `reference` other than `"center"` (named or `[x, y]`), a non-zero `skewX` or `skewY`, or a `warp` / `style` / `mesh` / `grid`.
  - Also refused: `corners`, Transform Selection's alias for `quad`, which slipped past the existing `quad` check.
  - Defaults (`"reference": "center"`, zero skew) still export.

I didn't map other reference points to Photoshop's `QCSt` values, because which value means which point can't be checked offline. Mapping them later would only need the import and export pair and a round-trip test.

## Test

`transform_selection_keeps_its_interpolation_and_refuses_what_it_cannot_carry`:
- a Transform Selection with `"interpolation": "nearest"` round-trips unchanged; on `main` the interpolation is lost.
- for both commands, a named or point reference, each skew, a warp and `corners` all fail strict export, and the defaults still export.

## Evidence

`897e1d74` on `main`, Windows x86_64 (rustc 1.99.0): engine lib and integration tests 1,997 passed, 0 failed; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -D warnings` pass.

included.head: b8f323a7c4f27e301c40bded2c208b25ad6168b3
included.title: fix(atn): refuse strict export of options the descriptors can't carry
included.body:
Fixes #7502, fixes #7512, fixes #7513, fixes #7514, fixes #7503, fixes #7506, fixes #7507, fixes #7196, fixes #7236, fixes #7246, fixes #7287.

Strict `.atn` export succeeded on these steps but wrote descriptors that can't carry one of their options, so the imported step replayed differently. The tickets ask for the option to be kept, or for strict conversion to be refused. Neither the exporter nor the importer maps these options today. Writing them would mean inventing Photoshop descriptor keys that can't be checked offline, so this change refuses them. Strict export now fails with the step named, as for any step without a Photoshop equivalent, and an export with `skipUnsupported` lists it as skipped. Steps without those options export exactly as before.

| Command | Refused when | Tickets |
|---|---|---|
| `layer.new.layer` | `clipToPrevious`, a `color` label, `fillNeutral`, or `position: "below"` (non-default values) | #7502, #7512, #7513, #7514 |
| `file.new` | `background` is `black` or a hex colour, or `backgroundColor` is given (`Fl  ` holds only white, transparent or Photoshop's own background colour) | #7503 |
| `select.loadSelection` | `invert`, or `operation` other than `new` | #7506 |
| `layer.newFillLayer.solidColor` | a `color` the opaque RGB descriptor can't hold (alpha, or unparseable) instead of silently exporting no colour | #7507 |
| `layer.setProps` (and its rename and label twins) | any key other than `layer`, `name`, `opacity`, `fill`, `blend`, `visible`, `color` (`locked`, `locks`, `clipped`, `channels`, an explicit `layers` list) | #7196, #7246 |
| `layer.groupLayers` | an explicit `layer` (the descriptor always groups the selection) | #7236 |
| Any mapped 32-bit integer field (e.g. Add Noise `seed` → `FlRs`) | a value outside `i32`, which was clamped to `i32::MAX`/`MIN` (seeds above 2147483647 replayed as 2147483647) | #7287 |

Mapping any of these options properly later only needs the matching import and export keys, and a test showing the round trip.

- `new_layer_options_the_descriptor_cannot_carry_refuse_strict_export`: each New Layer option fails strict export and is skipped by a partial one. included.head: d08a16507c1a02d82f77263412a274f6f0d3e87a
included.title: Actions: stop when a Save step's document is closed by a Save Document script (#7367)
included.body:
Fixes storytold/photocraft#7367

## Root cause

An imported Photoshop action step **Close** with **Save: Yes** plays as two steps: `file.save {}` then `file.close {}`. Neither step names a document, so each one acts on whichever document is active when it runs. If a Save Document script event (`saveDocument` hook) closes document A during the save, the next step, `file.close {}`, closes whatever document is active then. In the issue's steps that is the unrelated dirty document B, so its unsaved changes are lost.

## Fix

- `crates/engine/src/actions_cmds.rs`: new helper `save_target_closed(session, id, target)`. For a played save step (`file.save`, `file.saveAs`, `file.saveACopy`), it reports a failure when the document that was active when the step started is no longer open.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/actions.rs`: shell playback notes the active document before each step. After a save step, it calls the helper. If the saved document is gone, playback stops at that step with a clear error ("the document was closed during the save (by a Save Document script event); playback stopped so later steps don't act on another document"), so no later step runs on B.

The check sits in `ui-egui` because the desktop shell runs the playback loop that performs saves.

Behaviour change: any action whose save step is followed by more steps now stops if a Save Document script event closes the saved document. Before, those later steps silently ran on another document.

## Testing

- New test `actions::tests::save_hook_closing_the_target_stops_an_imported_close_with_save`. It imports a real one-step `.atn` with Close / Save: Yes, then plays it with three Save Document hooks: none, activate B, and close. Each time it checks that A is saved once and closed, and that B stays open with its unsaved `KeepB` layer. For the closing hook, it also checks that playback fails at step 0 (`file.save`) with the new error.
- Locally only `rustfmt` on the two changed files. Nothing was compiled or run on this machine.
- **CI is running.** Fork run: https://github.com/Higgs32584/photocraft/actions/runs/39172120309 (in progress when this PR was opened). This PR's own checks will run too. I'll push normal fix commits if anything fails.

## Not verified

- The build and the new test, which wait on CI.
- Photoshop's own behaviour for this case.
- Manual playback in the desktop app.

included.title: Refuse strict .atn export of a mask/channel-targeted Free Transform
included.body:
Fixes #7195

## Cause
`transform_to` always built a layer reference for `edit.transform` and never looked at `target`. A transform recorded against an unlinked mask, an alpha channel or the Quick Mask therefore exported without error, and when the .atn was imported and played back it transformed the layer's colour pixels instead.

## Fix
`transform_to` now returns no descriptor for `edit.transform` when it has an explicit target other than pixels. Photoshop's transform descriptor has no field for such a target, so strict export now refuses the step, and non-strict export lists it as skipped. That matches how the exporter already handles filters with a mask target.

## Verified

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Transforms with no target or a pixels target still export and re-import exactly as before. Quad, matrix and rect forms are still rejected, and `select.transformSelection` is unchanged. Explicit Quick Mask targets are also refused now, because whether they replay correctly depends on Quick Mask being on at playback time. No mask or channel target encoding was added to the descriptor.

included.title: Record actions.conditional as one step with its predicate
included.body:
Fixes #7238

## Cause
`replayable` let only `actions.play` through among `actions.*` ids, so the journaled `actions.conditional` entry was never recorded. When no branch ran, nothing went into the action. When a branch ran, only the nested `actions.play` of that branch was recorded and the predicate was lost (#7198).

## Fix
`replayable` now also accepts `actions.conditional`. `Session::execute` already pauses recording during a replayable command and drops the nested journal entries it produces, so the Conditional is recorded as one step with its original params, and playback evaluates the predicate again on the current document.

included.head: 86b4c67adf6dcf26836803c8e1b2fc0c957ff5e3
included.title: Preserve saved PCraft previews when manifest replacement fails
included.body:
Saving an existing directory `.pcraft` without replacement previews deletes its old thumbnail and composite before publishing the new manifest. If manifest replacement fails, the saved manifest still references files that have already been deleted.

Commit the manifest first, then remove omitted previews as best-effort housekeeping, matching unreferenced-object cleanup. A locked leftover is retried on a later save; it cannot turn an already committed save into a reported failure. Existing path validation and directory-handle protections remain in place.

Fixes #7549. This does not fix replacement previews in #7548.

Validation (standard public-fork cloud runners; no local builds):
- [Windows baseline and fixed regression](https://github.com/jonathanwxh-cell/photocraft/actions/runs/39168226606/job/117795737619): unchanged main fails because `thumb.png` disappears after a blocked manifest commit. The fix preserves the old manifest, both previews and reopened document across 8/16/32-bit depths. Full format tests and strict Clippy pass.
- [Final-source checks](https://github.com/jonathanwxh-cell/photocraft/actions/runs/39168809458): Windows/Linux format tests and strict Clippy, formatting, dependency layering and WASM. The Unix permission regression now verifies successful commit with a locked stale preview, followed by cleanup on the next save.
- [Corpus job](https://github.com/jonathanwxh-cell/photocraft/actions/runs/39168226606/job/117795737549) passed on the same production source; the only subsequent source-branch change updates the Unix test expectation. The earlier Linux job failed on that old expectation, which the final run replaces.

The failure reproduction uses a real Windows handle denying delete-sharing, not a simulated power loss. Temporary verification workflows are excluded from this PR.

Prepared for @jonathanwxh-cell (credit jonathnwxh) with OpenAI Codex assistance.

included.head: 2a9a35f038408cd3f57c06c755db8aedee040ea7
included.title: Menu bar: Alt held through a shortcut no longer takes the keyboard, so Enter reaches the dialog (#7481)
included.body:
Fixes #7481

### Problem
After a shortcut that includes Alt (Ctrl+Alt+I for Image Size, or a custom Ctrl+Alt+E for Expand), releasing Alt put the keyboard on the menu bar with File lit, as a lone Alt tap does. The dialog the shortcut opened then didn't get Enter: Enter opened the File menu instead of confirming.

`menu_keys::Keys::keys` tells a lone Alt tap from Alt used in a chord: any key, text or click while Alt is held cancels the tap. It read the frame's `InputState::events`. The shortcuts run before the menu bar each frame and consume their key from those events (`consume_key`). So the bar never saw the I of Ctrl+Alt+I, and the Alt release counted as a tap.

### Solution
`crates/ui-egui/src/menu_keys.rs`: the tap is now judged on `InputState::raw.events`, every event the frame received, including keys another handler consumed. Which mnemonic or menu key the bar acts on still comes from the unconsumed `events`, so it still won't act on a key a shortcut already took.

A lone Alt tap still puts the keyboard on the bar, and Alt+letter still opens that menu.

### Tests
`menu_keys::harness_tests::alt_held_through_a_shortcut_does_not_put_the_keyboard_on_the_bar` drives the whole app (shortcuts, dialogs and the menu bar), not only the bar. It fails before this change, where the bar took the keyboard.
- Alt down, then Ctrl+Alt+I, then Alt up: Image Size is open and the bar did not take the keyboard.
- Enter then confirms Image Size and opens no menu.
- A lone Alt tap still focuses the bar.

```
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib menu_keys    # 11 passed; the new test fails without the fix
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib shortcut     # 99 passed
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib menu_nav     # 23 passed
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib alt_click    # 23 passed
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib menus        # 52 passed
cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt --all -- --check                         # clean
```

Checked in the running app on Windows with real key events (`keybd_event`: Ctrl down, Alt down, I down/up, Alt up, Ctrl up): Image Size opens, the menu bar stays unfocused, and Enter confirms the dialog. (That before-and-after is the whole-app test above; my real-input run was on the fixed build only.)

#7500 (Alt+F as a chord) is not part of this: with an English UI it opens File for me with real input, so I asked the reporter for their language and layout there.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved Alt-key handling so shortcuts that include Alt no longer incorrectly open the menu when Alt is released.
  * Preserved standalone Alt taps as a way to focus the menu bar.

included.head: e371bc34e389cafe5c4debc71c246909e4ef0db4
included.title: Refuse strict .atn export of Apply Image with a blending mask
included.body:
Fixes #7247

## Cause
`apply_image_to` turned `image.applyImage` into an `AppI` descriptor without looking at the optional blending mask (`mask` or flat `maskChannel`), so the mask was silently dropped. Because the export still succeeded, the converted step applied to the whole layer instead of only the masked area.

## Fix
`apply_image_to` now returns no descriptor when an effective blending mask is set (a mask channel other than none or empty). Strict export now fails for these steps, and lenient export reports them as skipped instead of writing a wider edit. Unmasked forms, and masks with channel `none`, export as before.

## Verified
- Regression test `apply_image_with_blending_mask_is_not_exported_without_its_mask`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib apply_image_with_blending_mask_is_not_exported_without_its_mask`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
No `.atn` descriptor mapping for the blending mask was added, so masked Apply Image steps are refused rather than converted. The normalization of flat source fields (#7197) and the destination layer-mask target (#6780) are not changed.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Apply Image steps with an active blending-mask channel are now reported as unsupported during export instead of being exported without that setting. Strict exports fail for these steps, while exports configured to skip unsupported steps report them as skipped.
  * Apply Image steps with no blending mask, or with the mask set to “none,” continue to export and import without a mask setting. Their source and blending parameters are retained.

included.head: 824f93a69fe4800599db859a54c95702e32e465c
included.title: fix(atn): a preset-only Photo Filter step exports its resolved colour (#7235)
included.body:
Fixes #7235 (denstu473): ".atn export loses Photo Filter preset and replays a different filter color."

## Root cause, as far as the code shows it

A recorded step is stored as raw command params, and `image.adjustments.photoFilter` accepts preset-only params (`{"filter": "cooling80", "density": 60}` — no `color` key; `crates/engine/src/adjust_params.rs` resolves the preset through `PHOTO_FILTERS` at run time). The `.atn` exporter built its descriptor straight from those params (`adj_fields!("PhtF", …, F("Clr ", "color", …))`), so a preset-only step exported **with no `Clr ` at all**: the export succeeded (a valid descriptor), the preset was gone, and re-imported playback fell back to the default warming filter — that is the issue's "accepted and lose their preset; imported playback uses the default warming filter".

The honest caveat the fix carries: Photoshop's own descriptor keeps no preset key for Photo Filter. That is what this repository's `phfl` notes conclude from the Photoshop CS2 oracle files (#3777/#4940, `crates/io/src/adjust_map.rs`: "the Yellow filter holds (24191, 25002, 3827) … Warming Filter (85) holds (15548, 12029, 0)"), and it is what the existing `.atn` event table shows (colour, density, preserve-luminosity, nothing else). So "keep the preset" can only mean "export the resolved colour", which keeps the output identical.

## What

`crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs`, the `PhtF` entry of `ADJUSTMENTS`:

- a preset-only step now exports its resolved colour (`preset_color` looks the id up in the same `adjust_params::PHOTO_FILTERS` table the command itself uses, so the export matches what running the step in PhotoCraft produces);
- an explicit `color` keeps precedence over `filter`, exactly like running the command;
- an unknown preset id keeps the previous export (no colour) — export still never rejects a step;
- density stays implicit when the step had none (playback then applies the same default both for the original preset-only step and for the re-imported one).

Import is unchanged: neither direction can recover a preset name, and none is invented.

## Verification

Run locally on Windows 11 (`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) against current `main` (`8d2e615a`):

- new `photo_filter_preset_only_step_keeps_its_resolved_color` — a real `write`→`read` byte round trip through `atn::write` and the import table, following the bucket test from #7199: preset-only step → `#006dff` (Cooling 80 from the shared table), `#ea1a1a` for `red`, explicit colour wins, unknown id keeps the old shape;
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib` — **1732 passed, 0 failed, 13 ignored**;
- `cargo fmt --check -p photocraft-engine` — clean;
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.

Not verified locally:

- I do not have Photoshop, so the descriptor-level behaviour on a Photoshop-authored preset-only Photo Filter action is not rerun here; the colour-only form is cited from this repository's oracle-based notes (see above) and is not my claim.
- The recorded-through-the-UI path is covered indirectly: the same params shape (`{"filter": …}`) is what `from_params` accepts, and the test drives the exporter with it directly.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Photo Filter adjustment exports now correctly resolve recognized preset IDs to their corresponding RGB colors when no explicit color is provided.
  - Explicit colors continue to take precedence over presets.
  - Unknown preset IDs leave the color unset, preserving previous behavior.
  - Photo Filter settings now maintain consistent field handling during import and export.

included.head: ccdf082c62da26ffea52cbea51e03ebc3195c877
included.title: Content-Aware Fill workspace: an erased sampling area previews as an error, and a failed OK keeps it open (#7384)
included.body:
Fixes #7384

Follow-up to the review of #6670 (Content-Aware Fill with nothing to sample, #6532), which suggested it as a separate change.

### Problem
In the Content-Aware Fill workspace (#2376):
- **Black preview.** When the sampling area had no pixels outside the fill area (the Sampling Brush erased it all under Auto or Rectangular), the live preview showed the black fill such an area produces. It gave no hint why.
- **OK lost the work.** OK closed the workspace even when the fill failed. The error only reached the status bar, and the sampling strokes and fill edits were lost. With #6670, an empty sampling area is one such failure (the command refuses it); a locked layer is another, already today. The control channel's `commit` behaved the same way.

### Solution
`crates/ui-egui/src/caf_ui.rs`:
- **Preview.** `compute_preview` returns "nothing to sample from: the sampling area has no pixels outside the fill area" when the plan's `source` is empty, the same words the engine's refusal in #6670 uses. The panel already shows preview errors in place of the image, so the user sees what is wrong instead of a black fill. The check is in the preview, not in `content_aware_plan_with`; an empty Custom area with nothing painted yet already fails earlier, in the plan, with "custom sampling needs `area`…".
- **OK.** OK closes only when the fill ran. On an error the workspace stays open, and the error goes to the panel (`report`, next to the controls) as well as the status bar, so the areas can be fixed and OK pressed again. Apply's errors go through the same `report`.
- **Control channel.** `commit` keeps the workspace open on an error too, and still returns the error.
- **Undo / Redo.** Undoing or redoing a sampling stroke clears that panel error, as a new stroke does. The other steps already clear it through `rebase`. Otherwise the stale error would stay drawn over the recovered preview.

**Merge after #6670.** The preview check is local, and a failed OK keeps the workspace open whatever the error. But until #6670 makes the engine refuse an empty sampling area, OK would still fill black there while the preview already says "nothing to sample from". This should land after #6670; together they catch it in both places.

### Tests
`caf_ui::tests` (both fail before this change):
- `an_erased_sampling_area_previews_as_an_error`:
  - Rectangular, then a subtracting stroke wider than the window: 0 sampled pixels, and the preview error is "nothing to sample from";
  - undo brings the preview back.
- `a_failed_ok_keeps_the_workspace_open`:
  - with the layer's pixels locked, OK (the button's `commit`) leaves the workspace open, with the error in its panel and the status bar, and so does the control channel's `commit`;
  - unlocked, OK fills and closes.
- `undo_and_redo_of_a_stroke_clear_a_failed_oks_error`: after a failed OK, Undo of the sampling stroke clears the panel error; after another failed OK, Redo clears it too.

```
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib caf_ui    # 16 passed; the three new tests fail without the fix
cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt --all -- --check                       # clean
```


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Failed fill attempts now keep the workspace open and display the error in the panel and status bar, allowing you to correct the issue and try again.
  * Previews with no source pixels now show an error instead of a black fill.
  * Undoing or redoing a sampling stroke clears a previously reported workspace error, so the error display reflects the current state.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

included.head: afc817d1fae968465bff78a557d0806c499fd292
included.title: test(engine): make the define-brush mask allocation fail on its own (fail-after-one) (#212)
included.body:
Follow-up to #5469, addressing @FredApps' non-blocking testing nit from the merged review: "fail_next_for_test currently fails the **first** buffer allocation, so this command regression does not independently exercise failure of the second mask allocation. A fail-after-one allocation test would protect that path too." The same re-review noted "The assertions do not directly compare document pixels"; the new test does. No runtime code change: every added line is `#[cfg(test)]` or inside test files, so non-test builds compile byte-identically to current `main`.

## What

1. `crates/engine/src/allocation.rs` — a second test-only thread-local flag with the helper `fail_after_for_test(skip)`: the failpoint trips only on the allocation/checkpoint after `skip` clean attempts, so a test can make a *later* fallible call fail, not just the first. `fail_next_for_test` keeps its exact one-shot semantics (`skip = 0` is equivalent); `capacity` and `checkpoint` now consult one shared `cfg(test)` helper (`failpoint_hits`) instead of each consuming the boolean. New unit test `fail_after_trips_only_on_the_counted_attempt` pins the counting: two clean attempts, the third fails with the same `not enough memory` error, the flag is then consumed.

2. `crates/engine/src/brush_cmds/tests.rs` — new regression `define_brush_from_selection_survives_failure_of_the_second_allocation`: `fail_after_for_test(1)` counts the tip buffer (`allocation::filled`) as the one clean attempt and fails the selection-mask read (`allocation::read_region`) instead. The test asserts the graceful error text ("not enough memory for defining a brush from the selection"), and that the current brush, the preset list, the history length and — now directly compared — the document pixels themselves are unchanged. The existing one-shot regression `define_brush_from_selection_survives_allocation_failure` (unchanged) keeps covering the first buffer.

## Verification

Run locally on Windows 11 (`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) against current `main` (`8d2e615a`):

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib` — **1731 passed, 0 failed, 13 ignored** (includes both new tests, the pre-existing one-shot regression and the two `define` happy-path tests);
- `cargo fmt --check -p photocraft-engine` — clean;
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.

Not run locally:

- `cargo xtask wasm`: not run. All engine additions are `#[cfg(test)]`, so the wasm32 code path is unchanged from `8d2e615a`; the `wasm32-check` CI job is the gate for that target.
- The counted failpoint is used to cover the reviewer-noted define-brush mask path only; other multi-buffer commands (copy/paste, transform, channel operations) still have their existing one-shot regressions and were not touched.
