included.head: 55dbbdf0604d8cff32a6f511d1f33edd61c54dcb
included.title: fix(atn): reject numeric layer references in .atn export (#7248)
included.body:
Resolves #7248.

### Problem
In `crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs`, `layer_ref(p: &Value)` converted any layer reference that was not a string (`Value::String(n)`) into the target layer reference (`target_ref("Lyr ")`).
When an action step explicitly specified an unselected layer by its numeric ID (e.g. `layer: 42`), exporting to `.atn` silently fell back to targeting the currently selected layer(s). Running such an action in Photoshop would modify/delete the wrong layer(s) instead of failing or skipping.

### Fix
- Updated `layer_ref(p: &Value) -> Option<D>` to return `Some(target_ref("Lyr "))` only when `layer` is missing or null, `Some(name_ref("Lyr ", n))` when `layer` is a string, and `None` when given explicit numeric layer references (or any other unsupported non-string representation).
- Propagated `Option<D>` via `layer_ref(p)?` to all callers (`make_to`, `set_to`, `transform_to`, `delete_to`, `visibility_to`, `move_to`, `duplicate_to`).
- In strict export (`skipUnsupported: false`), commands with numeric layer references fail gracefully. With `skipUnsupported: true`, such steps are cleanly skipped and recorded in `skipped`.

### Verification
- Added regression test `numeric_layer_references_refuse_silent_fallback_to_current_selection` in `crates/engine/src/atn_cmds/tests.rs` covering named references, omitted/target references, explicit numeric references across multiple command types (`layer.delete`, `layer.duplicate`, `layer.translate`), and `skipUnsupported: true`.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib atn_cmds` passed (12 of 12 tests green).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Action recording now preserves active-layer targets without unintentionally storing the active layer’s numeric ID.
  * Export no longer silently treats invalid numeric layer targets as the active layer; these steps fail conversion instead.
  * Errors for unsupported steps identify the numeric layer target, and the affected step can be skipped when unsupported steps are configured to be skipped.
  * Named layer targets and omitted layer targets continue to work. Recorded commands targeting the active layer also remain supported.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

included.head: 781a842d890ee13a8ae79ee5a7e258f69b941ee6
included.title: test(io): SVG text-transform test can't pass without a font (#4806)
included.body:
Follow-up to #5334, addressing @tanish2k09's review note there: `transformed_text_lands_where_resvg_draws_it` returned early, and passed without checking anything, when the import found no font.

## Why naming a bundled font isn't enough

- `photocraft_text::CRAFT_FONTS` is empty unless the build sets `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` (`crates/text/build.rs`).
- SVG import doesn't load the bundled UI fonts (`fonts::BUNDLED`).

So with the system fonts hidden, an SVG naming `"Inter, …"` still imports no text. The merged test then passed in 0.00 s.

## Changes (test-only)

- The test moves into the `src/svg.rs` unit tests, so it can call `parse_with` (the same hook the existing `no_fonts()` test uses) with a font database holding only the bundled Inter Regular, which is always compiled in.
  - The resvg reference is rendered from the same parse, so both sides use the same face.
- The early return is gone: an empty import now fails, and the test expects exactly one text layer.
- The old copy in `tests/svg.rs` is removed.
- `text_becomes_outline_shapes_or_warns_without_a_font` stays either/or on purpose, because it exercises the real font lookup, where "no font, so a warning" is the correct behaviour.

## Tested

To hide the system fonts I used a private mount namespace with tmpfs over `/usr/share/fonts` and `/usr/local/share/fonts` (`fc-list` reported 0 fonts).

- **With the #5334 fix reverted:** the test fails, both with system fonts present and with them hidden.
- **With the fix:** it passes, including with system fonts hidden.
- **Unmodified `main`, fonts hidden:** the old test "passes" in 0.00 s.
- **All passed:**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`;
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked --features heif -- -D warnings`;
  - `cargo test -p photocraft-io`: 604 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored (the existing ones that need external files);
  - `cargo xtask layers`.

**Not run:**
- `cargo xtask wasm`: only `#[cfg(test)]` code changed.
- The corpus tests: the downloads were blocked in my environment.
- The FreeBSD job: I couldn't check which fonts that VM has, because its setup lives in the shared `craft-common-actions` workflow. On Linux and Windows CI the old test most likely did run, since those images ship DejaVu or Arial. The point of this change is that the test no longer depends on the machine's fonts.

---

_AI assistance: written with Claude Code; the commit carries a `Co-Authored-By` trailer._

included.head: 121002e1b9891e41c3a6d11ae5c8a22a0ac3c48d
included.title: fix(atn): reject off-center radial blur in .atn export (#7234)
included.body:
Fixes #7234

### Problem
PhotoCraft supports off-center Radial Blur (`centerX`/`centerY`), but the ATN event table previously used the generic `ev!` mapping for `RdlB` with `amount`, `method`, and `quality` only. When exporting an action containing Radial Blur with a custom center, the center coordinates were silently dropped. On replay, the blur reverted to the default center (0.5, 0.5), changing pixel output without warning the user or rejecting the unrepresentable step.

### Solution
- Defined custom `radial_blur_from` and `radial_blur_to` in `crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs`.
- In `radial_blur_to`, checked `centerX` and `centerY`. If either center coordinate is specified and differs from the default `0.5`, `radial_blur_to` returns `None`.
- Default center forms (`None`, `null`, or `0.5`) export normally to Photoshop's `RdlB` descriptor.
- Strict export (`actions.save`) returns an unrepresentable error on off-center blurs, and `skipUnsupported: true` safely records `filter.blur.radialBlur` in `skipped`.
- Added regression test `radial_blur_off_center_strict_export_refuses_silent_recentering` in `atn_cmds/tests.rs`.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Radial Blur imports now preserve amount, method, and quality settings.
  * Radial Blur exports require a pixel target and support omitted, null, or centered coordinates.
  * Exports reject unsupported off-center settings or mask targets without changing the action list.
  * When unsupported steps are skipped, affected Radial Blur steps are omitted and reported.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

included.head: 7145df8ded385ce253ca3f0c90866712f2bf2377
included.title: fix(atn): reject non-replace select.rect modes in .atn export (#7194)
included.body:
Fixes #7194

### Problem
When exporting recorded actions containing `select.rect` with `mode: "add"` or `mode: "remove"`, `atn_cmds::set_to` previously ignored the `mode` parameter and mapped the step into a standard marquee replace `set` event (`Elps` or `Rctn`). When replayed in Photoshop or imported back, the step would silently replace the active selection instead of adding to or subtracting from it, potentially corrupting selection workflows.

### Solution
- Updated `select.rect` in `atn_cmds::set_to` to check `p["mode"]`. Only `None` and `Some("replace")` produce an ATN descriptor.
- Non-replace modes return `None`, causing strict export (`actions.save`) to return an unrepresentable error as intended, or when `skipUnsupported: true` is supplied, record the step in `skipped`.
- Added a regression test `select_rect_mode_strict_export_rejects_unrepresentable_modes` covering default, replace, add, remove, and `skipUnsupported` modes.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Selection rectangle actions now export correctly when the mode is omitted or set to “replace.”
  * Actions using “add” or “subtract” are no longer exported as though those modes were supported. Strict exports report these actions as unsupported, while exports configured to skip unsupported actions omit them and report them as skipped. The action list remains unchanged when a strict export fails.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

included.head: f5d346e28bbecc77bd1ccfa5f4e08157238766c6
included.title: Camera Raw: vignette Midpoint 0 darkens only the corners
included.body:
Fixes #7183

**Problem.** In Camera Raw's post-crop vignette, Midpoint 0 put the falloff circle exactly on the frame edge, so the whole border darkened. At the lowest Midpoint the circle should be larger than the frame, so only the very corners get darker.

**Change.** `crates/algo/src/camera_raw.rs`, `vignette()`: the inner radius mapping goes from `1.0 - mid * 0.8` to `1.4 - mid * 1.2`. Midpoint 0 now places the circle beyond the frame (corners only), and Midpoint 100 stays tight to the centre. Note that this also moves the falloff for intermediate Midpoint values, including the default.

**Test.** `vignette_midpoint_zero_targets_corners_not_frame_edges`: on a 200×100 flat grey frame with Amount −80, Midpoint 0, Feather 50, the corner is darker than the middle of the top edge and the centre stays neutral.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Adjustments**
  * Vignette roundness now accounts for the image’s aspect ratio, reaching the frame corners at full roundness.
  * The vignette midpoint controls falloff more consistently: at 0, darkening extends toward the corners rather than the edges; at 100, it remains concentrated near the center.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

included.head: fb47b479b187c935cba8b95c147b5751ed9edbdc
included.title: fix(atn): export recorded layer.select with name parameter (#7185)
included.body:
## Summary

Fixes #7185.

When an action is recorded in PhotoCraft, selecting a layer records `layer.select {"name": ...}` (as introduced in #2441 for portable layer referencing). However, `select_to` in `crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs` only looked for the `"layer"` string parameter.

As a result:
- In strict `.atn` export, `actions.save` failed with an error claiming `layer.select` has no Photoshop equivalent.
- In the desktop UI (which uses `skipUnsupported: true`), the layer selection step was silently dropped from the exported action, causing subsequent recorded commands to act on whichever layer was previously active.

## Changes

1. **`select_to`**: Support both `name` and `layer` targets: `jstr(p, "name").or_else(|| jstr(p, "layer"))?`.
2. **`occurrence` handling**: Explicitly reject duplicate-name `occurrence` targets (`p.get("occurrence").is_some()`) because Photoshop name references cannot faithfully distinguish duplicate layer names; this avoids silently selecting the wrong layer on playback.
3. **Regression Tests**: Added `recorded_layer_select_exports_to_atn` in `crates/engine/src/atn_cmds/tests.rs` covering normal action recording, strict `.atn` save, `skipUnsupported` behavior, and duplicate occurrence rejection.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Layer selections can now resolve using the layer name, with the layer identifier as a fallback.
  * Recorded layer selections export as a single step without being skipped, including when unsupported steps are configured to be skipped.
  * Export now rejects layer selections that specify an occurrence target.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

included.head: cc3ca41c6d3f552bb8ce8cb5e5d58107c3f714be
included.title: Liquify: zoom the preview with the zoom keys, a trackpad pinch and ×1.1 wheel notches (#7210)
included.body:
Fixes #7210

### Problem
Liquify's preview could only zoom by turning a mouse wheel over it. The issue is from macOS, where people usually zoom another way, and none of those worked:
- **Pinch.** A trackpad pinch arrives as egui's `Event::Zoom` (`zoom_delta`), which the preview ignored.
- **Keyboard.** ⌘+ / ⌘− / ⌘0 / ⌘1 weren't handled in Liquify. While the dialog was open with one of its controls focused, they went to the canvas behind it (`nav_keys`) and zoomed that.
- **Wheel steps.** The wheel zoom used its own smoothed curve (`exp(scroll / 200)`) instead of the app's ×1.1 per notch.

Photoshop's Liquify zooms with the usual zoom keys and with a pinch.

### Solution
`crates/ui-egui/src/liquify_ui.rs`:
- **Keys.** Zoom In / Zoom Out step the preview along the canvas's zoom ladder (`zoom_levels::step_in_range`, within the preview's 1 %–3200 %). Fit on Screen fits and centres it again. Actual Pixels is the dialog's 100 %.
  - They are found through the canvas commands' own shortcuts, including Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts overrides and ⌘+ typed as Plus, so a remapped Zoom In works here too.
  - The key press is consumed, so the canvas behind the dialog keeps its zoom.
  - On macOS the native menu's key equivalents come back to egui as key presses (`native_menu`), so they reach the dialog the same way.
- **Wheel and pinch.** The preview reads the wheel through `wheel_nav::read`, as the Navigator does:
  - a notch zooms ×1.1 about the pointer, and ⇧+wheel snaps to the next ladder step;
  - a pinch zooms about the pointer, unless Preferences › Enhanced Controls › Zoom with Trackpad Pinch is off; Windows and Linux touchpad pinches are already folded into pinch events app-wide;
  - a sideways scroll pans.
- **Zoom range.** The preview's range is named once (`ZOOM_MIN`, `ZOOM_MAX`) instead of repeated literals.

`crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs`: `nav_keys` is split so the lookup, `nav_shortcut`, can be reused: it returns which navigation command's shortcut was pressed. `nav_keys` behaves as before.

### Tests
`liquify_ui::tests` (both fail before this change):
- `zoom_shortcuts_zoom_the_preview_not_the_canvas`:
  - ⌘1 → 100 %, ⌘= → 200 %, ⌘+ → 300 %, ⌘− → 200 %, ⌘0 → fits again on the next frame;
  - the canvas view's zoom is unchanged.
- `pinch_and_wheel_zoom_the_preview_about_the_pointer`:
  - a ×2 pinch doubles the zoom and keeps the document point under the pointer;
  - one wheel notch is ×1.1;
  - a pinch does nothing with Zoom with Trackpad Pinch off.

```
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib liquify      # 15 passed; the two new tests fail without the fix
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib shortcut     # 97 passed
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib wheel        # 56 passed
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib navigator    # 8 passed
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib input_tests  # 35 passed
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib zoom         # 80 passed
cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt --all -- --check                          # clean
```
I don't have a Mac, so the pinch is tested with egui's `Event::Zoom`, which is what a macOS pinch arrives as.

included.head: 00e4423fcca9ac0d9a117b229386d9665d307ce5
included.title: Layer effects in Dissolve mode speckle, as in Photoshop (#6995)
included.body:
Fixes #6995

### Problem
A layer effect set to **Dissolve** painted exactly like Normal. In Photoshop, a Dissolve Outer Glow turns into scattered, noisy speckle that thins out with the glow. Ours stayed a smooth fade. The effect painters passed Dissolve to `psblend::composite`, which has no noise and so blends it as Normal. Only a Dissolve *layer* got the per-pixel choice (`blend_into`, `fs_blend`). The open PRs on Dissolve (#3193, #4711) cover a Dissolve layer with effects, adjustments and clipping, not an effect's own mode.

### Solution
An effect in Dissolve mode now covers each pixel fully or not at all. The chance is its coverage × opacity, and the pixel is picked with the same document-coordinate noise as a Dissolve layer.

- **CPU** (`crates/compose/src/effects.rs`):
  - `paint` handles Dissolve. Every effect drawn through it gets it: drop and inner shadows, outer and inner glows (including gradient glows), colour, gradient and pattern overlays, satin, inside and centre strokes, and bevel highlights and shadows.
  - Outside strokes build their own coverage share. A Dissolve stroke's share becomes 0 or 1 the same way.
- **GPU** (`crates/gpu/src/compose.wgsl`): the same rule. `fx_composite` serves `fs_fxpaint` and the vector-stroke step in `fs_fxinit`, and `fs_fxstroke` resolves an outside stroke's share. An outside stroke runs two passes, its colour and its coverage, and `crates/gpu/src/plan.rs` now gives the coverage pass the stroke's mode as well; it used to be Normal there. Before that, the colour was all or nothing while the coverage stayed smooth, so the result was half transparent.
- **Tiling:** `maps_are_local` now treats a Dissolve effect like noise. Dissolve turns any coverage above zero into a chance of a full pixel. A tile's maps could carry blur rounding that differs from the whole layer's, so a pixel could flip at a tile edge.

### Tests
- `compose::tests::dissolve_effects_are_speckled_not_faded`. It fails before this change.
  - A Dissolve outer glow: every pixel in the ring is either the glow colour or the backdrop, with more speckle near the shape than further out. The Normal glow fades smoothly.
  - A tile renders exactly the same pixels as the whole document.
  - A 50 % Dissolve outside stroke: about half of the band is covered, and no pixel is half blue.
- `gpu/tests/parity.rs` `effect_cases` gains a Dissolve outer glow, inner gradient glow, drop shadow and outside stroke, compared with the CPU at U8 and U16.

```
cargo test -p photocraft-compose --lib                               # 290 passed
cargo clippy -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                           # clean
```
I couldn't run the GPU parity tests locally. My GPU (Intel Iris Pro 5200 on DX12) fails every `layer_effects_*` test with `Buffer is not mapped`, on unchanged `main` too. The changed `compose.wgsl` parses and validates with naga 30.0.1 (the version in `Cargo.lock`). The Windows CI run of the first push caught a mismatch in the Dissolve outside stroke between CPU and GPU (the coverage pass above), now fixed; CI's GPU job runs the new parity cases.

included.head: 3ee662093555182044d2e1f2bfa83ddd656a83ed
included.title: fix(ui): right-click an Adaptive Wide Angle constraint for its orientation menu, as in Photoshop
included.body:
### Problem
In Filter › Adaptive Wide Angle…, right-clicking a constraint line deleted it at once. Photoshop instead opens a menu on the constraint to choose its orientation or delete it ([Adobe's Adaptive Wide Angle help](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/using/adaptive-wide-angle-filter.html)). `docs/context-menu-parity.md` lists this as a P1 behaviour mismatch.

### Solution
`crates/ui-egui/src/wide_angle_ui.rs`:
- **The menu.** Right-clicking a constraint opens `constraint_menu` with Free, Horizontal and Vertical (the current orientation checked) and Delete. The menu uses the same hit test as before: the constraint whose curve passes within 10 pt of the click.
- **Away from a constraint.** A right-click away from every constraint opens nothing and deletes nothing.
- **Labels.** The menu reuses the labels the constraint list in the panel already shows ("Free", "Horizontal", "Vertical", "Delete"), so the two read the same. Photoshop's Arbitrary angle isn't offered because the solver has no arbitrary-angle constraint yet.
- **Control channel.** It gains `"orient": {"index": i, "orientation": "free|horizontal|vertical"}` beside `add` and `remove`, so agents can do what the menu does. A missing or out-of-range index is an error.
- **Hint.** The dialog's hint no longer says "right-click to delete". It now reads "…; right-click a constraint to change or delete it." The 20 catalogs that carried the old hint get the new key, with only its last clause rewritten, so `complete_menus` stays satisfied.

`docs/context-menu-parity.md` marks the row done, except Arbitrary.

### Tests
- `right_click_on_a_constraint_opens_its_menu` drives the dialog with real pointer events through egui_kittest:
  - right-click the constraint, choose Horizontal: the constraint is kept and turns horizontal;
  - right-click away from it: no menu, nothing deleted;
  - right-click it again, Delete: it is gone.
- `orient_sets_a_constraint_orientation` covers the control-channel op and its bad indices.

included.head: cfa5242098c408ee1c3477eb5b5fc060de235a7e
included.title: Smart Filters: double-clicking a Liquify filter reopens it in the Liquify workspace
included.body:
## What's wrong

Double-clicking a Liquify smart filter in the Layers panel opens the generic parameter form, whose only field is Mesh Size, instead of the Liquify workspace. `smart_ui::open_editor` (`crates/ui-egui/src/smart_ui.rs:280-311` on `main`) sends Camera Raw and the Filter Gallery to their own dialogs, adjustments to their Image › Adjustments editors, and every other filter to `filter_dialog`. OK on that form replays the recorded strokes on the form's mesh size. Filter › Liquify always opens with no strokes (`liquify_ui.rs:466`), so the recorded strokes cannot be edited again.

To see it: make a smart object, run Filter › Liquify, drag one stroke, press OK, then double-click the Liquify row under Smart Filters.

## What changed

- `open_editor` sends a Liquify smart filter to a new `liquify_ui::open_smart_filter`.
- `open_smart_filter` opens the workspace on the smart object's pixels below that filter, with the filter's recorded strokes and mesh size, as `gallery_ui::open_smart_filter` does (#3426).
- OK then runs `layer.smartFilter.setParams` with the strokes and the mesh size in one history step, and no second Liquify filter is added. OK after Restore All leaves the filter with no strokes. Cancel leaves the filter unchanged. Filter › Liquify on a smart object still adds a new filter.

Ten-W reported this in #6571. Part of #6571: the Puppet Warp and Perspective Warp smart filters it also lists are left for later.

## Tests

New tests in `liquify_ui.rs` use a smart object with a Liquify filter (one stroke, mesh size 3) under a Gaussian Blur:

- `smart_filter_double_click_edits_the_recorded_liquify` checks the workspace's strokes, mesh size and source pixels, then that a new stroke and OK update the filter in one step and Undo restores it. Without the new `open_editor` branch it fails at "no generic parameter form".
- `smart_filter_cancel_keeps_and_restore_all_clears_the_recorded_strokes` fails without the `setParams` route in `commit`.
- `open_smart_filter_rejects_other_filters_and_layers` (the blur, an index past the end, a pixel layer) fails without the Liquify check.

These ran with #6906 applied (`main` at 5f65579 does not build, #6911):

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- liquify_ui:: gallery_ui::tests::smart_filter camera_raw_ui::tests::smart_filter smart_ui::` (22 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo xtask layers`

On Windows 11 (x86-64) with rustc 1.99.0, with `main` at ead6d21 merged in (cfa5242), and with two fixes for tests that fail on Windows on `main` applied: #5230's commit d6df2c17 (`photocraft-algo`'s `stack::tests::statistics_are_bit_identical_to_the_serial_implementation`) and #7152 (`photocraft-text`'s `tests::works_without_craft_fonts` with current craft-fonts):
- `cargo xtask ci` passes fmt and clippy. Its test step stopped on `an_ambient_map_or_lut_never_renders_unfiltered_pixels_into_the_stack_cache`, which passes when run alone.
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 9,101 passed, 0 failed, 73 ignored.
- `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` pass.

The branch merges cleanly into `main` at ead6d21. It conflicts with #3283 in `open_editor` (keep the Liquify branch after the Filter Gallery branch) and with #6519 in `liquify_ui::open` (keep #6519's selection set-up in `open` and pass it to `open_on`).

included.head: b8727aff860775e6f1ee2c8063bf726a7c0fe60e
included.title: Type: register craft fonts of every script, not only the Japanese ones
included.body:
## What's wrong

`crates/text/build.rs` embeds every font in craft-fonts' `fonts/manifest.txt`, but `FontDb::new` registers only the entries whose scripts include `Jpan` (`crates/text/src/fonts.rs:227` on `main`). craft-fonts `8dcdacd5` adds Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic, and `3d9ab3a1` (its `main`) adds Noto Sans Thai. Built with either, the binary carries those fonts, but the font list does not show them and text layers do not fall back to them, although the fallback lists name all three (`fonts.rs:63`, `:67-68`, `cjk.rs:211`). In `TextEngine::new()`, 中文图层 set in Inter lays out with 2 `.notdef` glyphs of 4, and مرحبا lays out with 5 `.notdef` glyphs of 5. `tests::works_without_craft_fonts` fails ("Noto Sans CJK SC registered under its manifest name"). CI checks out craft-fonts at `abb83316`, which has only Japanese fonts.

## What changed

- `FontDb::new` registers every `CRAFT_FONTS` entry through a new `register_craft_fonts`. A single-face file registers under its manifest family, whatever family its `name` table gives (`FontInfoOverride`, as `select_named_face` uses it). Each face of a collection keeps its own family.
- Behavior change: with Noto Sans CJK SC built in and no Simplified Chinese system font, Japanese text set in Inter takes Noto Sans CJK SC when the UI locale is not Japanese, in the order `cjk::script_order` gives shared Han. `craft_fonts_cover_japanese_without_system_fonts` now expects the first CJK craft family in that order.
- Comments that said craft-fonts holds only Japanese fonts are updated.

#2169 by diax7 registers the Arabic craft fonts and makes `build.rs` embed only Japanese and Arabic lines; this change keeps `build.rs` and registers every embedded font.

## Tests

- New `craft_fonts_of_every_script_register_under_their_manifest_families` registers in-memory `Hans`, `Arab` and `Jpan` entries made from Inter and checks their families and the fallback stack; it fails with the `Jpan` filter back, with or without craft-fonts.
- New `craft_font_collections_keep_their_face_families`: a two-face collection keeps its faces' families. It fails when collections take the manifest family.
- New `craft_fonts_cover_their_other_scripts_without_system_fonts`: 中文图层, مرحبا and ภาษาไทย set in Inter lay out without `.notdef` when the build has a craft font for the script. With the `Jpan` filter back it fails.
- `tests::works_without_craft_fonts` fails on `main` at `efa1edd` with craft-fonts `8dcdacd5` and `3d9ab3a1`, and passes with the change.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-text` with either checkout (157 passed, 4 ignored), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-text --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo xtask layers` pass.

On Windows 11 (x86-64) with rustc 1.99.0, with `main` at ead6d21 merged in (b8727af), and with #5230's commit d6df2c17 applied. That commit fixes `photocraft-algo`'s `stack::tests::statistics_are_bit_identical_to_the_serial_implementation`, which fails in incremental Windows builds on `main` (its Kurtosis comes out 1 ULP high in two values):
- `cargo xtask ci` passes its 5 steps: 9,096 tests passed, 0 failed, 73 ignored.

`git merge-tree` reports no conflicts with `main` at ead6d21. #2169 and #424 (TheSeanLavery) already conflict with `main` and change the same loop. With #2169, keep this loop, which registers every font its `build.rs` still embeds. With #424, `register_craft_fonts` reads each font through #424's `bytes()`.

included.head: c05d827fdea5ee0c96231b83936d4994fa25afbc
included.title: perf(type): refresh type layers without cloning the document (#7092)
included.body:
Fixes #7092. Typing in a type layer no longer clones the whole document on every keystroke and pointer move.

### Root cause
`type_cmds::refresh` reads only the document's resolution and pixel format, but it took `&Document`. Every call site that holds the layer mutably had to clone the whole document to pass it: 15 of them across `type_cmds`, `type_extra_cmds`, `type_spell_cmds`, `type_styles_cmds`, `variables_cmds`, `warp_cmds` and `edit_menu_cmds`. `with_text_layer` (behind `type.edit`) and `with_text` also handed that copy to their closures, but every closure reads only `resolution_dpi` from it.

### Fix
- New `type_cmds::refresh_at(dpi, format, t)`. `refresh(doc, t)` stays as a wrapper, so callers that already hold the document (ui-egui, `canvas_geom`, `transform_cmds`, open PRs) don't change.
- The 15 sites read `(doc.resolution_dpi, doc.pixel_format())` before borrowing the layer, instead of cloning.
- `with_text_layer` and `with_text` pass their closures the resolution instead of a document copy. `type_extra_cmds` gets `layout_at(dpi, t)` next to `layout(doc, t)` for those closures.
- Two clones stay because they're used for more than `refresh`: Convert to Shape (`text_path`, `refresh_shape`) and the warp command's `refresh_text`.

### Numbers
`type.edit` on a 6000 × 4000 document with filled raster layers and a two-letter type layer, alternating the text, median of 300 edits. Release build, Intel Core Ultra X7 358H, Linux, with another job keeping all cores busy (main and this PR ran back to back).

| Layers | `Document::clone` | `type.edit` main | `type.edit` this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 60 | 0.26 ms | 5.60 ms | 5.14 ms |
| 20 | 0.09 ms | 4.33 ms | 3.90 ms |

The saving is a little more than one clone, because the copy also had to be dropped. On a big paragraph the render dominates (#7032), so this matters most for small edits and many-layer documents.

### Tests
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests` (1916 passed), `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p photocraft-ui-egui -p photocraft-automation`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` all pass. No behaviour changes, so there's no new test. The existing type command tests cover every edited path.

Note for #6935: it reads these snapshots as the "before" state in `guard_fit` (only `fit.is_some()` of the old layer). Whichever lands second can read that one bool before borrowing the layer.

included.title: Layer Style: keep gradient overlay colours when reopening the dialog (#7031)
included.body:
Fixes #7031

Reopening Layer Style on a layer whose gradient overlay has more than two stops (classic interpolation or a PSD import bakes interior stops) reset the From/To fields to the factory black-to-white, because `values_of` only loaded endpoint colours and geometry for plain two-stop gradients.

Now the dialog always loads the first and last stop colours plus reverse, style, angle and scale. Interior stops stay in the effect snapshot, so applying the dialog again keeps the baked curve and only retints the ends.

Test: `baked_gradient_overlay_keeps_endpoint_colours_on_reopen` in `crates/ui-egui/src/layer_style.rs` applies a classic red-to-blue overlay, reopens the dialog, checks From/To are still red/blue, and re-applies to confirm the multi-stop curve and endpoints survive.

included.head: a6d36d0879dfc9b1c8f04449fbb764235ec6ce95
included.title: Crop: X with a ratio preset turns the frame instead of shrinking it (#7057)
included.body:
**TL;DR:** With a ratio preset (e.g. 16:9), X now turns the crop frame to 9:16 at the same size instead of shrinking it, and X again brings it back.

Fixes #7057.

## What was wrong
`swap_orientation` (`crates/ui-egui/src/crop_ui.rs`) swapped the preset ratio and then fitted it inside the old, unswapped frame. Fitting never adds area, so every X shrank the frame: a centred 80x45 frame became 25.3x45, then 25.3x14.2 after a second X. Without a preset, X already turned the frame.

## Fix
The frame turns first (`keyed(app, swapped(r))`), then `apply_ratio` fits the swapped ratio to it (a no-op for a frame that already matches).

## Test
`x_swaps_the_frame_orientation_not_the_colours` extended: 16:9, frame [60,27.5,140,72.5]; X → 9:16 and [77.5,10,122.5,90]; X again → 16:9 and the original frame. It fails on main.

included.head: 52ad01f426910e1780ee9419c9cb1b4c80eeb035
included.title: Eyedropper: a large sampling ring that reads on any colour (#6973)
included.body:
## Eyedropper: a large sampling ring that reads on any colour (#6973)

The comparison ring drawn while the Eyedropper is held was 22 pt across with 4 pt arcs, outlined only by a thin semi-transparent dark stroke. Over a flat area of the colour being sampled the upper arc had the image's own colour and disappeared, so the ring looked broken (https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/6973).

Now it follows Photoshop's structure, measured from the screenshots in the issue (316 px vs the old 42 px on the same screen):

- an **opaque neutral grey outer band** (~17 pt) around the pointer,
- a **coloured band of the same width** inside it: the sampled colour on the upper half, the current foreground on the lower, meeting at 3 and 9 o'clock as in Photoshop (the old gap is gone),
- **thin dark and light hairlines** (one physical pixel) on the ring's two edges, so every boundary reads even on a flat mid-grey that matches the band itself,
- the **pipette stays visible at the centre**, its tip on the sampled pixel — a ring this size says nothing about where it samples without it.

Sizes are in points, so the ring scales with Interface › UI Scale. `Show Sampling Ring` off and Preferences › Cursors › Precise keep their old fallbacks.

### Implementation notes

- `eyedropper_ring` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` draws the bands with `circle_stroke` (which in egui 0.36 paints its stroke *outside* the radius) and the upper half-ring with a centred `Shape::line` arc.
- New integration test `crates/ui-egui/tests/eyedropper_ring.rs` renders the real app offscreen over a flat `#7f7f7f` document — exactly the ring grey, the worst case — and asserts both ring edges and the pipette differ from the background, and that nothing is drawn with Show Sampling Ring off. Verified visually with the offscreen renders.

### The build-fix commit

`main` currently doesn't compile: `Persisted` misses `export_presets` in `load_presets_json` (E0063, #6965 / #6911). The first commit adds the missing line so this PR builds standalone; it overlaps with the pending fixes (#6906, #6921, #6930, #6981) and can be dropped if one of those lands first.

### Tests

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` (2988 pass) and `--tests` (all integration files, 0 failures)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib` (1702 pass)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- `cargo xtask layers` clean

## What

Fixes #6958 — File Info showed a stored exposure of 0.031714 s (about 1/32 s) as `0.03 s`.

`exposure_text` in `crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs` used the `1/n` form only when `1/t` was within 1 % of a whole number. For exposures longer than 1/50 s that tolerance is smaller than half a denominator step, so most real camera values (phones store 1/32 as 31714/1000000) fell through to `short_num(t, 2)` and lost a digit or two.

Now:

* sub-second exposures use the **nearest whole denominator** when it is within 5 % of the stored value — `0.031714 s → `1/32 s`, `0.0215 s → `1/47 s` (the issue's fixtures), while `0.4 s` still renders as `0.4 s`, not `1/3 s`;
* the decimal fallback for sub-second times keeps **three significant digits** instead of two decimals (`0.2731 s → `0.273 s`), per the issue's suggestion;
* exposures ≥ 1 s are unchanged.

Tests: extended `camera_data_formats_like_photoshop_and_falls_back_to_xmp` with the fixture values and the fallback. `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib` (1702 passed), clippy clean, `cargo xtask layers` OK.

## Note on the first commit

Main currently does not compile: the `Persisted` initializer in `load_presets_json` misses `export_presets` (E0063, #6965 / #6911). Since that blocks building and testing the engine crate, this branch carries the same one-line fix as #6906 / #6921 / #6930 / #6981, byte-identical to #6930's hunk so whichever lands first merges clean and this commit drops out. Drop it if you prefer to merge a build fix first.

included.title: Color Picker: update the colour on press, not on release (#6937)
included.body:
## Problem

Closes #6937

In the Color Picker dialog, clicking and holding on the vertical component strip (hue/saturation/value bar) or the colour field did nothing until the mouse button was released — the issue reports a ~2 s delay, which is the hold time. Photoshop updates the selected colour the instant the bar is pressed.

## Cause & fix

`color_field` gated both interactions on `resp.dragged() || resp.clicked()`. egui's `clicked()` fires on **release**, and `dragged()` only after the pointer moves past the drag tolerance — so a stationary press produced no update.

Both handlers now use `is_pointer_button_down_on()`, which is true from the press frame onwards and covers dragging too (the existing clamping keeps drags outside the widget pinned to the edge, as before). `clicked()` is kept for the release frame and keyboard-style clicks.

## Tests

- New regression test `hue_strip_updates_the_color_on_press_not_on_release`: presses and holds near the bottom of the hue strip in a kittest harness and asserts the colour has already changed **before** release (and that release doesn't move it again). Verified to fail on the old code and pass on the new.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests` green, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo xtask layers` OK.
- Note: `cargo xtask wasm` cannot run in my environment (Homebrew rustc without the wasm32-unknown-unknown std); the change is egui-API-only and `is_pointer_button_down_on` is already used elsewhere in this crate (e.g. `titlebar.rs`, `brush_panel.rs`), so wasm risk is nil — CI will confirm.

included.title: Selections don't mark a document modified (#6865)
included.body:
Fixes #6865.

Using the marquee, lasso, Magic Wand, Quick Selection, Object Selection or any Select menu command no longer marks a clean document as modified. You don't get a title-bar asterisk or a save prompt on close just for selecting.

**How**
- `Session::edit`, `undo`, `redo` and `history.selectState` keep a clean document clean when the step changed nothing but `Document::selection` (`DocState::keeps_clean` / `bump_revision`). Making a selection is still a history step, so undo and the History panel work the same as before.
- `layer_multi_cmds::selection_only_change` decides what counts as selection-only. It uses `same_pixels` to compare pixels by tile pointer, which also turns down video layers. Every other field is compared structurally, and `Arc`-of-`Eq` data shortcuts on pointer identity, so the check stays cheap on big documents. The destructure is exhaustive, so a new `Document` field won't compile until someone decides whether it counts.
- A real edit still dirties the document, and a later selection change or undo can't make it clean again. Save Selection (adds a channel) and Quick Mask also still dirty it.

**Tests**
- New `tests::selection_tools_do_not_dirty_the_document`, at 8, 16 and 32-bit: rect, ellipse add, lasso subtract, inverse, all, deselect, then undo/redo, a history jump, and a real edit afterwards.
- Ran `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib` filtered to `dirty|clean|save|undo|history_select|selecting_a_layer|edits_that_change_no_pixels`: 111 passed.

**Notes**
- `main` doesn't compile right now (`Persisted` is missing `export_presets` in `presets/mod.rs`, which #6906 fixes). I patched that line locally only so I could run the tests. It is not part of this PR.
- A `.pcraft` save still writes the current selection. A selection change just doesn't, on its own, count as unsaved work.

included.title: fix(shortcuts): Page Up/Down and arrow-key shortcuts never fired (#6827)
included.body:
Fixes #6827.

**Cause:** `prefs::normalize_shortcut` Title-cased multi-letter key names, so a shortcut recorded in Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts as `Shift+PageUp` was stored as `Shift+Pageup`. egui's `Key::from_name` is case-sensitive, so `shortcuts::parse` returned `None` and the binding was silently dropped. This is why Flip Horizontal/Vertical on Shift/Ctrl/Alt+Page Up/Down did nothing, while the same commands on other keys worked. Arrow keys (`Arrowleft`) and other camel-case names were affected the same way.

**Fix:**
- `crates/engine/src/prefs.rs`: `normalize_shortcut` keeps egui's spelling for camel-case key names (PageUp, PageDown, Arrow*, Open/CloseBracket, Numpad*…) and accepts PgUp/PgDn.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs`: new `key_from_name` falls back to a case-insensitive match, so bindings saved by older builds (`Shift+Pageup`) start working with no migration. It is used by `parse` and by the native menu's `key_event`.

**Tests:** engine `shortcuts_normalise_and_detect_conflicts` gets PageUp/PageDown/PgDn/ArrowLeft cases. ui-egui `page_and_arrow_keys_recorded_in_the_editor_fire` round-trips editor capture through `parse` and `key_matches`, plus the legacy spellings. Not run locally: the engine lib-test target doesn't compile on main right now for an unrelated reason (`presets/mod.rs:180`, missing `export_presets`), and the ui-egui suite is too slow to build here. CI will run them.

included.title: Shortcuts: custom bindings on PageUp/PageDown (and other multi-word keys) fire again (#6827)
included.body:
Fixes #6827.

## Cause

`normalize_shortcut` (`crates/engine/src/prefs.rs`) title-cases every named key. So a binding set to `Shift+PageUp` in Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts was saved as `Shift+Pageup`, and egui's case-sensitive `Key::from_name` matches no key with that spelling: the shortcut never fired.

This affected every command, not just Flip. The reporter's other PgUp/PgDn shortcuts worked because built-in defaults keep the right spelling. The other keys affected are the ones egui spells with several capitals: OpenBracket, CloseBracket, OpenCurlyBracket, CloseCurlyBracket, BrowserBack and IntlBackslash. Arrows are named `Up` etc., so they were fine.

## Change

- **`normalize_shortcut` (via `capitalize`):** multi-word key names keep egui's spelling.
- **`shortcuts::parse`:** matches key names case-insensitively, so bindings already saved as `Pageup` by earlier versions work without re-binding.

## Tests

- **`layer_shortcut_tests::custom_page_up_and_page_down_bindings_fire`:** binds Shift+PageUp, Ctrl+Shift+PageUp and Ctrl+Alt+PageDown to `edit.transform.flipHorizontal`; each press runs it. Without the change, nothing runs (`left: []`). The test also checks that `Shift+Pageup` parses.

| Binding | v0.9.x | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Shift+F9 (control) | flips | flips |
| Shift+PageUp | nothing | flips |

included.head: 643c9b7044fc6b6e88b389eb3b01d5202c0a563b
included.title: Web: one press per tap, so menus open again on touch (#2095)
included.body:
Fixes #2095.

## Cause
In the browser, eframe 0.36.2 turns one finger or pen tap into **two** primary presses and two releases: one pair from Pointer Events (`pointerdown` / `pointerup`, which fire for touch and pen too) and one from Touch Events (`touchstart` / `touchend`), which mobile browsers fire for the same contact. `pointerdown` runs a frame of its own, so the `touchstart` press lands in the next frame while the button is still held. The menu bar titles (`menus.rs` `title_press`) and press menus (`press_menu.rs`) toggle on the press, so the twin press closed the menu the first one had just opened. Desktop Chrome with a mouse sends no Touch Events, which is why it works there.

## Fix
New `photocraft_ui_egui::touch_twins::drop_twins`, called from the web shell's `raw_input_hook`: it drops a primary press that arrives while the button is already held (pressed within 0.5 s) and a primary release that arrives while it is already up. A press held longer still passes, so a release the browser never sent can't lock the pointer down. Desktop builds are unchanged.

## Tests
- `touch_twins::tests::a_tap_opens_a_menu_title_every_time`: drives the real menu bar with the event sequence eframe produces for a tap. Without the hook the tap leaves File closed (the bug); with it, tap opens, tap closes, tap opens again.
- `touch_twins::tests::a_press_held_for_long_still_passes`: twin press and extra releases are dropped; a stale press is kept.

Not tried on a real Android device. The report also mentions a DeX mouse; a mouse sends no Touch Events, so that case isn't explained by this and may need a follow-up if it persists.

Note: `origin/main` currently fails to compile `photocraft-engine` (`Persisted` is missing `export_presets` in `load_presets_json`, from #5616 meeting #5344); I patched it locally only to run the tests and left it out of this PR.

included.head: be9cca9bd96491c97fecfcce46b71ed483b6de0c
included.title: Background redraw: keep the last finished composites, so a solo's restore uploads instead of recompositing (part of #6528)
included.body:
Part of #6528 (solo/restore).

### Cause

When the layers exceed the GPU memory budget, a large visibility change is redrawn by the CPU compositor in 1024 px blocks (`background_redraw`). Each finished block was uploaded to the canvas texture and dropped, and nothing remembered which document state a finished redraw showed. Alt-clicking an eye to solo a layer (which fits the GPU) overwrites the texture, so the restore composites every layer again from scratch (about 4 s on a 50 MP PSB, ~100 s on a multi-GB PSB), and a second restore is no faster.

### Fix

`background_redraw` now keeps the texels of its last two finished redraws (`KeptComposites`), keyed by the whole `Arc<Document>` they drew, plus the display transform's texture key, the texture format and the block grid. A redraw that starts for a state equal to a kept one uploads those blocks instead of compositing (perf kind `kept`).

- **Exact key.** The key is the document itself, compared with `==` (same approach as the GPU compositor's prefix cache in `crates/gpu/src/prefix.rs`): layer pixels (Arc-shared tiles compare without reading pixels), visibility, opacity, blend, masks, adjustments and every other document field. It can miss more than strictly needed (e.g. a selection changed in between), never hit stale. A redraw that is restarted on an edited document drops the blocks it collected from the old state, so only a composite drawn entirely from one state is kept.
- **Bounded memory.** At most two composites, within what Memory Usage leaves beside the document's own pixels and History (`history_budget_bytes() - memory_bytes()`); a collection that would pass that cap is abandoned, the cap is re-checked (and older entries dropped) at every fresh redraw, and a closed document's entries go with it.

### Tests

- `kept_composites_come_back_only_for_the_exact_state_and_stay_bounded`: store; hit on the same state (also an equal document in another `Arc`, as after a solo + restore); miss on a visibility, opacity, blend or pixel change, another display key, texture format or block grid; LRU eviction at two entries; byte cap; closed documents.
- `showing_a_hidden_layer_again_reuses_the_redraw_from_before_it_was_hidden` (GPU, skips without an adapter): hide then show a layer on a CPU-only document; the show starts no redraw, reports `kept`, and the texture matches the synchronous CPU composite; a later opacity change composites again.

Locally the unit test passes. The GPU harness on this machine crashes with an access violation inside the driver, also on the existing `a_full_cpu_refresh_draws_in_the_background_with_the_synchronous_pixels`, so the GPU test relies on CI here. Clippy wasn't run locally.

### Not in this PR

- The second part of #6528, "raising Memory Usage doesn't change the GPU budget" (the budget stays 3006 MB at 50000 MB): untouched.
- Only states drawn by the background CPU redraw are kept. A state first drawn on the GPU (or by a synchronous CPU refresh) isn't, so e.g. a solo that is itself over budget still composites once before its own restore can hit; a stack-prefix cache (re-blend only the layers above the toggled one) would be the next step.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

* **Performance**
  * Returning to a previously displayed layer state can reuse its completed background composite when document, display settings, texture format, and layout match, reducing background redraws.
  * Changes to layer visibility, opacity, blend mode, or pixel content trigger a new composite.
  * Recent composites are retained within entry-count and memory limits, and removed when documents close or memory limits change.
  * Background redraws preserve compatible progress across continuation, improving responsiveness during repeated updates.

included.title: test(ui): a toolbar click with no prior hover picks the tool (part of #2603)
included.body:
Part of #2603.

## Cause

Not a hover or hit-test bug in the toolbar. The tool buttons are plain `Sense::click()` widgets, and egui hit-tests a press at the press position, so a click needs no hover before it. The report's other symptom, a blank band along the window's top and left edges, matches #2246: on some Windows 10 systems the compositor kept the undecorated window's caption and border, so the UI was drawn offset from where the pointer reported. A click then landed on the wrong spot. Hovering seemed to help because the hover highlight showed where the pointer really was, so the reporter could move until it sat on the intended icon. #2401, the fix for #2246, landed after 0.6.0 and shipped in 0.7.0.

## Fix

Nothing to change on main. This PR adds a regression test so that a toolbar click never comes to depend on a prior hover.

## Tests

- `panels::tests::a_click_without_a_prior_hover_picks_the_tool` sends only a primary press and release at the Brush and Type buttons, with no `PointerMoved` before them (the pointer has never entered the window), and checks that the tool becomes active.

The real-window offset fix (#2401) can't be tested headlessly; the reporter has been asked to retest on 0.9.0.

included.head: 616ab9d56a00e47a0a1f79edf1de1f559d0283c2
included.title: Actions: .atn Select Subject, Select and Mask, Color Range, clipping and layer masks, colours map to commands (part of #6745)
included.body:
Part of #6745.

### Cause

The `.atn` event table (`crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs` `EVENTS`) had no entries for `autoCutout`, `smartBrushWorkspace`, `colorRange` or `groupEvent`, and the converters for events it did know missed shapes common in retouching sets:

- `selectiveColor` was mapped, but the `Clrs` table used `Yllw` (the yellow-ink key) for the yellows range. Photoshop writes `Ylws`, so any Selective Color step that touched yellows failed to convert. Export wrote the same wrong code.
- `make` did not handle Add Layer Mask (a `Chnl` made at the mask channel).
- `set` did not handle setting the foreground or background colour.

### Fix

| `.atn` event | command | params translated |
|---|---|---|
| `autoCutout` (Select Subject) | `select.subject` | `sampleAllLayers` |
| `smartBrushWorkspace` (Select and Mask) | `select.refineEdge` | radius, smart radius, smooth, feather, contrast, shift edge, decontaminate + amount, output, sampleAllLayers |
| `selectiveColor` / `SlcC` | `image.adjustments.selectiveColor` (and the adjustment layer) | the yellows range is read as `Ylws` and now exported as `Ylws`. Legacy `Yllw` from older PhotoCraft exports still reads |
| `colorRange` / `ClrR` (presets) | `select.colorRange` | reds…magentas, highlights/midtones/shadows (fuzziness and range limits), skin tones (fuzziness), out of gamut, invert |
| `groupEvent` / `GrpL` | `layer.createClippingMask` | target or named layer |
| `ungroup` / `Ungr` | `layer.releaseClippingMask` | target or named layer |
| `make` of a layer mask (`UsrM` `RvlA`/`HdAl`/`RvlS`/`HdSl`) | `layer.layerMask.revealAll` / `hideAll` / `revealSelection` / `hideSelection` | none |
| `set` of `FrgC` / `BckC` (RGB, HSB or gray) | `tools.setColors` | `foreground` / `background` |

All of these also export back to the same Photoshop events, except Select and Mask, which still exports as `refineSelectionEdge` like before.

Steps whose parameters can't be translated faithfully still import as kept Photoshop steps and are reported as unsupported. That covers Color Range with Sampled Colors (a Lab min/max range), Color Range with any key the converter doesn't know, mask/colour variants other than the ones above, and colours in Lab, CMYK or a colour book.

**`groupEvent` is not Group Layers.** The issue suggests `layer.new.group`, but Photoshop's `groupEvent` (`GrpL`) is Create Clipping Mask (the old "Group with Previous"). Grouping layers is recorded as `make` of a `layerSection`, which was already mapped. This matches the high-pass sharpening action (duplicate, High Pass, blend mode, clip).

### Tests

- `retouching_set_events_map_to_their_commands`: synthetic Photoshop-shaped descriptors for each new mapping, written as stringID events like the issue's file (`autoCutout`, `smartBrushWorkspace`, `selectiveColor` with `Ylws`/`Whts`, `colorRange` skin tones, `make` mask, `set` foreground, `groupEvent`). Each one is checked against the expected (command id, params). Sampled Colors, an unknown Color Range key, a Lab colour and an unknown event still report unsupported. Legacy `Yllw` still reads.
- `every_mapped_command_exports_and_imports_back`: round-trip cases for `select.subject`, `select.colorRange` (4 shapes), both clipping-mask commands, the 4 mask commands, `tools.setColors` (fg and bg) and yellows in Selective Color.

### Not in this PR

- **`Adobe Camera Raw Filter`**: skipped. The descriptor layout of a recorded Camera Raw step isn't verified. `photocraft-io`'s Camera Raw decoder only accepts the PSD smart-filter layout (process version 5/6, known keys only). Mapping it without a real recording risks running with wrong values. A sample `.atn` from the reporter would settle it.
- **`move`**: skipped. Layer nudges in px/pt and Bring Forward/Send Backward/Front/Back already map. The remaining shape seen in recorded sets moves a layer to an absolute index (a panel drag). That index has no meaning in another document, so it stays unsupported.
- **Other `set` / `make` shapes** in the reporter's file can't be identified without it (blend mode, opacity, fill, name and visibility on a layer were already mapped). With the file, `actions.load`'s `unsupported` list names each step that is left.
- `docs/gaps.md` G11 is not updated here.

included.head: 1069d30cb1f0ff682161ee11f4cc36b2d376d8f0
included.title: HEIF: honour the nclx colour description; HLG/PQ HEICs open as linear BT.2020 32-bit (#6752)
included.body:
Fixes #6752.

## Cause

`photocraft-heif` only read the `colr` **ICC** profile (`icc_for_item`). The `nclx` box was read by heic-rs, which applies its matrix and range when converting YCbCr to RGB, but its **primaries and transfer characteristics** were never passed on. A 10-bit HEIC tagged BT.2020 + ARIB STD-B67 (HLG) therefore opened as if its HLG-encoded BT.2020 values were sRGB: too bright and desaturated/shifted.

## Fix

- `photocraft-heif`: `Decoded::nclx` (primaries, transfer, matrix, full-range), inherited from the grid tiles like the ICC profile already is.
- `photocraft-codecs`: `Image::cicp` plus a small `cicp` module with the BT.2100 transfer functions. A PQ or HLG image is decoded to **linear light in a 32-bit float image**: HLG inverse OETF, then the OOTF for a 1000 cd/m² display (system gamma 1.2, luminance weights of the declared primaries), scaled so BT.2408's 203 cd/m² diffuse white is 1.0. PQ uses the ST 2084 EOTF on the same scale. The memory limit is checked again for the float image.
- `photocraft-cms`: `builtin::cicp_rgb(primaries, transfer, linear)` builds the profile for an H.273 description (BT.709 / BT.2020 / P3-D65 primaries; sRGB, BT.709, linear, gamma 2.2/2.8 curves), reusing the built-ins where they match.
- `photocraft-io`: a HEIF with no ICC profile gets that profile: linear BT.2020 for the HLG case, Display P3 / Rec. 2020 for SDR P3 / BT.2020 files. BT.709/sRGB SDR files stay untagged, as before.

**Why linear 32-bit float rather than tone-mapping to 16-bit:** PQ and HLG can't be an ICC tone curve, and the import path already supports 32-bit float with a linear profile (that is how OpenEXR and Radiance HDR open). So no new tone-mapping curve had to be chosen, and highlights above diffuse white are kept (values up to 1000/203 ≈ 4.9 for HLG) the way Photoshop holds HDR. Display and 8/16-bit conversion then go through the normal colour-managed path.

Out of scope (open PRs): matrix/range when the description is only in the HEVC VUI or only on grid tiles (#6089, #2354). An HLG file whose `nclx` is only in the VUI (no `colr` box) is not covered by this change.

## Tests

- `heif`: `nclx` parsed from hand-built `colr` boxes on a coded picture, and inherited by a grid from its tile; an ICC-only file has no `nclx`.
- `codecs::cicp`: HLG inverse OETF segment join (E' 0.5 → 1/12) and BT.2100/BT.2408 reference points (75 % HLG → 203 cd/m² = 1.0, peak → 1000/203, 50 % → 50.7 cd/m²), PQ (0.5807 → 203 cd/m², 1.0 → 10000/203), hue kept, NaN/inf/negative are safe; `linearize` gives F32, keeps alpha, drops the encoded ICC; SDR input is returned unchanged.
- `cms`: CICP → built-in mapping, linear BT.2020 colorants/curve and a valid ICC encoding; HLG/PQ without linear and unknown primaries are `None`.
- `io`: HLG BT.2020 (and unspecified primaries) is tagged linear BT.2020; BT.709/sRGB `nclx` stays untagged; P3 is tagged Display P3.

Not verified against the reporter's file (none attached); no corpus fixture added.

included.head: bb6bd84d8eb827867689ed85cc51d61a7018176a
included.title: Keep shape fill and stroke alpha through PSD round-trip (#6180)
included.body:
Keep shape fill and stroke alpha through a PSD round-trip.

Fixes #6180.

Photoshop colour descriptors (`RGBC` and friends) have no alpha channel, so a rectangle fill at 50% opacity saved as opaque. PhotoCraft now writes a private `pcAl` (0..1) key on the colour descriptor for fill, which Photoshop ignores. Stroke colour alpha is folded into `strokeStyleOpacity` because that field is the PSD-native stroke opacity.

Tests: `color_descriptor_keeps_photocraft_alpha`, `vstk_folds_color_alpha_into_stroke_opacity`.

included.head: 10fc2a3839d532a62a10d4cb36e95395e54f0fbe
included.title: Hue/Saturation: hue tracks and spectrum bars use full-strength sRGB hues, one shared hue_color (#6540)
included.body:
Closes #6540

The Hue track was pastel because `widgets::hue_stops` built its stops with `Hsva::new(h, 0.85, 1.0, 1.0).to_srgb()`: 0.85 saturation, and `Hsva` is linear, so every stop was washed out and hues bunched up. The Colorize spectrum bars had the same linear-light spacing.

- New `widgets::hue_color(deg)`: the fully saturated hue built on sRGB values with the existing `color_picker_ui::hsv_to_rgb` (0 is 255,0,0, 60 is 255,255,0, ...).
- `hue_stops` (Hue slider in Hue/Saturation, Camera Raw, Color panel) now uses it at full saturation.
- `adjust_editors.rs` drops its own linear `hue_color` and uses the shared one (Saturation track end, input spectrum bar). The adjusted spectrum bar now samples its input hues with `hsv_to_rgb` too, so both bars are spaced evenly by hue angle.
- `camera_raw_ui.rs` drops its second copy of `hue_color` (which capped channels at 220) and uses the shared one for the HSL band tracks.

The Lightness track is left alone; that is #6539.

Test: a new unit test in `widgets::tests` checks that the 13 stops have the track ends and the six 60-degree stops at exactly (255,0,0), (255,255,0), (0,255,0), (0,255,255), (0,0,255), (255,0,255), and that `hue_color` returns the same. On main the first stop is (255,125,108)-like pastel, so it fails.

included.head: 4c730d3889cfe4499077aa21e6a64bde1dc2e1a5
included.title: Object Finder: hovering with an empty active layer shows the status-bar hint (#6549)
included.body:
Fixes #6549.

With Object Finder on and Sample All Layers off, hovering over a spot where the active layer has no pixels (for example a new empty layer above the photo) showed nothing. The click already reports this as an error ("the active layer is empty; set sampleAllLayers..."), but the hover gave no reason.

Changes:

- `smartselect_cmds`: the check behind the click error moves into a public `empty_sampled_area(doc, layer, all_layers, area)`. `check_sampled_pixels` (the `select.object` click and rect paths) now calls it and returns the same error text as before.
- `object_finder::update`: before it looks for an object, it runs the same check on the pixel under the pointer. If the sampled layer has no pixels there, it starts no lookup and returns a hint: "The active layer has no pixels here — turn on Sample All Layers or select a layer with pixels".
- `object_finder::draw`: puts that hint in the status bar as a normal message, not an error. It clears the hint when the pointer moves to a spot that has pixels, and it never clears other status messages.
- The hint is translated in every complete catalog, so `every_tl_literal_is_translated` still passes. It uses each catalog's existing name for "Sample All Layers".
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: the Object Finder row describes the hint.

Nothing changes with Sample All Layers on, or when the active layer has pixels under the pointer.

Test: `hovering_an_empty_active_layer_gives_a_hint_not_silence` adds an empty layer over the disc document. The hover returns the hint, starts no lookup and shows no overlay. With Sample All Layers on, there is no hint and the disc is highlighted.

included.head: 76f19e6e2e48193bd13105e3da3e891ed4610f32
included.title: Title bar: only the primary button starts a window drag (#6729)
included.body:
Part of #6729 (the stuck middle-button drag).

The title bar's drag gap (`panels::title_bar`) and the overlay that keeps the gap draggable while a modal is open (`titlebar::modal_drag_overlay`) sent `ViewportCommand::StartDrag` on `drag_started()`, which is true for a drag with any mouse button. winit's `drag_window()` expects the left button to be down, so a middle-button drag on the gap (here from an AutoHotkey window-snap script) started a native move in a state the OS doesn't expect and the window got stuck.

Both now check `drag_started_by(PointerButton::Primary)`, the same check the edge resize zones (`resize_zones`) and the Linux caption-button drag (`caption_buttons`) in `titlebar.rs` already use. A left drag and a double-click on the gap work as before; a middle or right drag on the gap does nothing.

Not in this PR: the issue's second point, returning `HTCAPTION` from `WM_NCHITTEST` for the gap so external window tools see it as a native caption. That is a Windows-only window-procedure change, and the triage comment asks for it as its own ticket.

Test: `middle_button_drag_in_the_gap_does_not_start_a_window_drag` (`crates/ui-egui/src/titlebar.rs`) does a middle-button drag on the gap and checks that no `StartDrag` is sent, then an ordinary left drag, which sends one, then a middle drag again with a modal open (over the overlay). Without the fix the middle drags send `StartDrag`. The test helper `gesture_by` takes the button; the existing helpers still use the primary button.

included.head: 6511eed63db71ebd37aa2d4106925918c24ad9ae
included.title: Actions: Shift-click layer select in .atn imports as range select and exports back (#6784)
included.body:
Fixes #6784.

A recorded Shift-click on a layer is stored in `.atn` as `select` with `selectionModifier: addToSelectionContinuous`. The importer only knew `addToSelection` and `removeFromSelection`, so this fell through to a plain select, and a following Group Layers grouped one layer.

- `select_from`: `addToSelectionContinuous` now maps to `layer.select` with `mode: "range"` (the mode `layer.select` already supports for Shift-click in the Layers panel).
- `select_to`: `mode: "range"` now exports back as `addToSelectionContinuous`. Before, export refused it.
- Test: added a `range` case to `every_mapped_command_exports_and_imports_back`, next to the existing `add` case. Without the fix, the export returns nothing and the test fails.

included.head: ac5b4cd56f002e4c664ea8612886fecebfae12e4
included.title: Don't pan the canvas when a dialog's title bar is dragged (#6810)
included.body:
Fixes #6810.

With a dialog open, the canvas still pans under it (Hand tool, Space-drag, middle-drag). `dialogs::pan_delta` decided whether a drag is a canvas pan by checking that the press origin is outside every dialog rect. But when you drag a dialog by its title, the dialog follows the pointer, so after a few pixels the original press point is no longer inside the (moved) dialog. From then on the title-bar drag counted as a canvas drag and the image moved with the window.

Fix: `press_began_on_dialog` records, on the frame of the press, whether the press landed on a dialog, and keeps that answer until the next press. `pan_delta` ignores a held press that began on a dialog. `free_press` (canvas tools under a dialog: eyedroppers, Field Blur pins, Refine Edge brush, Layer Style shadow drag) uses the same check, so a dialog drag can't reach those tools either, e.g. when the pointer runs ahead of last frame's dialog rect during a fast drag.

Dragging the image itself on the free canvas (point 1 of the issue) works as before: a press that begins outside the dialogs still pans.

Test: `dragging_a_dialog_title_does_not_pan_the_canvas` presses on a dialog, then moves the dialog away from the press origin while the button is held, and checks that neither `pan_delta` nor `free_press` reports a canvas drag. Without the fix `pan_delta` returns the pointer movement.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Dragging a dialog no longer accidentally pans the canvas or activates the canvas tool, even if the dialog moves away from where the drag began. Canvas interactions that begin outside a dialog remain unchanged.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

included.head: ae0823efe41d5be9793d4bfe3548c70c487106a7
included.title: PSD: keep Photoshop 2026 Light adjustment layers verbatim and warn (#6542)
included.body:
Part of #6542.

## Cause
Photoshop 2026's Light adjustment layer is stored under the Brightness/Contrast `brit` key, with a `CgEd` descriptor holding more settings. `adjust_map::parse_any` read any `brit` + `CgEd` as Brightness/Contrast (only `Brgh`/`Cntr`), so Exposure, Highlights, Whites and Blacks were dropped with no warning (https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/io/src/adjust_map.rs#L207-L218).

## Fix
- `adjust_map::is_extended_brit`: if a `brit` layer's `CgEd` has keys outside the Brightness/Contrast set (`Vrsn Brgh Cntr means "Lab " useLegacy Auto presetKind presetFileName`), it now stays `Adjustment::Unsupported`. The PSD writer then keeps its `brit` and `CgEd` blocks byte for byte while the layer is unchanged.
- The import warns about the layer by name: "its Light settings could not be read (Light adjustments ... aren't supported yet); the layer is kept as saved but has no effect".

## Tests
`psd_export::tests::light_adjustment_is_kept_verbatim_and_warned`: a synthetic Light-style `brit` + `CgEd` layer goes through export, import (with the warning) and re-export, and both blocks come back byte-identical. A plain Brightness/Contrast `CgEd` is still read as Brightness/Contrast. The existing `adjust_map` tests and clippy pass.

## Not in this PR
- The Light adjustment itself (#6543). Until then the layer has no visible effect (warned).
- Detection rests on the `CgEd` having extra keys. I had no real Photoshop 2026 file, so the test descriptor's extra key names are placeholders. Someone with `largetest.psb` should confirm that the layer's `CgEd` holds the Light values (and not a separate block), then map its real keys for #6543. The corpus suite was not run.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Extended Light adjustments containing Exposure, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, or Blacks settings are now preserved when files are imported and exported, rather than being treated as standard Brightness/Contrast adjustments.
  * Warnings now identify these adjustments as Light and describe the unsupported settings. Plain Brightness/Contrast adjustments continue to be handled as before.

included.head: d5d937ac3eb0217e61f0bc76c7a2f0389a0a9fc2
included.title: A layer that doesn't fit in GPU memory no longer breaks GPU drawing: older pages are freed and the layer is retried
included.body:
Fixes #6563.

## Cause
`Compositor::sync` (`crates/gpu/src/lib.rs`) created each `pc_compose_layer` page texture with a bare `device.create_texture`. The new page's bytes weren't checked against the resident budget (eviction ran only after each cell), and an Out of Memory went uncaptured, so every later texture in the pass was invalid and the error reached the health watcher.

## Fix
- Before creating a page, `evict_residents` drops least recently used pages (never the current cell's, never the page being replaced) so its bytes fit the budget.
- Creation runs in the existing `first_error` error scopes on native. On Out of Memory every page the current cell doesn't use is dropped and creation is retried once.
- If it still fails, the cell draws nothing and the refresh returns `Unsupported(OVER_BUDGET)`: that refresh goes to the CPU and the next one tries the GPU again. The captured error no longer reaches the health callbacks, so it doesn't mark the device faulted. Turning *uncaptured* errors into non-permanent faults stays with #6564.
- WebGPU (wasm) reports errors asynchronously, so there creation is unscoped as before (pre-admission eviction still applies).
- `OVER_BUDGET` moves to `photocraft-gpu`; `ui-egui` re-exports it, so the existing GPU Memory Full notice shows for this case too.

## Tests
- New unit test `layer_pages_are_admitted_by_evicting_least_recently_used_first` covers the pure LRU admission function `lru_victims` (fit, partial eviction, zero budget, overflow). The existing post-cell `evict` now uses the same function.
- Not verified: a real driver OOM, and the full gpu/ui-egui test suites (only the new test was run locally).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * GPU rendering now recovers from layer-page memory pressure by evicting less recently used pages and retrying allocation.
  * When GPU memory remains insufficient, full refreshes fall back to the CPU compositor.
  * Layer pages can be evicted and re-uploaded as needed, including with a zero-page budget.
  * GPU results remain consistent with CPU rendering across repeated refreshes and document edits.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

included.head: 0750751261545077b36707cbf691c6f8f152dc17
included.title: Actions that start with Deselect play on when nothing is selected
included.body:
Fixes #6744 (the Deselect part).

## Cause
`select.deselect` is enabled only when there is a selection. Action playback runs each step through `Session::execute`, which checks that precondition first, so an action whose first step is Deselect stopped at step 1 with "no selection" whenever nothing was selected. In Photoshop, Deselect with nothing selected is a silent no-op during playback.

## Fix
- Action playback (`actions_cmds::run_recorded`) treats a Deselect step with an open document and no selection as done and plays on.
- `select.deselect`'s `run` returns `Ok` without touching the document or adding a history step when there is no selection (defensive; `enabled` is unchanged, so the menu item still greys out like Photoshop's).

## Tests
- `actions_cmds::tests::deselect_with_nothing_selected_is_a_noop_in_playback`: Deselect's `run` with no selection returns `Ok` and adds no history step; an action `[Deselect, New Layer]` plays both steps.

## Not in this PR
The other problems in #6744: the `layer.rasterize` step failing after a layer copy with no selection, and a playback mode that skips steps whose precondition does not apply.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Deselecting when no document or selection is active no longer creates an unnecessary history entry.
  * During action playback, a deselect step with no active selection is treated as successful, allowing subsequent actions to continue.
  * Deselecting an existing selection continues to clear it as expected.
  * Outside action playback, invalid deselection commands remain rejected.

included.title: feat(ui): System Info shows the graphics card's own memory
included.body:
Follow-up to #5234, as offered in its review.

Since #5234, a discrete card's own memory caps the GPU budgets, so a huge canvas can fall back to the reduced CPU canvas on a card with little memory. Nothing said why. System Info now shows the card's memory.

## Change

- `GpuInfo::lines()` adds **Graphics memory: {size}** after the driver line when the card reports its memory (`video_memory_mb`, from DXGI on Windows and amdgpu on Linux). It appears in both Help › System Info and Preferences › Performance › Graphics.
- The size uses the same compact format as #5973's "GPU memory budget" line (`chrome_ui::fmt_bytes`, e.g. `8.0G`), so the two lines compare directly.
- Integrated GPUs and cards that report nothing show no line: their textures share system memory, which the RAM-based budgets already cover.
- **Translations:** the new string is in all 20 catalogues, worded to match each catalogue's existing "GPU memory" term.

## Test

`system_info_shows_the_cards_memory`: with 8192 MB reported, the line `Graphics memory: 8.0G` follows `Driver: …`; with none, no such line appears and nothing else changes.

## Evidence

On `main` (`2a952f16`), Windows x86_64: `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings` pass. `ui-egui` lib tests: 2,960 passed, 0 failed (including the i18n catalogue tests).
