included.head: be98937e996e8a2f5be777d0deafd5186e82afc8
included.title: Polygonal Lasso: the last corner of a small shape no longer closes it (#6578)
included.body:
Fixes #6578

## Root cause

`polygon_click` (Polygonal Lasso) closed the outline whenever a click with at least three vertices placed landed within 8 screen points of the first vertex. When you draw a small rectangle, the fourth corner sits one side length from the first. If that side is shorter than 8 points, the click closed the polygon on the third vertex and the selection became a triangle. The Lasso's Alt-click polygonal mode (`lasso_ui.rs`) had the same fixed 8-point reach.

## Fix

Both tools now take their close reach from a new shared helper, `canvas::polygon_close_reach`. The reach is still 8 points on screen, but it is never more than a quarter of the outline's own on-screen size (and never less than 1 point). Outlines larger than 32 points keep exactly today's behaviour. On small shapes, the last corner adds a vertex, and a click on the first vertex (or a double-click) still closes the outline. Non-finite points are ignored.

## Tests

- `polygon_lasso_tests::the_last_corner_of_a_small_polygon_does_not_close_it` clicks the four corners of a 6x6 square at 100% zoom. It checks that the polygon stays open with 4 vertices, then that a click on the first vertex closes it as a square. The test fails without the fix ("four corners, still open").
- `polygon_lasso_tests::polygon_close_reach_scales_with_small_outlines_only` checks that large outlines keep the full 8-point reach at zoom 1 and 2, that small outlines get a smaller reach with a 1-point floor, and that NaN input falls back to 8.

## Commands

```
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- polygon lasso   # 48 passed
cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -- -D warnings
cargo fmt -p photocraft-ui-egui -- --check
cargo xtask layers
cargo xtask wasm
```

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Small Polygonal Lasso outlines now stay open when adding nearby corners, making it easier to draw them accurately. Clicking the starting point still closes the outline.
  * The closing threshold adjusts to the outline’s size, with a minimum of 1 screen point and a maximum of 8.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

included.head: d19399576270538c23400a1f0fcebda9abdcefcc
included.title: Add a curated pattern library: 38 CC0 photographic tiles
included.body: ## What The Patterns panel only had small procedurally generated tiles. This adds a curated library of 38 photographic pattern tiles built from CC0 ambientCG material scans, grouped like Photoshop's default folders: Brick & Tile, Concrete, Fabric, Foliage, Ground, Marble, Metal, Paper, Plants, Wood. Each tile is the material's Color (albedo) map, downscaled to 512x512 and embedded from crates/engine/assets/patterns/. The set is generated once and shared (a session clones the patterns, whose tiles are Arc). ## Licences and clean-room ambientCG releases its scans into the public domain under CC0 1.0 Universal, so the tiles are free to embed and redistribute. No Photoshop or other proprietary asset was used. Per-file sources are in crates/engine/assets/patterns/SOURCES.md, the licence ships as LICENSE-cc0.txt, and ATTRIBUTION.md and NOTICE carry the rows. ## Size The 38 tiles are about 3.8 MB (JPEG q92). They are native-only: on the web that would push the wasm past its per-file cap, so photographic() is empty under wasm32 and the procedural tiles are identical there. ## How it was tested - cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib — 1699 passed. - cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, the wasm32-unknown-unknown check — clean. - New tests: a photographic tile decodes at 512x512 with a real tonal range, and every built-in pattern is in exactly one group. - Manually in the app: opened Window > Patterns, checked the new folders and applied tiles through Layer > New Fill Layer > Pattern... at several scales. No new commands are added. ## Notes - This change was made with an AI coding agent. ## Screenshots ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Expanded the built-in pattern library with 38 photographic material tiles, including brick, concrete, fabric, foliage, marble, metal, paper, and wood. * Added material-based preset categories to make patterns easier to browse, alongside the existing geometric and texture categories. * **Documentation** * Added source and licensing information for the photographic pattern assets.

included.head: 289ad2bb3ed5d5cd6b47cf226cf2638aa600b86a
included.title: Canvas overlays stay visible while panning (#6592)
included.body:
Follows up #6592, which #6625 closed by keeping the transform box and the Pen path on screen during a pan. This PR does the same for every other canvas overlay (paths, guides, grid, crop, slice, gradient, artboard) and replaces #6625's special case with the general fix.

## Problem
The Pen path, finished or still being drawn, disappeared while you panned the canvas with Space. In fact *every* canvas overlay (paths, guides, grid, the transform box, crop/slice/gradient/artboard overlays) was skipped for as long as a Hand drag lasted: the Hand tool, Space or the middle mouse button. In `canvas_view` they were drawn under `if primary && !(hand_pan && response.dragged())`. This dates back to when the overlays sat in the `else` of the pan branch; #3610 had patched only the transform box.

## Fix
- Overlays always draw, so they move with the image during a pan, as in Photoshop.
- Only the tool-cursor chain is skipped while panning, so the fist cursor (#2196) is kept.
- The transform-only special case from #3610 is removed; the general fix covers it.

## Tests

included.title: Automation: resolve configured root aliases for absolute paths (#6426)
included.body:
Fixes #6426.

Automation roots were stored with `std::path::absolute` and matched as text. A root configured through a directory link or `..` could therefore reject the actual absolute location of a file inside its granted directory.

Resolve the trusted root once at startup and retain both its canonical and configured absolute spellings as names for the same held directory capability. Strip a matching component prefix, validate the remaining relative path, and keep every read, create and rename in cap-std. Windows ordinary/verbatim drive and UNC prefixes compare equivalently. Existing launch spellings, nonexistent output files and nested export directories keep working; request traversal, sibling prefixes, ungranted aliases and link escapes remain refused. Retargeting a launch-time link does not grant a new directory. Update the control-protocol documentation.

Initial validation on Windows/MSVC, Rust 1.95, at `567de6c7`:

- Full `cargo test --offline --locked --release -p photocraft-automation -- --test-threads=2`: 76 unit + 70 integration tests passed, 0 failed/ignored; all 12 integration targets ran, 0 doctests.
- Seven regression tests added: five shared Windows/Unix cases, a Windows drive/UNC/device-prefix case (no network access), and a Unix-only trusted-root-name case. The six Windows-applicable tests ran locally, including actual junctions; Unix symlink/name cases await CI.
- Initial reproducing workspace run before the fix: 19 passed / 4 failed with the expected outside-root rejection.
- Strict scoped Clippy (`-p photocraft-automation --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`), `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` passed. The wasm command checks the repository's wasm-safe set; automation itself is native-only.

Local resource profiles use workspace opt-level 1, dependency opt-level 0 and no release LTO (codegen-units 16). No dependency, Cargo.lock, engine command or format changes.

### Windows TEMP follow-up (`66a11952`)

Reproduced the two failures reported in review on the original PR head with a real Windows 8.3 TEMP: 23 workspace tests passed and the same two failed. The assertions used a third spelling of the target directory after granting access through a junction. They now read through the canonical target spelling. Production path handling and the held capability boundary are unchanged.

Added a Windows subprocess regression that runs both cases with TEMP through a junction, making the mismatch reproducible even when 8.3 names are disabled. It failed before the assertion fix and passes afterwards. TEMP/TMP are changed only in the child process. Added `crates/automation` to the CI platform selector so future automation changes also run native Windows test legs.

This follow-up changes tests and CI selection only; no dependencies or production filesystem code changed. New hosted CI is tracked on this head; the earlier successful run and approval apply to `567de6c7`.

The only content conflict was in the `app.open`/`app.save` documentation: keep upstream DDS compression/mipmap options together with this PR's canonical/configured-root path policy. included.head: 20385b70439b1fe2d5986218483e3c04ee32de0b
included.title: Type: commit the edit when another layer or document becomes active (#6483)
included.body:
Closes #6483.

The issue lists two symptoms, but they have one cause. While a type edit is open, the Type tool treats every key without ⌘/Ctrl as typing (Photoshop does the same). The edit never ended when you selected another layer, so tool shortcuts like V typed a letter instead. Once the edit ends, the shortcuts work again.

The reporter's build is 0.9.0. #5612 fixed the Layers-panel row click, but it merged a few hours after the `v0.9.0` tag. That fix covered only the row click: every other way of selecting a layer still left the edit open.

## Changes

1. **The edit ends when you move on.** `type_tool::end_if_left` runs every frame, next to the existing check that commits when you switch tools, and at the top of `handle_keys`. It commits the edit once its layer isn't the active layer, or its document isn't the active document. That covers:
   - layer and smart-object menu picks
   - the canvas layer picker
   - Select ▸ Deselect Layers
   - automation and MCP `layer.select`
   - document tabs
   - File ▸ New / Open
2. **Typing can no longer reach the wrong document.** `TextEdit` used to store only a layer id. `.pcraft` files keep their saved layer ids, so opening one file twice gives two documents with matching ids. After switching tabs, typing went into the other document's layer with the same id: a test saw `"Bee"` become `"BeZe"`. `TextEdit` now records its document (`document: Option<u64>`, serde default):
   - `commit_with` commits in that document, in its own history.
   - If that document has been closed, the edit is dropped without running anything.
   - `draw_overlay` draws nothing for an edit that belongs to another document.
3. **The layer you picked stays selected** (from review). Ending an empty Type Mask undoes its session, and the undo also restored the selection from before it. So the layer you had just picked (or Deselect Layers) was reversed. `end_if_left` now puts your selection back through a new `Session::restore_layer_selection`. That call drops layers that no longer exist and refuses an active layer that no longer exists. It isn't an edit, so a saved document stays saved.

The early commit from #5612 in `panels.rs` stays. It's still needed when you click the row of the layer you're already editing, because then the active layer doesn't change.

## Tests

- `crates/ui-egui/src/type_commit_tests.rs` (8 tests):
  - After a tab switch, typing leaves the other document untouched.
  - Selecting another layer commits the edit and names the new layer after its text.
  - An empty new type layer is deleted.
  - Deselect Layers commits the edit.
  - A Type Mask session isn't committed on its first frame.
  - Closing the edited document drops the edit without touching a layer with the same id elsewhere.
  - In the full window, V selects the Move tool after `layer.select`.
  - Ending a Type Mask (empty or with text, by selecting another layer or deselecting) keeps the new selection.

  The tab-switch, V-key and empty-Type-Mask tests failed before the fix.
- Engine: `restore_layer_selection_puts_back_what_still_exists`.
- Results: ui-egui lib 2967 passed, plus the integration tests. Engine lib and integration tests passed. Clippy (`-D warnings`), `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm` and fmt are clean. After rebasing on main, the type tests pass again (176).

## Not changed

⌥[ / ⌥] are still ignored while typing, as before; Photoshop's typing mode works the same way.

included.title: Fail control startup promptly when its port is occupied
included.body:
## Summary

Bind the control listener before GPU/display initialization, and pass the bound listener to the server. An occupied port now exits promptly with a useful diagnostic and status 2.

```text
control startup
  validate token and workspace
  bind 127.0.0.1:port → on failure: report error, exit 2
  initialize display/GPU
  start server with bound listener
```

Fixes #6428.

## Evidence

- **Before:** With its requested port held by another process, the desktop logged a bind error but remained running beyond a 10-second deadline.
  **After:** The rebuilt desktop exits promptly with status 2 and the bind diagnostic, without creating the GPU-startup marker.
- Added an occupied-port process regression with a bounded deadline, and a unit test that authenticates and dispatches through a prebound listener.
- Windows GNU: all 130 desktop unit tests and 5 startup integration tests passed. Strict all-target Clippy, formatting, layer checks, and all 24 WebAssembly checks passed for the combined local changes. Loopback tests ran outside the sandbox because it denies local socket access.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

No data-format or dependency changes; the startup ordering can be reverted.

**Blast Radius:** startup

Control-enabled launches now fail before display initialization when the requested listener cannot bind.

included.head: c8023bfed356148a2417f089f49bc50ec88f3316
included.title: perf(hdr): Merge to HDR Pro and HDR Toning 3× faster, bit for bit the same
included.body:
Merge to HDR Pro and HDR Toning spent most of their time on one core: serial per-pixel loops in `hdr::merge` and `hdr::tone_map`, serial box blurs in `fxutil`, and two tone-map methods with no parallelism at all. On 24 MP with 3 exposures, merge with ghost removal plus Local Adaptation now takes 944 ms instead of 2994 ms (3.2×), and every output is bit for bit the same.

### Fix
`crates/algo/src/fxutil.rs` (shared by box and Gaussian blurs):
- `box_rows_n` runs rows in parallel. `box_cols_n` cuts columns into 64-float bands, copies each band into a small buffer, blurs it there and writes it back, with no `unsafe`.
- `gauss_blur_n` runs its three passes together per row or band.
- Every column keeps the same f64 running sum, started and updated in the same order, so every caller (artistic filters, Reduce Noise, Iris and Tilt-Shift Blur, Oil Paint, Relight, Shadows/Highlights, HDR) gets identical output.

`crates/algo/src/hdr.rs`:
- `merge`:
  - The ghost threshold writes straight into the mask, so the score map is gone.
  - Sharpen, count and blend are one parallel pass, and the three channel scalings are one pass.
  - The three response curves are solved in parallel.
  - The scale median and the stops percentiles use `select_nth_unstable_by(total_cmp)`. That picks the same elements a full sort would, because elements that tie under `total_cmp` have the same bits.
  - `g_at` truncates instead of calling libm `floor`. Its input is clamped to 0..=255, so the two agree, and NaN gives 0 in both.
- `tone_map`:
  - Every per-pixel loop is parallel.
  - The log-mean computes its `ln` terms in parallel, then adds them strictly in pixel order, so the sum keeps every bit.
  - Equalize Histogram uses per-chunk integer histograms.
  - Exposure/Gamma no longer computes a log-mean it never used.

`crates/algo/src/tone.rs` (`hdr_toning`):
- The alpha count is parallel, and the mean is branch-free with the same order of additions.

Left serial on purpose: the f32 mean in `hdr_toning` and the final add of the f64 log-mean. Each must keep its order to keep every bit, and each is one chain of about 25 ms at 24 MP.

### Numbers
24 MP, 3 exposures, release build, median of 5 runs, before and after interleaved. Intel Core Ultra X7 358H (16 threads), Linux. A long C++ build was running at the same time (load average 10 to 17), so absolute times are high, but before and after ran under the same load.

| Step | Before | After | Speed-up | 1 thread before | 1 thread after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Merge, ghost removal | 1432 ms | 511 ms | 2.8× | 4744 ms | 3366 ms |
| Merge, no ghost removal | 682 ms | 341 ms | 2.0× | 2725 ms | 2074 ms |
| Tone map: Local Adaptation | 1562 ms | 433 ms | 3.6× | 2441 ms | 2094 ms |
| Tone map: Exposure and Gamma | 1268 ms | 180 ms | 7.1× | 1459 ms | 1195 ms |
| Tone map: Highlight Compression | 763 ms | 156 ms | 4.9× | 764 ms | 776 ms |
| Tone map: Equalize Histogram | 1707 ms | 217 ms | 7.9× | 1722 ms | 1615 ms |
| HDR Toning | 855 ms | 248 ms | 3.4× | 1809 ms | 1445 ms |
| Shadows/Highlights (also uses fxutil) | 3395 ms | 2679 ms | 1.3× | 4927 ms | 4739 ms |

A Gaussian blur alone (sigma 9, 2000×1500) goes from 49 ms to 5.4 ms, and from 54 ms to 25 ms on one thread, because the column bands stay in cache. Peak memory for merge with ghost removal goes from 1.69 GB to 1.64 GB (the inputs alone are 1.13 GB).

### Tests
- Old code against new: all 316 output hashes match.
  - Image sets: 24 MP, 97×61, 513×300, 1×1000, 1000×1 and 1×1.
  - Merge with and without ghost removal, at base exposure 0 and 2.
  - Every tone-map method with default and non-default settings, plus all-transparent and all-opaque inputs.
  - HDR Toning and Shadows/Highlights.
  - A box-blur sweep: widths 1–70 and 95–257, 1–5 channels, radii 0 to 1000, and empty shapes.
- New unit tests keep the old serial `box_rows_n`/`box_cols_n`, `merge` and `tone_map` as references, and compare against them bit for bit across band and chunk boundaries. They also check hashes recorded from the old code. The hashes for merge, tone map and HDR Toning go through the platform's `ln`, `exp` and `powf`, so they run on Linux x86-64 only; the reference comparisons run everywhere.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-algo --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p photocraft-algo --locked` (564 passed; includes the Iris, Tilt-Shift, Reduce Noise, Oil Paint and Relight tests), the engine's HDR tests, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` all pass.

included.title: fix(ui): preserve shape stroke settings at zero width
included.body:
Fixes #6191.

## Summary

Changing a selected shape's stroke width through **4 px → 0 px → 4 px** currently discards its paint and style. Keep the existing stroke in the document and update only its width in both the options bar and Properties:

```diff
- 0 px → remove the stroke → rebuild from defaults
+ 0 px → retain the stroke → restore the original style when width increases
```

- Preserve color/alpha, opacity, alignment, caps, joins, miter limit and dash settings, including a native save/reopen at zero width.
- Keep explicit **No Color** removal and deliberate 3 px activation from color/style choices. Opening or dismissing Stroke Options alone does not enable a zero-width stroke.
- Use the existing Properties gesture convention for options-bar undo keys: one history step per drag, with separate numeric edits undoable independently.

Related: #6259. This alternative retains the original `ShapeStroke` in the document model and covers both width controls, rather than reconstructing a removed stroke from tool defaults.

## Evidence

**Before:** the actual-widget regression failed twice because setting width to zero changed the stroke to `None`.

**After:** both new regressions pass. They exercise 8/16/32-bit documents, Properties and Rectangle/Path Selection/Direct Selection options, exact style preservation, invisible zero-width rendering, native persistence, undo/redo, No Color and deliberate re-enabling.

```sh
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib vector_ui::paint_tests::zero_width
```

The screenshots use the Properties width field for **12 px → 0 px → 12 px**. The original resets to black/Solid; the fix retains the blue/Custom dashed stroke.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: stroke resets to black Solid](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/denstu473/photocraft/80a4eec4eff73c45f59f87f8e8edbba3be981bab/.pr-evidence/6191/before.png) | ![After: blue Custom stroke is retained](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/denstu473/photocraft/80a4eec4eff73c45f59f87f8e8edbba3be981bab/.pr-evidence/6191/after.png) |

Validation:
- **Rebased onto `58f855a4`:** both regressions pass; the UI unit suite passes (2,960 passed, 13 ignored); formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Broader validation before rebase (`4e7a17cd`):** 2,930 unit tests passed (13 ignored), all 26 integration targets passed (109 tests), and doctests passed. Strict all-target Clippy (`-D warnings`), dependency layers (30 crates), and all 24 wasm checks passed.
- Inspected 28 captures covering all 14 themes at 1440×900 and 1000×700.
- Native validation used Windows GNU and the software GPU adapter. The original parallel integration run encountered a WARP access violation in `checker_canvas`; all integration targets then passed with `--test-threads=1`. That unrelated test is outside this patch.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way. Reversible UI change using the existing document model and native format; no schema migration or dependency changes.

**Blast Radius:** Shapes. Selected-shape stroke controls and options-bar edit coalescing.

included.title: fix(photocraft): `--control 0` logs the port actually bound (#6427)
included.body:
Fixes #6427.

Port 0 is accepted on purpose, so the OS picks a free port. But `control_server::start` printed the requested port, so the log said `listening on 127.0.0.1:0` and a client had no way to find the server.

**Not in this PR:** the issue's optional extra, writing the bound port somewhere machine-readable (e.g. next to the token file). It could be a follow-up.

included.head: abd3755d41d92906a18a1418ca10f55d9a9eb6ea
included.title: Survive a lost window GPU device: draw nothing, save unsaved work for recovery, close (#3438, #1215)
included.body:
Fixes #3438. Fixes #1215 (the egui-wgpu "Failed to create staging buffer for index data" panic).

## What was wrong

The window can lose its own wgpu device, for example through a driver reset after the PC slept, or the OS killing a submission. After that, egui-wgpu can't draw another frame, and PhotoCraft never handled it. Depending on which egui-wgpu path meets the dead device first, the user gets one of two failures:

- **A crash.** A frame with shapes panics inside egui-wgpu (`renderer.rs:984`, "Failed to create staging buffer for index data"). The app exits with code 101 and unsaved work is lost (#1215). I reproduced this on an RX 6900 XT, on both Vulkan and DX12, by destroying the device in a running app.
- **A freeze that X can't close.** Frames that can't be presented are dropped ("Dropped frame with error: Validation"), so the window freezes. The close button then opens the unsaved-changes prompt, which the dead window can't draw. That's #3438's "unresponsive, and X won't close it". I reproduced it by keeping the frames empty after the loss: the app kept running, and `ui.inspect` showed the `discard` prompt open for `file.exit`.

Why the existing handling and tests missed it:
- The device-loss handling from #243 moves only the *document canvas* to the CPU.
- `ui.gpu.simulateLoss` only marks the health flag, so no test ever ran a frame on a really lost device.

## Change

- **`photocraft-gpu`:**
  - `DeviceHealth::device_lost()`: true only when wgpu itself reports the device lost (its callback, or a panicking poll), unlike a recorded fault.
  - `DeviceHealth::probe()`: a non-blocking poll that keeps running after a recorded fault.
- **`photocraft-format`:** `RecoveryStore::flush()` finishes queued autosaves and waits for them.
- **`photocraft-ui-egui`:**
  - The app keeps the window's device and its health flag: the GPU canvas's, or one from `watch_window_device` for the CPU canvas.
  - `gpu_status::check_window` runs at the end of every frame and probes the device. Once the device is lost, the frame draws nothing (the egui graphics are cleared), so egui-wgpu has nothing to upload.
  - The first time it sees the loss, it queues every unsaved document for crash recovery (whatever the autosave timer says), waits for the writes via `Services::flush_autosaves`, and closes the app without the prompt. The next launch reopens the documents ("Recovered …").
  - `ui.gpu.simulateLoss {destroy: true}` destroys the real device, so this path can be driven from the control channel.
- **`photocraft` (app):**
  - `flush_autosaves` is backed by `RecoveryStore::flush`.
  - The CPU-canvas path now watches the window's device instead of discarding its health flag.
- **Docs:** `docs/development.md` (device loss) and `docs/control-protocol.md`.

## Tests

- **`gpu_device_loss::a_lost_window_device_saves_unsaved_work_for_recovery_and_closes`** (ui-egui; runs on any adapter, WARP and llvmpipe included):
  - It runs the real eframe frame loop, makes a document dirty, destroys the device, then uploads the last frame through egui-wgpu's `Renderer::update_buffers`.
  - **Without the frame clearing, it panics with #1215's message and fails** (`left: (141, false)`).
  - With it, there's nothing to upload, the document was autosaved and flushed exactly once, and the app is closing.
- **`device_loss::only_wgpu_reports_a_real_device_loss`** (gpu).
- **`autosave::flush_writes_every_queued_autosave_before_returning`** (format).

## Evidence

Windows 11, RX 6900 XT, main `3cb3580a`. Destroying the window's device in the running app:

| Backend | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Vulkan | exit 101, egui-wgpu panic, unsaved stroke lost | exit 0, recovery entry written, next launch shows "Recovered Lost Device Test" |
| DX12 | exit 101, egui-wgpu panic, unsaved stroke lost | exit 0, recovery entry written, next launch shows "Recovered Lost Device Test" |

- **Checks:** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (gpu, format, ui-egui, photocraft) and `cargo xtask layers` all pass.
- **Tests:** `cargo test --lib --tests --bins` on those crates: 43 test binaries; 3,404 passed, 1 failed, 13 ignored. The failure is `canvas_mips_preserve_opaque_pixels_and_partial_updates`, the AMD-on-Vulkan mip corruption from #6418 (fixed by #6438). It fails the same way on `main` on this card and is unrelated to this change.
- **Rebased onto `6368e6a8`** (current main, which includes #5973): fmt and clippy are clean again, and the device-loss tests (gpu, ui-egui), the format autosave tests and the app's tests all pass.

Not verified:
- **A real sleep/resume on this machine.** Whether a driver reports a loss on resume depends on the driver.
- **The timing of a real loss.** On a real driver loss, wgpu calls the lost callback immediately (`lose()`). `destroy()` instead waits for the queue to empty, which is why the test waits for the device to go idle.

## For review

- **The app closes on its own after a loss.** Alternatives would be a native message box first (PhotoCraft has none today), or having the app restart itself, which needs care with `--control` ports. I'm happy to add either.
- **The recovery save ignores the Autosave preference.** `recover_on_launch` still decides whether the next launch reopens the documents.
- **`probe` adds one non-blocking `device.poll` per frame.**

included.head: 6cef19e38a13d70c31b4f75453f68e683fc02f71
included.title: perf(quantize): Indexed Color palette build 8× faster, bit for bit the same
included.body:
Image › Mode › Indexed Color and Save for Web build their Perceptual, Selective and Adaptive palettes on one core, and a 24 MP photo took 4 to 5 s (14 s on a noisy image). This makes it about 8× faster, and every palette comes out bit for bit the same.

### Root cause
- `median_cut` re-measured the extent and weight of **every** box on every split, though only the two new boxes change. With up to 256 boxes over millions of points, that was most of the time.
- Each split sorted with a comparison `sort_by`.
- `histogram()` did a SipHash `HashMap` insert per pixel, and the k-means nearest-centre search was serial.

### Fix (all in `crates/algo/src/quantize.rs`)
- `median_cut` caches each box's (axis, score) in lockstep with `boxes` (same `swap_remove` and pushes) and scores only the two new boxes, with the same expressions, so the box chosen at each step is unchanged.
- Boxes of 256 or more points sort with a stable LSD radix sort on a key whose unsigned order is exactly `f32::total_cmp` order. Stable like `sort_by`, so ties keep their order. Smaller boxes keep `sort_by`.
- `histogram()` packs opaque pixels into one `u32` each, `par_sort_unstable`s them and counts the runs (integer counts, so the order of work cannot change the result; no per-thread tables).
- k-means finds the nearest centre for every point in parallel, then adds the f64 sums **sequentially in the original order**, so float rounding is unchanged. The Lab conversion of the histogram is a parallel map that keeps order.
- `to8` drops the per-channel `roundf` call: truncate, then add one when the exact remainder is at least 0.5 (same as `f32::round` on 0..=255, NaN gives 0 in both).
- wasm keeps the serial paths, following the `cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")` pattern `liquify.rs` uses.

### Numbers
Release build, 256 colours, median of 5 runs, Intel Core Ultra X7 358H (16 threads), Linux. Synthetic 24 MP images: a photo-like one (4.2 M unique colours) and a noisy one.

| Case | Before | After | Speed-up | 1 thread before | 1 thread after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Photo, Perceptual | 5068 ms | 601 ms | 8.4× | 4841 ms | 1651 ms |
| Photo, Adaptive | 4044 ms | 608 ms | 6.7× | 3859 ms | 1251 ms |
| Photo, Selective | 4862 ms | 617 ms | 7.9× | 4720 ms | 1716 ms |
| Noisy, Perceptual | 14124 ms | 1643 ms | 8.6× | 13726 ms | 4018 ms |
| Noisy, Adaptive | 10891 ms | 1485 ms | 7.3× | 10600 ms | 2701 ms |

Peak memory goes down too (the HashMap is gone): photo Perceptual 802 → 644 MB, noisy Perceptual 1667 → 1151 MB (both include the 384 MB test image).

### Tests
- Bit-exactness, old against new build: 120 palette hashes match (Adaptive, Perceptual, Selective and Exact at 256, 64 and 16 colours, Forced none and Black and White, on 5 images: the two 24 MP ones, one with fewer colours than requested, one with 300 colours, one semi-transparent). A further 240 match for 2, 3, 8, 12 and 100 colours with every Forced option on the small images.
- New unit tests: palettes recorded from the old code (5 cases, hard-coded); the old `median_cut` and k-means kept as reference oracles and compared bit for bit on tie-heavy data; the radix sort against stable `sort_by`, including NaN, ±infinity and -0.0; a histogram test; `to8` against `round` on every half-way point and its neighbours, plus an `#[ignore]`d exhaustive check over all 2^32 floats (about 1 s in release; passes).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-algo --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p photocraft-algo --locked` (562 passed), `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`: all pass.

included.title: Context menus: an overflowing menu shows ▲/▼ scroll arrows (#2091)
included.body:
Fixes #2091 (the remaining part).

`widgets::menu_scroll` already caps right-click menus (the layer's, the canvas tools', …) at the visible window height and scrolls them. As the reporter pointed out, the only cue was egui's thin floating scroll bar, which is invisible until hovered, so nothing showed that more items were hidden.

- clicking an arrow jumps 200 pt;
- an arrow dims at its end of the list.

Menus that fit are unchanged. All 10 callers get this through the shared helper.

**Test.** `overflowing_menus_get_scroll_arrows_that_scroll_on_hover` (kittest): a 3-item menu shows no arrows, an 80-item menu in a 300 pt window overflows, and hovering the lower arrow scrolls it down.

included.head: 562601eb476f492f7245945751cba47a57420a48
included.title: Save for Web: Width, Height, Percent and Resample in Image Size, linked in proportion (#6388)
included.body:
Save for Web: set the export's Width and Height (linked in proportion), Percent and the resampling method.

In Photoshop, Save for Web's Image Size has Width and Height linked by a chain, a Percent field and a Quality menu for the resampling method. Before this PR, PhotoCraft only had Percent plus a read-only "W: H:" line. The export command already accepted `width`, `height`, `percent` and `resample`, so this change is only in the dialog. A typed width or height sets the other side from the document's aspect while Constrain proportions is on (the default each time the dialog opens). Percent sets both sides. Turning Constrain proportions back on sets the height again from the width in the document's proportions. Resample offers Photoshop's list: Nearest Neighbor, Bilinear, Bicubic, Bicubic Smoother, Bicubic Sharper. It defaults to Bicubic, the engine's current default. I labelled it "Resample" rather than "Quality" so it doesn't clash with the JPEG Quality field. Happy to switch both the default and the label. As #1857 decided, each opening starts at the document's full size; the resample method is remembered with the other encoding choices. When the preview proxy is full size (2048 px or less), it now uses the chosen method, so the preview, colour table and size estimate show it. The document itself is never resized. The size helpers are reused from Export As (`resize_from_side`, `resize_from_scale`).

Part of #6388: this covers point 1 only. Dropping "Legacy" from the name and adding new formats stay out. Possible follow-ups in the engine, untouched here: `file.export.saveForWebLegacy` passes any `resample` through to Image Size, and `"none"` exports without resizing. The `.atn` mapping also doesn't read Save for Web's resize.

Validation:
- `save_for_web_width_keeps_proportions_and_sizes_the_file`: fails on main (no Width field in the dialog), passes here. Typing 60 px on a 120 × 80 document gives a height of 40. Unlinked, a height of 50 stays; linked again, it goes back to 40. The file comes out at 60 × 40, and the document's revision and size are unchanged.
- `save_for_web_reopens_at_full_size_with_the_resample_method`: fails on main (no Width field), passes here. Reopened on a 240 × 160 document, the dialog is back at 240 × 160 and keeps `nearest`.
- Mutations checked: with the proportion lock ignored, the first test fails (height stays 80); without the re-link step, it fails too (height stays 50); carrying width/height across openings makes the second fail.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- save_for_web web_preview` (13 passed), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (clean for the changed files; it reports `crates/automation/tests/smart_filter_authorization.rs`, untouched and the same on main)
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

included.head: 7e7defd0fb2649061353d105155b58c635a22a40
included.title: Artboards: layers outside the boards stay visible over the pasteboard (#5712)
included.body:
Fixes #5712.

**Cause.** In a document with artboards, `canvas.rs` paints the pasteboard (the grey/dotted area between boards) *on top of* the composited image, over every canvas rect that isn't inside a board (`artboard_ui::pasteboard_rects`). Drawing a new artboard next to existing work puts that work outside every board, so it gets covered: "my original work just disappears, it's still there if I hover over layers". Photoshop shows layers that aren't in an artboard.

**Fix.** `pasteboard_rects` now subtracts the composite bounds (`photocraft_compose::composite_bounds`) of every visible top-level layer that isn't an artboard. The document's Background, and any layer whose bounds are unbounded (e.g. a fill layer) or cover the whole canvas, count as backdrop rather than loose work, so they keep the pasteboard. Boards still get their pasteboard between them as before.

**Tests.** New `layers_outside_the_boards_show_over_the_pasteboard` (a 20×20 loose pixel layer beside a board is not covered), `full_canvas_layers_keep_the_pasteboard` (the default white Background plus a full-canvas pixel layer leave the pasteboard intact) and `subtract_splits_around_holes`. The existing pasteboard test runs on the default white document again. `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib artboard_ui` passes (8).

included.head: 5fe57626a6c6d9ad8bba75148031cd13e6b86442
included.title: CI: ready for a merge queue: merge_group trigger and one required `ci passed` check (#6400)
included.body:
**TL;DR:** gets CI ready for a GitHub merge queue. After this merges and a maintainer changes the settings below, merging is one click: GitHub merges the PR once CI passes on top of the latest main, and nobody has to wait for the run.

Fixes #6400. Also does the "one required check" part of #5118.

## What changes in `ci.yml`

- **`merge_group:` trigger.** The queue tests each queued PR on a temporary branch (main plus the PRs queued ahead of it). Without this trigger a queued PR waits for its check forever.
- **New `ci passed` job.** It always runs last and reports red if any job failed or was cancelled, green if every job passed or was skipped. It waits for every job, including the Windows legs, `test (windows-latest)` (the gate job main added when Windows was split into two legs) and the Linux test variants. This is the one check to require: a required check that never starts stays "Expected" forever, and the per-job checks only cover part of CI (the gate job doesn't see corpus, wasm or web).
- **Merge groups choose platforms the way PRs do.** The queue starts one CI run per queued PR (see the [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue)), so a full Linux + Windows + web run for each one would double the load on the runners. Windows and web run when the group changes paths that need them; `main` still always runs everything.

Nothing changes until the ruleset below is on. Until then `merge_group` never fires and `ci passed` is just one more green check.

## What maintainers need to change (after merging this PR)

Order matters: merge this PR first. `ci passed` has to have reported once before it can be picked as a required check, and the queue needs the `merge_group` trigger.

**Settings › Rules › Rulesets › New ruleset › New branch ruleset**

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Ruleset name | `main` |
| Enforcement status | Active |
| Bypass list | Repository admin (for emergencies; leave everyone else out) |
| Target branches | Add target › Include default branch |
| **Require status checks to pass** | on, add check `ci passed` (source: GitHub Actions) |
| └ Require branches to be up to date before merging | **off** (the queue already tests against the latest main) |
| **Require merge queue** | on |
| └ Merge method | Squash (what main uses today) |
| └ Build concurrency | 3 (each entry is a full CI run; the runners are the bottleneck, see #5543) |
| └ Minimum / maximum pull requests to merge | 1 / 5 |
| └ Wait time to meet minimum group size | 5 minutes |
| └ Only merge non-failing pull requests | on |
| └ Status check timeout | 150 minutes (a run takes about 50–70 minutes, plus time waiting for a runner) |
| Restrict deletions, Block force pushes | on (defaults) |

**How merging works afterwards**

- On a PR, the button becomes **Merge when ready**: click it, and the PR joins the queue and merges by itself when its run is green. If the run fails, it drops out of the queue with the failure shown on the PR.
- CLI and AI mergers: `gh pr merge <number>` adds the PR to the queue (no `--squash`/`--merge` needed). Don't use `--admin` routinely, because it bypasses the queue.
- To turn it off again: set the ruleset's enforcement to Disabled.

## Trade-offs

- The queue adds one CI run per merged PR on top of the PR's own runs. In exchange, nobody has to merge main into a branch just to re-check it, and main stops breaking from untested combinations. Build concurrency limits how much it can take from the runners at once.
- `main` still runs full CI after each merge, because only main's runs save the build cache that PR and queue runs restore.

## Testing

- The workflow parses, and `merge_group` sits next to `push`, `pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch`.
- The platform-selection script, run locally for `merge_group`, `pull_request`, `push` and `workflow_dispatch` with a small and a large diff: merge groups and PRs pick Linux only, or Linux + Windows depending on paths; push and manual runs pick everything.
- The `ci passed` logic, checked with sample job results: all success → green; success + skipped → green; any failure → red; any cancelled → red; failed `platforms` with skipped dependents → red.
- This PR's own CI run exercises `ci passed` for real. The `merge_group` path can only run once the queue is on.

included.head: 1f374b6964e47ecc671742e026901803b35fa40a
included.title: PSD smart filters: Sharpen, Dust & Scratches and Hue/Saturation stay editable (#6267)
included.body:
Fixes #6267.

**Cause.** `crates/io/src/smart_map.rs` had no mapping for these three Photoshop smart filters, so they imported as `psd.unsupportedFilter`. The stored composite showed them, but any re-render of the smart object (Replace Contents, Relink) dropped them.

**Fix.** New `KNOWN` entries and param mappings, both directions:
- **Sharpen** (`Shrp`): Photoshop stores no `Fltr`, only the name and `filterID`, so it is matched by `filterID` and written back with `hasoptions` false.
- **Dust & Scratches** (`DstS`): `Rds ` / `Thsh` ↔ `radius` / `threshold`.
- **Hue/Saturation** (`HStr`): `Clrz` plus `Adjs` `Hst2` entries (`H   `/`Strt`/`Lght`, and `LclR` with `BgnR`/`BgnS`/`EndS`/`EndR` for the six colour ranges) ↔ the `image.adjustments.hueSaturation` params. A range without bounds is written with Photoshop's defaults. `Hue ` is accepted on import too.

**Tests.** The known-filters round-trip test covers all three. A new test imports Photoshop's settings-less Sharpen item and checks that malformed Hue/Saturation and Dust & Scratches data fail cleanly. `cargo test -p photocraft-io --lib smart_map` passes and clippy is clean.

included.head: 8bfbbf816025942b74130adf16fb07265817b691
included.title: Video Frames to Layers: every page of a multi-page TIFF (part of #6379)
included.body:
Part of #6379 (the multi-page TIFF part).

File › Import › Video Frames to Layers loads every frame of an animated GIF as its own layer, but a multi-page TIFF gave only its first page. `load_frames` (also behind Layer › Video Layers › New Video Layer from File) now takes every full-resolution page of a TIFF's main IFD chain, in file order, one layer (or frame) each:

- `tiff_pages` lists the pages through `codecs::tiff_info`: main-chain directories (`parent: None`) of kind `TiffPageKind::Page`. Thumbnails and other reduced-resolution copies, transparency masks and SubIFDs are left out.
- Each page opens through `io::import_tiff_page`, so its orientation is applied and a page with Photoshop layer data contributes its composite, as when that page is opened.
- A TIFF with one page goes through the usual import as before.

The change sits next to the GIF branch in `load_frames`. @LloydNicholson's #5635 (animated WebP) changes the same function; the two merge without a conflict in `video_cmds.rs`, and the new test sits apart from #5635's tests.

APNG frames and an option to open frames or pages straight away as layers (the rest of #6379) aren't part of this.

Test: `video_cmds::tests::video_frames_to_layers_takes_every_tiff_page` writes a TIFF with a thumbnail and two pages of different sizes and grey levels: Video Frames to Layers gives exactly two layers, "Frame 1" 6×4 and "Frame 2" 3×5, with each page's grey, and a single-page TIFF still gives one layer. It fails on main (one layer). The other `video_cmds` tests pass (30).

included.head: 74aadae69e3b3f5cd257bca1926acc1b1297b1a2
included.title: Windows releases ship a symbols zip: the release build's PDBs for profilers (#688)
included.body:
Fixes #688.

Windows releases ship no PDBs, so a profile of the installed PhotoCraft (WPA, Superluminal) shows addresses instead of function names, and a PDB from a local rebuild of the same commit doesn't match the published exes. The release build already writes `photocraft.pdb` and `photocraft_cli.pdb` (the exes record them by bare file name), they just weren't packaged.

## Change
- `packaging/windows/package.ps1`: after the portable zip, copies both PDBs from the release build into `photocraft-<v>-windows-<arch>-symbols.zip` in `dist/release`, plus `symbols.txt`. It fails the packaging step if a PDB is missing rather than shipping a partial zip. Signing doesn't change the PDB signature an exe records, so the PDBs match the signed exes. The shared release workflow (`craft-common-actions` `release.yml` → `draft-release`) uploads everything in `dist/release` and adds it to `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so no workflow change is needed.
- `packaging/windows/symbols.txt` (new): which binaries they match, and how to load them (copy next to the exe, or add the folder in WPA / Superluminal / Visual Studio / `_NT_SYMBOL_PATH`).
- `docs/releasing.md`: the asset table and a short "Symbols zip" note.

The release profile has `debug = 0`, so these PDBs carry function names but no source line tables. That is what function-level flame graphs need. Line tables (`CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=line-tables-only` for the Windows build) could follow if maintainers want them; I left the build settings alone. The PDB from my local release build is about 9.8 MB (2.3 MB zipped). macOS dSYMs and Linux debug files would be follow-ups in their own packaging scripts.

## Tests
There's no test harness for the packaging scripts. I ran these locally:
- PowerShell's parser on `package.ps1`: 0 errors.
- The new block on its own against a local `target/release`: it copied `photocraft.pdb` and `symbols.txt` and zipped them. It threw the intended error for the missing `photocraft_cli.pdb`, since I had only built the app.
- Checked that a release `photocraft.exe` records its PDB as just `photocraft.pdb`, so the shipped file names resolve.

I haven't run the full `package.ps1` (it needs WiX and signing). The release workflow will exercise it.

included.head: 1d21c921f8bed94876f1e9289b0eb9566e5c5107
included.title: Make brush cursors follow pen orientation and projection
included.body:
Pen tilt and barrel rotation changed the painted brush orientation while its cursor kept the static tip orientation. Apply the shared paint angle controller and pose overrides to the cached outline before the canvas view transform, and show Brush Projection foreshortening.

Fixes #5428. Addresses the pen-orientation example in #6350. This does not preview every pressure, jitter or stroke-direction dynamic.

Verified source: 6b9fc995 on upstream 2b3d0563.

- [Baseline regression](https://github.com/jonathanwxh-cell/photocraft/actions/runs/38817773811): simulated pen tilt leaves the old native cursor bitmap unchanged; the workflow requires that exact assertion failure.
- [Candidate cloud verification](https://github.com/jonathanwxh-cell/photocraft/actions/runs/38821241859): full UI library 2,960 passed, 0 failed, 14 ignored, plus UI integration tests; formatting, strict UI Clippy, layers and WASM passed. Focused cursor tests overlap the full suite and are not added to its count. Software Vulkan was required.
- Cursor tests compare rotation against both an emitted dab angle and a static 90-degree cursor reference, and cover projection, mouse/disabled dynamics, pose overrides, view transforms and outline-cache reuse. Inspected all six exported cursor PNGs: tilt/barrel rotation turn the flattened tip, and projection foreshortens the round tip.
- Release component probe, five samples of 360 updates: changing rotation took 61.7–62.7 microseconds/update; cached static cursor took 0.44–0.47 microseconds after its first 2.32-microsecond sample. This measures cursor generation, not physical tablet or end-to-end latency; it is added work, not a speedup.

The earlier verification attempt lacked a graphics adapter and failed five UI tests. The linked complete run installs Mesa, requires Vulkan, and passes those tests. No production change was needed for that environment failure.

Credit: jonathnwxh. Implemented and verified with OpenAI Codex assistance. No physical tablet testing claimed.

included.head: f343abda5d6278cd49c3d3d8a3436dd2c7c729a0
included.title: New Document: Color Profile, the working space or another profile of the mode (#321)
included.body:
Addresses point 1 of #321 ("I expected to set working space per document on document creation"). It's Photoshop's New Document › Advanced Options › Color Profile.

## Change
- **Engine** (`file.new`): new optional `profile` param: `"working"` (default, unchanged behaviour), a built-in id, or a path to an .icc file. It's resolved with `ColorState::resolve` and must match the mode's colour space (`mode_space`). Both checks run before the document opens, so a bad profile opens nothing. `validate_new_params` accepts the key, and the params doc lists it.
- **New Document dialog** (`new_doc_ui.rs`): a **Color Profile** menu under Color Mode. It lists "Working: <profile>" first, then the built-in and installed profiles of the mode's space. Changing the mode drops a profile chosen for the old space. Both labels reuse strings that are already translated in every catalog.

The other points in #321, with my notes:
- (2) The document's profile can already be shown in the status bar (its Show menu › Document Profile).
- (3) View transforms are #564 (OCIO).
- (4) Color Settings, Assign Profile and Convert to Profile sit in the Edit menu in Photoshop too, so they stay there for parity.

included.head: a5e7e6387d09908aa946ede188c60e61a247e4af
included.title: fix(io): open DDS textures with their alpha as an Alpha 1 channel
included.body:
what happens: a DDS with an alpha channel opens fully transparent. for the
reported DXT5 AO map every one of the 262,144 alpha values is zero, so the
canvas is blank although the RGB data is intact.

root cause: `import_flat` in `crates/io/src/flat.rs` kept the decoded alpha as
layer transparency for every flat format except Targa, which #2225
special-cased (`tga_alpha_to_channel`): a 32-bit TGA opens as a locked opaque
"Background" layer with the fourth byte preserved as an "Alpha 1" channel.
DDS was the remaining format with the old behavior.

the fix: DDS takes the same path as Targa. a DDS with an alpha channel now
opens as a locked opaque "Background" layer plus an "Alpha 1" document channel
holding the original alpha — the same default as Photoshop's DDS import with
"Load Transparency" unchecked. nothing is discarded.

| | before (5f9190f8) | after (a5e7e638) |
|---|---|---|
| repro file | `ext_caliper_AO MAP.dds`, 512×512 legacy DXT5, sha256 `5f420282018bd76dccb52387d4ffe478d96168c4a3393f80c41ad1f55ef4e367` | same file |
| layer | "Layer 0", alpha 0 everywhere → blank canvas | locked "Background", alpha fully opaque |
| original alpha | lost as transparency | "Alpha 1" document channel, original zeros preserved |
| layer rgb | base decode | byte-identical to base decode (interleaved RGB sha256 `946974fc…4fff1f` in both) |
| oracle | — | Pillow decodes the same file with all-zero alpha and RGB within one byte per channel of PhotoCraft's decode (max per-channel diff R,G,B = 1,1,1), matching the issue thread's own measurement |

Fixes #5696

Related #5676 (the explicit import option remains open there; this PR does not
add a dialog).

included.head: 802a1b179093d6926b6493497831b1b49b10f035
included.title: fix(compose): interior effects see the backdrop through a Normal layer's fill
included.body:
Fixes #6232.

`premerges_layer()` left Normal layers out, on the idea that Normal gives the same result whether the interior effects paint over the merged layer or over the layer alone. That only holds for Normal effects. At Fill 0 % the layer's own buffer is transparent, so a Soft Light Color Overlay blended against nothing and came out as its plain colour, which then went over the background in Normal. Photoshop blends it against what shows through the layer. Now a Normal layer merges first, the same path #4231 added for #3996, when one of its enabled interior effects (overlays, satin, inner glow/shadow, inside stroke, inner bevel) blends in a mode other than Normal. The GPU planner picks this up too because it uses the same predicate. Thanks to @sageford for the source analysis in the issue, which pointed straight at the right place.

I kept other Normal layers off the merge path on purpose. With a half-transparent backdrop under a layer below 100 % fill, the merged layer goes over a backdrop that already contains it, so the backdrop counts twice: red at 50 % under blue at fill 50 % with only a drop shadow ends at alpha 0.876 instead of 0.75. The second test pins that down. Non-Normal layers have the same double count today (since #4231), and so now does a Normal layer with a non-Normal interior effect, but only on a half-transparent backdrop. Fixing it means finishing the merge with a lerp by the shape's alpha, and the outside-stroke share would have to change with it, on CPU and GPU. I'd rather keep that for a follow-up and am happy to open one, or to switch approach if you prefer.

Validation:
- `advanced_tests::interior_effects_blend_with_the_backdrop_through_a_see_through_normal_layer` (#04170F under a Fill 0 % Normal layer with a yellow Soft Light overlay, opaque and half-transparent parts, 8/16/32-bit): fails on main (plain yellow `[1.0, 1.0, 0.0]` instead of Photoshop's soft light `[0.125, 0.300, 0.003]`), passes here
- `advanced_tests::a_see_through_normal_layer_without_interior_effects_counts_the_backdrop_once`: passes on main and here; it fails if every Normal layer merges (`[0.429, 0, 0.571, 0.876]`)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-compose --lib` filtered on `effects`, `advanced_tests`, `stroke`, `shadow`, `fill`, `glow`; `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --test parity effect` (8 GPU/CPU parity tests)
- `cargo test --release -p photocraft-io --features corpus --test corpus oracle`: pass counts unchanged (photoshop 188, io 148, psd-tools 249)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-compose --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

included.head: 08487cdd293c311e86c33f6009170d32f15eb6e6
included.title: Preserve opaque edges when placing scaled Smart Objects
included.body:
Fixes #5746.

Bicubic downscaling during image placement and transform prefiltering previously sampled transparent support beyond the rectangular source edge. Opaque images therefore gained partially transparent border pixels, which became visible as faded edges after Smart Object filters such as Gaussian Blur. Repeat the source edge pixels for these reductions, preserving the source's existing alpha while retaining the current behavior for transparent pixels inside the source bounds.

A regression test covers initial placement, Smart Object rerender, and Gaussian Blur at 8-, 16-, and 32-bit depths.

Validation: focused engine regression passes; algo/engine library tests, clippy, formatting, and `cargo xtask layers` pass. `cargo xtask wasm` passes its 24 checks. The full engine package test suite was interrupted during compilation; it was not reported as passing.

included.head: 40b3bf9b6b9522838914264e3bae7a796e017add
included.title: GPU: pin the keep-overlap ordering with a tile-growth regression test
included.body:
Companion to #5697's area: a regression test for the tile-growth ordering that `keep_overlap` implements.

When a resident GPU texture's region shifts, `keep_overlap` carries the old texels over the overlap and the current update rewrites tiles inside it. The two must not race: `crates/gpu/tests/parity.rs` now grows a raster layer's tile footprint one tile per render (256 → 1024 px, 4 steps), rewrites the full extent with per-step noise each time, and compares every render against the CPU oracle on both the whole-texture and the paged compositor (`tile_growth_rewrite_keeps_fresh_texels_in_the_overlap`). If the keep copy could ever overwrite fresh tile writes, step 2 would already show stale texels — dropping the `ordered` flag makes it fail at 254/255 (measured, then restored).

A first version of this PR also moved the keep copy into the frame's encoder to save a queue submission per shifted region. That reordering is **withdrawn** per the review discussion: in the only scenario where the submission count differs (a layer whose region shifts every frame, a pure tile-coordinate remap), a controlled A/B on Vulkan (median of 7 repetitions × 300 frames) measured 6.684 ms/frame with the batching vs 6.484 ms/frame with the original separate submission — no speedup, consistent with the noisy P46 medians quoted earlier. The original deliberate separate submission is restored; this PR now only adds the ordering regression test, which passes with either submission shape by construction.

included.head: 59d42f39980317bd931290a55d0cf42b311eff2c
included.title: Free Transform: a rotated sprite's soft edge keeps its colour instead of a light border
included.body:
Fixes #6203.

The Free Transform warp samples in premultiplied alpha, but it clamped the accumulated alpha to 1 before un-premultiplying. Photoshop's Bicubic (Keys, a = -0.75) overshoots, so next to partly transparent pixels (the soft edge of a sprite, or a piece that was already rotated once) the alpha comes out a little above 1, and dividing by the clamped value scaled the colour up by the same amount: a light rim along the rotated edge, pure white on light textures as in the screenshots. Multiples of 90° land on the pixel grid and never overshoot, which is why they looked clean. The fix divides by the unclamped alpha and still stores the clamped one. The mesh warp (Edit > Transform > Warp) had the same line, so it gets the same change.

Validation:
- `transform::tests::rotation_keeps_the_colour_of_a_soft_edged_sprite` and `warp::tests::a_rotated_soft_edged_sprite_keeps_its_colour` (a one-colour 20 px sprite with a half-transparent rim, rotated 45°): fail on main (an opaque edge pixel comes out 209/157/105 instead of 204/153/102), pass here
- `cargo test -p photocraft-algo --lib transform::` and `warp::`, `--test warp_clipped`
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-algo --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

included.head: 3f9a76a4afa642f41e8fa4611909efcdbb755d55
included.title: Make Crystallize 4x and Pointillize 3x faster on 24 MP layers
included.body:
Crystallize was rebuilding jittered sites per pixel and accumulating cell averages it almost never used. Pointillize was rebuilding dot geometry and resampling its colour for every candidate pixel.

On a 24 MP RGB8 layer, the actual commands at small cell sizes now take about 140 ms:

| Command | Cell size | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Crystallize | 10 | 560.8 ms | 137.5 ms | 4.08x |
| Pointillize | 5 | 430.5 ms | 146.4 ms | 2.94x |
| Crystallize | 100 | 1387.5 ms | 202.1 ms | 6.87x |
| Pointillize | 100 | 543.5 ms | 131.9 ms | 4.12x |

These are `Session::execute` timings, including the history commit. Five runs, median, 6000 x 4000, 16 workers on a c7i.4xlarge. Setup, hashing and GUI repaint are outside the clock.

Background layers have a smaller gain because the existing transparency restoration pass takes a large share of the time. At cell sizes 10/5, Crystallize goes from 891.5 to 441.1 ms (2.02x), Pointillize from 738.5 to 608.2 ms (1.21x). At size 100 they improve 3.42x and 1.94x. The report includes those rows and single-worker runs too.

What changed:

- Prepare jittered sites, dot radii and source colours once per cell in each tile. Read cell centres directly rather than materializing a dense halo where it is unnecessary.
- Only accumulate Crystallize averages for cells whose centres fall outside the image. Boundary sums keep the original row order and f32 rounding.
- For larger cells, certify horizontal spans using bounds on the actual rounded f32 distance scores. A span is filled only when one candidate's worst score beats every other candidate's best. Ambiguous spans split down to scalar pixels. No approximate bisectors or epsilon tests.
- Encode U8/U16/F32 output on the tile workers. The serial commit copies native bytes instead of converting every sample.

The old scalar implementations remain as independent fallbacks and test oracles. Site-grid scratch is capped; failed optional reservations keep the old path.

All 44 measured before/after configurations have identical full-output hashes. The command bench also verifies Undo and Redo. New scalar comparisons cover colour models, alpha, fractional cells, negative origins, boundary averages, nonfinite samples, soft selections, clamped extents and storage depths. Span tests include coordinates near f32 precision boundaries.

Validation:

- 2,447 tests passed across algo and engine, 43 ignored.
- Clippy for both crates, all targets, warnings denied.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask scorecard --check`
- `cargo xtask wasm`
- `cargo xtask perf --quick`

[Method, full tables and reproduction commands](https://github.com/excited-raccoon/photocraft/blob/perf/cell-raster-filters/docs/pixelate-cell-performance.md). [Raw trials and output hashes](https://github.com/excited-raccoon/photocraft/blob/perf/cell-raster-filters/docs/pixelate-cell-timings.json).

included.head: de095be6cb18192e5fe548d989ceaf534b9b3de7
included.title: fix(compose): stop effect noise from painting empty blur tails
included.body:
Fixes #5638.

Adding Noise to a shadow or glow can paint speckles across otherwise empty parts of the layer's bounds. The running-sum blur leaves tiny positive cancellation residues after its last covered sample; the noise stage amplifies those residues into visible coverage. On main df055f3d, a synthetic sloping shape with a 5 px blur and 26% noise produces 280 visible pixels where the direct convolution is exactly empty.

Track the last covered sample and reset the sum only when its window is empty. This preserves real faint coverage without an opacity cutoff. Tests compare the noisy blur against the existing direct-convolution support at integral/fractional widths and check empty gaps plus 1e-20 coverage. No UI, dependency, or workflow changes are included.

Verification (public-fork standard runners):
- Baseline regression failed as expected: https://github.com/jonathanwxh-cell/photocraft/actions/runs/38726446081
- Candidate compositor tests: 290 unit + 3 integration passed; 3 existing tests ignored. Format, strict Clippy, and layering passed: https://github.com/jonathanwxh-cell/photocraft/actions/runs/38727310640
- Before/after coverage renders inspected; the stray tail is removed. Evidence and timing logs are artifacts on the same run.
- `cargo xtask wasm`, `cargo xtask test-corpus`, and `cargo xtask perf --quick` completed successfully: https://github.com/jonathanwxh-cell/photocraft/actions/runs/38727631358. Quick performance runs do not enforce full-size budgets; the repository baseline comparison was skipped because its Mac hardware differs from the Linux runner.
- Candidate `de095be6` and the verification refs have identical production/test source; only temporary `.github` verification files differ. Base is still `df055f3d` on the final refresh.

Cost: a same-runner release test of a 6000x4000 synthetic coverage map (blur + noise, three measurements per width) measured median 262.2 -> 274.4 ms at width 5, and 261.8 -> 276.2 ms at width 32. This is a correctness fix with roughly 5% measured overhead on that path, not a performance improvement; these are not end-to-end UI latency measurements.

Prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance; contributor credit: jonathnwxh.

included.head: 835259929469c647dd8cdd94800e8763721787ef
included.title: New Guide Layout: format in ruler unit, support arbitrary units, and normalize on lost focus (#6082)
included.body:
Fixes #6082

### Summary of Changes
In Photoshop, the **New Guide Layout** dialog (`View > Guides > New Guide Layout…`) displays its spacing, margin, and size fields formatted in the document's active ruler unit. Users can type any unit (`cm`, `in`, `px`, `pt`, `mm`, `pica`, `%`) or bare numbers without them being forced or immediately converted to pixels while typing.

This PR brings PhotoCraft's New Guide Layout into 1:1 Photoshop parity:
1. **Ruler unit formatting on open**: When the dialog opens or resets, fields (`gutter`, `rowGutter`, `width`, `height`, `margin`) format in the document's active ruler unit (`"0.71 cm"`, `"0.28 in"`, `"20 px"`).
2. **Support arbitrary units**: Singleline text edits replace the fixed `"px"` `value_field` widgets so users can type any supported unit or bare numbers without immediate conversion.
3. **Normalization on lost focus**:
   - Bare numbers append the document's active ruler unit (e.g. typing `10` -> `10 cm` when ruler is `cm`).
   - Unspaced unit entries format with a space (e.g. typing `10cm` -> `10 cm`, `2in` -> `2 in`, `20px` -> `20 px`).
4. **Tab vs Mouse Click selection**:
   - Tabbing into a field selects all text so typing immediately replaces it.
   - Clicking with the mouse places the caret at the clicked point without selecting all text.
5. **Live canvas preview**: Typed units are converted with document DPI/extent for instant preview and command execution.
6. **Reopening conversion**: Closing/confirming and reopening after changing the document's ruler unit converts the stored values to the new ruler unit.

### Testing
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib guide_layout_ui` (17/17 tests passing, including new tests for unit conversion, reopen formatting, and lost-focus normalization).
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- -D warnings` (clean, 0 warnings).
- `cargo xtask layers` (verified, no layering violations).

included.head: 248ba660576f4896f69cbb6639353e2f1d295271
included.title: Marquee: Fixed Size selects exactly the entered width and height (fixes #6015)
included.body:
Fixes #6015.

**Problem:** with the Rectangular (or Elliptical) Marquee set to Style › Fixed Size, the selection was one pixel larger on each side than the size entered: 10 × 10 selected 11 × 11, and 1 × 1 selected 2 × 2. The fixed rectangle starts at the press point, which usually sits between pixel edges (e.g. x = 50.4, so 50.4..60.4). `marquee_px` then floors the near edge and ceils the far edge, which gives 50..61. This is the same cause as #5472 for ⇧ squares.

**Fix:** `canvas::fixed_size_px` builds the Fixed Size rectangle on whole pixels: the near edge goes to the closest pixel edge and the far edge is exactly W × H away. Both the live outline and readout and the selection made on release use it, through `marquee_preview_px`. A click without a drag now places the Fixed Size selection, as in Photoshop. Before, a click deselected. Normal and Fixed Ratio are unchanged: a click still deselects.

**Tests:**
- `canvas::tests::fixed_size_px_is_exactly_the_size`: down-right and up-left, 1 × 1, fractional sizes.
- `marquee_tests::fixed_size_selects_exactly_the_entered_size`: through the real canvas, for both marquee tools and 10 × 10, 1 × 1 and 64 × 32. The press lands between pixels, then the test checks the readout, the dragged selection and a click.

**Checks run locally:** the marquee tests in `photocraft-ui-egui` (`fixed_size`, `marquee_styles`, `square_px`, `one_pixel`, `the_live_outline`), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`. No new UI strings. CI covers the rest.

included.head: 2551f3ddab90f57a64a91b0bc7a707950726bf9a
included.title: Rectangular Marquee: Style: Fixed Size selects exactly that many pixels (#6015)
included.body:
Fixes #6015

## Root cause
`marquee_corners` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`) built a fixed-size marquee from the press point plus the size, and `marquee_px` then floors the lower corner and ceils the upper one. The press lands somewhere inside a pixel, so `start + size` spans a pixel more each way: 1 × 1 selected 2 × 2, 10 × 10 selected 11 × 11, as reported. (A normal drag is unaffected: both its corners are pointer positions.)

## Fix
With Style: Fixed Size the corners land on the pixel grid: from the pressed pixel towards the drag (dragging up or left takes the pixels before it), or, with ⌥ during the drag, centred on the press, as before. `marquee_px`'s floor and ceil then add nothing, so the selection is exactly the size the options bar shows.

## Tests
`canvas::marquee_size_tests::a_fixed_size_marquee_is_exactly_that_size`: 1 × 1, 10 × 10 and 64 × 32 from a press at (10.4, 20.6), dragged right/down, on the press itself, up/left, and ⌥-centred: the selected rectangle is exactly the size each time (on `main` each case is a pixel larger both ways). The existing marquee tests (`cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui marquee`, 30 tests, incl. `alt_draws_from_the_centre_and_shift_alt_a_centred_circle` and `shift_square_pressed_between_pixels_has_equal_sides`) still pass; `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` clean, on a Linux (WSL) build host.

included.title: fix(compose): prevent outside stroke from bleeding into opaque character interior (#5861)
included.body:
Fixes #5861

### Summary of Changes
- In `crates/compose/src/effects.rs`, corrected the discontinuity in `outline_share(cov, l)` by immediately returning `0.0` when `outside <= 1e-6`, preventing opaque pixel interiors (`cov=1.0, l=1.0`) from evaluating `rest <= 1e-6` and receiving 100% outside stroke share.

included.head: e81fa94f3f159a96cfa806acde9c2d45b702ba05
included.title: BMP export: Indexed Color documents save as palette BMPs
included.body:
Follow-up to #3869, which made palette BMPs open in Indexed Color mode. The other direction was still missing: saving an Indexed Color document as BMP went through the ordinary RGB path and wrote a 24-bit file, so the colour table was gone on reopen. The PNG exporter already had a palette branch for this.

- `export_mode_specific` now sends Indexed Color to BMP as well as PNG, through a new `encode_bmp_indexed` that writes an 8-bit palette BMP with the document's colour table. BMP has no transparency, so a transparent index is written as its palette colour and the export warns about it. A document without a usable table (none, or more than 256 colours) keeps the old RGB path.
- `bmp_palette` returned the decoder's 256-entry padding, so a 3-colour BMP reopened with 253 extra black entries. It now trims the table to the colours the header declares. (The test added in #3869 only checks the first two entries, so it still passes.)

Checked on `upstream/main` at `cb319fd7`:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -j 12 -p photocraft-codecs -p photocraft-io --lib --tests -- --test-threads=8`
- `cargo clippy -j 12 -p photocraft-codecs -p photocraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo xtask layers`

New tests cover the codec round trip (table and pixels, row padding, bad input, header parsing) and the export/import round trip through `photocraft_io`. I did not run `cargo xtask wasm` or the corpus; the change is pure Rust on the existing `image` encoder, and CI runs both.

included.body:
**TL;DR:** the dock column can collapse to a strip of panel icons and expand again, like Photoshop's double arrow.

Fixes #4059.

Photoshop's dock column has a double arrow on top that collapses the panels to a strip of icons and expands them again. PhotoCraft had no equivalent, so the dock always took its full width.

## Change
- A bar on top of the dock column holds the double arrow (Collapse to Icons / Expand Panels). Double-clicking the bar, its context menu and every panel menu toggle it too.
- Collapsed, each visible panel shows as an icon (the tooltip is the panel name), with a line between groups. Clicking an icon opens its group as a flyout beside the strip on that panel. Clicking it again closes it, and so does a click outside when Preferences › Workspace › Auto-Collapse Iconic Panels is on.
- Window › <panel> and the icon rail open the panel in its flyout. Choosing it again while it shows hides it, as in the expanded dock. Right-to-left layouts mirror the strip and the flyout.
- The state is `DockLayout::iconic` (`ui.set {"dock": {"iconic": true}}`), saved with workspaces and the remembered layout. Older layouts load unchanged. The open flyout is not saved.
- The new strings are translated in every catalog.

## Tests
- New `crates/ui-egui/src/dock_icons_tests.rs` with 7 harness tests: the toggle in every theme, flyout open/close, the panel menu entries, serde round trip + `ui.set`, no panic with tiny windows or hidden panels, every panel has an existing icon, and Window menu and rail open the flyout.

- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

included.head: 76d7d27c5203e197ed03947a33eeea048ea935b5
included.title: Preferences: old settings files take Shift-to-switch-tools on (#5647)
included.body:
Fixes #5647.

### What was wrong
Pressing a tool's letter again cycled through its group (V: Move → Artboard, B: Brush → Pencil → …). In Photoshop the plain letter keeps the tool, and **Shift+letter** cycles ("Use Shift Key for Tool Switch", on by default).

PhotoCraft already behaves that way when the preference is on (`shortcuts.rs`), and #3528 (2026-10-12, first released in 0.8.2) made it on by default. But the preferences file stores **every** key, chosen or not. Every install that ran an earlier build has `"useShiftKeyForToolSwitch": false` saved, the old default, so the new default never reached existing users. The existing test only covers a file *without* the key.

### Change
`Session::load_prefs_json`: a settings file older than version 2 that stores `useShiftKeyForToolSwitch: false` drops that key, so it takes the new default (on). `prefs_value` now writes `"version": 2` (`PREFS_VERSION`), so a user who turns the preference off from now on keeps it off. This follows the existing appearance-mode migration in the same function.

One trade-off: someone who deliberately turned the preference off on 0.8.2–0.9.0 (when the file still said version 1) gets it back on once, and can turn it off again.

### Test
`prefs::tests::old_settings_files_take_the_shift_key_tool_switch_default`: files without a version and with version 1 storing `false` load with the switch on, and other Tools settings are kept. A preference turned off and saved now writes version 2 and stays off when reloaded. Not built or run locally; CI runs it.

included.head: c8ed14dc52d68f7ee1c3aa385afaa27717587d65
included.title: Save: a flat file that keeps the document is saved in place (#5733)
included.body:
Fixes #5733.

### What was wrong
"When you open a file, change it and save it (via Save), it opens a Save As dialog instead." File › Save on a document opened from a flat file (PNG, JPEG, TIFF…) always went through Save As (`menus.rs`, `file.save`: `_ => app.save_dialog_flow(..)`), even when the file still held everything. Photoshop's Save writes such a file back in place, and only asks once the document has something the format can't keep (layers, transparency in a JPEG, 16-bit in a JPEG…).

### Change
`saves_flat_in_place(doc, path)` (`lib.rs`): Save writes the document's own flat file back when that file keeps the whole document:
- one plain raster layer (`plain_raster`: visible, 100% opacity, Normal, no masks, effects or blending restrictions);
- no extra channels, RGB or Grayscale;
- a format that writes the document's bit depth (`FormatCaps::depths`);
- transparency only where the format has alpha, or the layer is the Background.

Anything else keeps today's behaviour (Save As, so the original is never overwritten with less, #3806). The replay rule for recorded Saves (#3531) is unchanged.

### Test
`file_open::tests::a_flat_file_that_keeps_the_document_saves_in_place`: a PNG with one plain layer saves in place. Add a second layer and Save asks. A JPEG whose one layer isn't the Background (JPEG has no alpha) asks too. The existing `pcraft_documents_save_in_place_but_flat_files_ask` still holds: its PNG has no plain layer. Not built or run locally; CI runs it.

included.title: Displace: OK asks for the displacement map, as in Photoshop (#5806)
included.body:
Fixes #5806.

### What was wrong
In Photoshop, **Filter › Distort › Displace** asks for the displacement map file (a PSD) after you click OK. PhotoCraft's dialog is generated from the command spec. It offered the map only as *Map Document* (a dropdown of open documents) or *Map Path* (a plain text field to type a path into). OK with neither set ran without a map, and no file picker ever appeared. That's exactly what the reporter describes.

### Change
- `filter_dialog::needs_displace_map`: Displace confirmed with no map document and no (non-blank) path.
- `filter_dialog::ask_displace_map`: opens the open-file picker in the last-used folder. On a choice it runs Displace with the dialog's values plus `mapPath`, through the same `smart_ui::confirm_command` path as OK (so editing a Displace smart filter works too), then remembers the values and resumes a playing action. Cancel applies nothing.
- `dialogs::confirm` calls it before running the command.
- In the browser the picker hands over contents, not a path the filter can read. There it reports that the map must be opened as a document and picked as *Map Document*.

### Test
`filter_dialog::tests::displace_asks_for_its_map_after_ok`: OK with no map asks once and Displace runs with the chosen PNG (one history step). A cancelled picker applies nothing. A map path or map document already set skips the picker. Not built or run locally; CI runs it.
